text: SignInDialog is a properly-labelled modal: the panel is role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby pointing at the generated id of its <h2> title (via React.useId), it focuses the email field on open and closes on Escape, and surfaces auth errors in a role="alert" live region. The labelledby-to-title wiring (not a hard-coded string) keeps the accessible name in lockstep with the visible heading.

CommandPalette is a labelled modal dialog implementing the ARIA APG combobox/listbox pattern: the surface is role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="command palette"; results render as role="listbox" with role="option" rows carrying aria-selected on the active item. Keyboard handling (ArrowUp/ArrowDown to move the active option, Enter to run, Escape to close) plus open-time focus of the search input make it fully keyboard-operable. This is the ⌘K command surface, so its dialog+listbox a11y contract is the reference for overlay launchers.

DataGrid is a WAI-ARIA APG composite grid: its root carries role="grid" with aria-label (the caller-supplied `label`), aria-rowcount and aria-colcount; the header band is role="row"/aria-rowindex=1 with role="columnheader" cells that expose aria-sort (ascending|descending|none) on sortable columns; body rows are role="row" with role="gridcell" cells, and group headers add aria-expanded. A single roving tabindex (one cell tabIndex=0, the rest -1) plus arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown key handling makes it keyboard-operable as one composite widget. This is the shared virtualized grid powering the blotter/risk/book workspaces, so the grid-pattern a11y contract is centralized here.

StatusBadge renders its stream-health glyph as role="img" with an aria-label (and matching title) derived from the StreamHealth state, so the purely-visual glyph is announced as a single labelled image to assistive tech rather than read as a bare emoji character. It is the StatusBadge story exercised by gui/storybook-static (components-statusbadge--* entries: Default/Healthy/Resyncing/Stale/All States), making it the canonical visual + a11y reference for stream-health status surfaces.

Rate sensitivities are layered, not duplicated: celnet-rates::risk is the LEAF-level curve-risk producer (analytic PV01, re-bootstrap parallel DV01, and the key-rate ladder = instrument Jacobian over calibrating OIS quotes), while celnet-risk-cube is the CONSUMER/aggregator that decomposes pre-computed weighted sensitivities into FRTB GIRR buckets (RiskBucket.ws + MAR21 bucket algebra). Per ADR-0008 §Sensitivities the factor decomposition into FRTB buckets happens at the risk layer; leaf engines emit raw sensitivities. The crates are disjoint (no celnet-risk-cube→celnet-rates edge; risk-cube's canonical leaves come from celnet-risk-normalize option Greeks, never from curve bumping), and ois_risk currently has only test callers (a foundation not yet wired). No real_overlap. The integration target is to feed OisRisk.key_rate buckets into a risk-cube GIRR RiskBucket; the review blocker to guard against is any curve-bumping/PV01 reimplementation INSIDE celnet-risk-cube.

DUPLICATION REVIEW (conventions / day-count): celnet-rates/src/schedule.rs does NOT reimplement or bypass day-count logic. Both its ACT/360 fixed-leg accrual (line 52) and ACT/365F discount-time coordinate (line 53) call the ONE canonical primitive celnet_calendar::daycount::year_fraction -- the same primitive celnet-conventions itself delegates to (lib.rs imports + vol_year_fraction). celnet-conventions owns day-count SELECTION (accrual_basis(ccy) ccy->DayCount, plus record day_count_accrual fields), NOT day-count arithmetic; celnet-calendar::year_fraction is the canonical realization of the DayCount enum (the single place the enum becomes a numeric accrual factor). Therefore celnet-rates correctly depending on celnet-calendar and NOT on celnet-conventions is right, not a gap: a USD-SOFR OIS fixed leg is a single-currency money-market instrument whose ACT/360 basis is fixed by the SOFR product spec, so the FX-options per-(pair,tenor) registry is not its source of truth. Hardcoded Act360 in schedule.rs agrees with accrual_basis(USD) by construction (USD is not GBP/AUD/NZD). VERDICT: already_integrated; no action.

ADR-0007 — ONE UNVERSIONED WIRE CONTRACT (evolve in place, zero legacy). Celnet has no external users and one uniformly-upgraded deployment, so the wire contract (celnet-proto) carries NO schema_version, no template/version field, no schemaId negotiation, and no N/N-1 back-compat shims. Growth is additive + default-compatible (new oneof arms/fields default to the prior behavior — e.g. ADR-0008 Underlying/CarryModel default to FX), so existing call sites are unchanged with no version handshake. Where a byte stream needs a discriminator it is a fixed CONTENT tag (ADR-0009 CELNHND1), never a schema version. API-first parity is binding: SDK, WS mirror, CLI, Excel all consume this one contract and change in lockstep. Doc: docs/adr/ADR-0007-one-unversioned-contract.md; CLAUDE.md guardrail #9.

DUPLICATION REVIEW (already_integrated, low): The newly-merged GUI ExcelWorkspace and the fixed-income celnet-rates schedule/curve/bootstrap do NOT reimplement or bypass existing capabilities. ExcelWorkspace.ExcelWorkspace is a pure presentational landing page (no WS/pricing; in_degree=out_degree=0); the real CELNET.* functions + transport live in excel/src/functions + excel/src/transport. celnet-rates::usd_sofr_ois_schedule/period_end_dates reuse celnet-calendar primitives (RollRule.adjust/add_months/year_fraction) and are domain-distinct from the FX celnet-calendar::fx::schedule. celnet-rates::Curve is the SOLE discount/forward curve type and realizes the ADR-0008-anticipated celnet-curve seam behind forward()/discount(); celnet-surface::TermStructure is an orthogonal vol term-structure, not a curve. Only residue: the ws://127.0.0.1:8081 default is triplicated as a string literal across excel runtime, gui transportConfig, and the ExcelWorkspace doc copy — a low-severity doc-drift hazard, not architectural overlap; fix by importing the shared GUI default into the doc page.

ADR-0008 — MULTI-ASSET ARCHITECTURE: identity / carry-producing market / agnostic payoff. The one fused FX seam is separated into three orthogonal layers: (1) Identity = Underlying, a discriminated union (Fx(CcyPair) now; Metal/DigitalAsset/Equity/Listed additive) — the ONLY place asset class is named; (2) Market = Carry as a forward/discount PRODUCER (forward(t)/discount(t)) — FX two-rate, equity (r,q), commodity (r,convenience), crypto (r,funding) all collapse to generalized-BSM F=S·e^{b·t}, df=e^{−r·t}, differing only in how b is assembled; Carry::FxRates reproduces FX forward/discount BIT-FOR-BIT (byte-identity invariant); (3) Payoff = asset-class-AGNOSTIC engines consuming forward(t)/discount(t)+vol surface only. NO-WORKAROUND TEST (binding): a payoff engine that does `match carry { FxRates=>…, CostOfCarry=>… }` is a review blocker, not a shortcut. Greeks stays a fixed zero-alloc POD shape (guardrail #11); factor decomposition lives in the risk layer (celnet-risk-cube), not an allocating map on Greeks. Doc: docs/adr/ADR-0008-multi-asset-carry-architecture.md.

NUMERICS NON-DUPLICATION (root-finders/optimizers): the tree has THREE distinct numerical kernels that are NOT reimplementations of one capability. (1) celnet-rates::solver::brent_root is a generic bracketed 1-D Brent (IQI + bisection safeguard, FnMut(f64)->f64 -> Result), isolated to celnet-rates with its only production caller bootstrap_ois; celnet-rates::solver::root is a #[cfg(test)] wrapper, not a seam. (2) celnet-vanilla::solver::strike_from_delta is a DOMAIN-SPECIFIC guarded Brent-lite (bisection bracket + analytic-slope Newton via delta_d_strike) that is deliberately branch-aware because premium-adjusted call delta is non-monotone in strike (ANALYTICS-SPEC §3.5) — it is NOT substitutable by the generic brent_root and must not be replaced by one. (3) celnet-surface::fitmath::gauss_newton_2/3/4 are damped Levenberg-Marquardt n-D least-squares smile calibrators, a different problem class; celnet-surface contains no 1-D root-finder. celnet-vanilla and celnet-rates are disjoint dependency subtrees and there is no shared celnet-numerics root-finder; ADR-0008 does not require one. VERDICT: acceptable_for_now / low severity — leave as is; do not create a shared numerics home (it would add a cross-subtree dependency edge and could not unify the branch-guarded delta inversion anyway). Revisit only if a second generic bracketed 1-D Brent appears outside celnet-rates.

ADR-0007 — ONE UNVERSIONED WIRE CONTRACT (evolve in place, zero legacy). Celnet has no external users and one uniformly-upgraded deployment, so the wire contract (celnet-proto) carries NO schema_version, no template/version field, no schemaId negotiation, and no N/N-1 back-compat shims. Growth is additive + default-compatible (new oneof arms/fields default to the prior behavior — e.g. ADR-0008 Underlying/CarryModel default to FX), so existing call sites are unchanged with no version handshake. Where a byte stream needs a discriminator it is a fixed CONTENT tag (ADR-0009 CELNHND1), never a schema version. API-first parity is binding: SDK, WS mirror, CLI, Excel all consume this one contract and change in lockstep. Doc: docs/adr/ADR-0007-one-unversioned-contract.md; CLAUDE.md guardrail #9.

DISCOUNTING-SEAM (ADR-0008): celnet-rates::Curve does NOT duplicate or bypass the asset-class-agnostic carry seam. The live forward/discount producer for ALL option pricing is celnet-types::Carry (FxRates|CostOfCarry) via its forward_factor/discount_df scalar accessors, consumed through celnet-core::carry::CarryInputs::forward()/discount_df(); Carry holds flat f64 rates (ADR-0008's 'degenerate single-point curve'). celnet-rates::Curve is the isolated P1 fixed-income term-structure toolkit (log-DF curve + bootstrap/OIS/risk/solver/schedule): celnet-rates depends only on celnet-types/celnet-calendar/time (NOT celnet-core), NO workspace crate depends on celnet-rates, and Curve.discount_factor has ZERO callers outside celnet-rates (only OIS/bootstrap/risk/schedule + its own tests). There is no bridge from Curve into Carry and no payoff engine reads a Curve, so the ADR-0008 no-workaround test PASSES (no match-on-carry, no carry-bypassing discount path). VERDICT acceptable_for_now: potential-but-not-actual overlap; Curve is simply not yet integrated. BINDING FORWARD CONSTRAINT: any future wiring of term-structure discounting into pricing must slot Curve BEHIND the carry seam (a curve-backed Carry/CarryInputs producer implementing forward_factor/discount_df), never via a direct Curve.discount_factor call in a payoff engine, with a flat-curve byte-identity test against the scalar Carry::FxRates path.

ADR-0009 — EDGE WIRE CODEC (hot-upgrade hand-off). The handoff module serializes the engine's live BookState (every booked option line) + MarketState essentials (spot, both rates, vol-time, ConventionRecord, calibrated smile reconstructed from its three benchmark pillars) to a flat deterministic little-endian byte buffer (fixed-width ints, IEEE-754 f64 bit patterns) under a single fixed magic tag CELNHND1 — a CONTENT tag, not a schema_version (honours ADR-0007 / guardrail #9). A freshly started process restores byte-identical book+market state and reprices bit-identically. This is the built hand-rolled codec, explicitly NOT rkyv. Doc: docs/adr/ADR-0009-edge-wire-codec.md.

Token-driven styling (DRY single source of truth). Button and DataGrid render exclusively through CSS-Module classes whose declarations reference the Celnet Aurora design tokens by their emitted CSS custom properties (var(--token)) — e.g. Button.module.css carries 32 var(--…) references and zero raw color literals, DataGrid.module.css likewise. Every such custom property (--bg-base, --accent, --space-3, --r-md, --row-h, …) is the cssVar formalized in gui/design-tokens.json (W3C DTCG format), itself a verbatim formalization of gui/src/design/tokens.css. A repo-wide scan of all 46 gui/src CSS Modules found zero raw hex/hsl color literals and exactly one rgba() (a text-shadow in CubeWorkspace.module.css). The only inline literals in component TSX are token-read fallbacks (root.getPropertyValue('--…') || '#…' in Sparkline.tsx / SmileChart.tsx), which read the token first. Editing a token value in tokens.css therefore propagates to these components with no per-component restyle — the invariant the styling-DRIFT derive-rule guards.

ReplayError::fmt surfaces exactly two outcomes with distinct prefixes: a host-layer failure during replay is rendered as 'replay host error: {e}', while a non-determinism failure (guest output differed from the snapshot) is rendered as 'replay diverged at {what} (not bit-identical)'. The 'not bit-identical' suffix is the contract that callers and observability tooling use to distinguish sandbox errors from determinism violations.

nonadditive_measures() re-derives VaR/ES and curvature-spot over a numeraire-scaled position set (both vanilla legs and exotic legs scaled the same way), using Cube's bump-and-revalue reducers as the oracle path. It is a pure re-derivation with no state mutation: positions are scaled into a transient `scaled_node` and the store is never written. Returns `NodeNonAdditive::default()` (all None) when neither VaR nor curvature is requested.

gate_e_compaction_shrinks_log_and_recovery_is_exact: log compaction at a committed interior boundary (committed/2) physically shrinks every node's durable log to retain only the tail above the boundary, without altering applied state. After compaction: retained_log_len == committed - boundary, base_log_index == boundary + 1, snapshot_index == Some(boundary), applied_bits unchanged. The cluster continues committing after compaction. A crash-recovered follower (restarted from durable snapshot + retained tail alone, no peers) reconstructs the exact same applied state bit-for-bit and converges to the final commit index.

Each vanilla call in a multi-subscription RFS session has its snapshot mid bracketed by a direct Garman-Kohlhagen price computed from the streamed `(spot, vol)` — confirming the maker's pricer emits real market-consistent numbers and not stubs. The check is: `is_close(mid, gk_direct, 1e-6, 1e-6) || price.bid == 0.0` (the bid == 0.0 escape handles an indicative-only line). Source: `market_maker_streams_many_instruments_over_one_session`.

scope_filter is a stateless helper that converts an optional wire RiskScope to an optional (DimensionId, u64) filter pair: a None scope (absent filter) produces Ok(None) meaning no filter (all positions); a present scope delegates to convert::dimension_of for validation and returns Ok(Some((dim, value))) on success. An unknown dimension tag propagates invalid_argument.

complete_execute_routes_by_correlation proves that complete_execute performs an exact correlation-id lookup: a call with an unknown id is a no-op (does not disturb other waiters), and a call with the correct id delivers the ExecuteOutcome to the registered oneshot sender and removes that entry from the waiter table.

request_vote_steps_down_on_higher_term_then_grants: when RequestVote arrives from a candidate at a strictly higher term, the handler first adopts the higher term (durably clears the previous vote), demotes any Candidate to Follower, and then evaluates and grants the vote to the new candidate. The adopt guard is `term > my_term` (strict). This kills `< with ==`/`<=` on the stale path and `> with ==`/`<`/`>=` on the adopt path.

read_one is the core decode kernel: it discriminates torn-tail from interior corruption by the completeness of the frame body. A missing/short sync word → TornTail (no record started here). An intact 8-byte sync word followed by a complete header + payload + CRC trailer whose CRC fails → CorruptInterior (bit-rot of a fully-written record, not a torn tail). A valid CRC with a non-monotonic sequence number → CorruptInterior. An oversized length field (> MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN but ≠ SNAPSHOT_MARKER) → TornTail (corruption of the final length field, not a fully-written record). The SNAPSHOT_MARKER sentinel in the length field routes to read_snapshot, which enforces that a snapshot record is legal only at log position 0 (at_start=true) and applies the same CRC / torn-tail discrimination logic.

AggregateReq.query constructs an AggregateQuery by composing optional modifiers in a deterministic order: (1) dimension + numeraire baseline; (2) scope filter if present; (3) entitlement policy if grants/denies are non-empty; (4) VaR parameters if var_shocks is non-empty; (5) curvature weight if non-zero. Each modifier is independently optional and skipped when absent.

`Cube::firm_aggregate` matches a naive double-loop accumulation exactly (to 1e-9) for all eleven `NetGreeks` fields (delta_base, gamma, vega, theta, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color, premium_quote) and the per-pillar vega ladder total. The oracle also verifies position/exotic/leaf routing: a mixed book of 4 vanilla positions and 1 exotic leg produces `firm.positions.len()==4`, `firm.exotic_legs.len()==1`, `firm.leaves.len()==5`. Every tested field is asserted non-zero to guard against vacuous passes.

`Client::get_smile` fetches a single volatility smile slice: it sends a `GetSmileRequest` carrying a `CcyPair`, `tenor_years: f64`, and `Conventions` to `SurfaceService/GetSmile`, then decodes the response into a typed `Smile`. The `Smile` value carries a vector of `SmilePoint` (delta, vol) pairs at a single tenor; `vol_at_delta` and `atm_vol` are the primary read accessors.

exotic_struck_families_require_a_strike enforces that all ten struck exotic families (vanilla, digital, barrier, window-barrier, asian, quanto, tarf, pivot, fixed-strike lookback, american) produce DispatchError::MissingStrike{family} when --strike is absent. The error carries the exact family name as a string, enabling actionable user messages. No network round-trip occurs before this validation.

price_linear::run validates three structural pricing identities through the SDK's unary `client.price` call: (1) a fair-struck FX forward (K = S·e^{(r_dom−r_for)·t}) must have PV within 1.0 of zero and must carry no MC standard error (`price_std_error` must be `None`), encoding that closed-form linear instruments are exact; (2) a long forward struck below fair (K=1.08 < 1.10·e^{0.01}) must have strictly positive PV; (3) a 6M USDBRL NDF priced via the server must be bit-accurate to within 1e-9 relative tolerance against the hand-derived discounted-cashflow formula PV = notional·e^{−r_dom·t}·(S·e^{(r_dom−r_for)·t} − K), asserting that NDF pricing is numerically identical to an equal-terms deliverable forward (non-deliverability changes only settlement mechanics, not risk-neutral PV). Both FX swap and NDF must carry no MC standard error.

Determinism rule (docs/INTERFACES.md §"Determinism rules baked into the interfaces": transcendentals via rust-lang/libm for bit-identical cross-platform results; f64 is the CPU-canonical scalar). `celnet_core::math::sqrt` is the canonical square-root wrapper: it is `pub fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 { libm::sqrt(x) }` — a pure (side-effect-free, no WRITES) total delegation to rust-lang/libm. Routing every sqrt(·) (e.g. sigma*sqrt(T) total variance/vol-time scaling) through this one libm-backed wrapper makes the f64 result byte-identical across platforms rather than depending on the host math library.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-calendar is the FX date-arithmetic engine for the pricing stack. Its public contract is: `schedule(pair, horizon, tenor) -> Result<FxSchedule, TenorError>` is the single top-level entry point; it returns (horizon, spot, expiry, delivery, vol_anchor) for any Tenor variant (Overnight, TomNext, SpotNext, Weeks, Months, Years, Imm(n), BrokenDate). The vol_anchor is `horizon` for ON/TN (so they never produce zero or negative vol-time) and `spot` for all other tenors. All internal date arithmetic flows through `BusinessCalendar` (multi-centre intersection semantics), `RollRule::ModifiedFollowing`, and the centre-specific `SettlementCentre::is_holiday` dispatch. New currency pairs plug in by extending `centre_for`/`is_t_plus_one_pair`; no change to `schedule` or any downstream pricer is required.

NodeCore::compact_to durably snapshots the BookState as-of a requested boundary (clamped to last_applied so only committed+applied entries are captured). It reconstructs the state machine at the boundary by starting from the prior snapshot's state (if its last_included_index matches the current log base) and replaying the retained committed prefix up to that boundary — not from the live applied state, which may include entries above the boundary. Then it atomically: (1) writes the Snapshot to disk; (2) discards the log prefix up to and including the boundary via Log::discard_prefix. Returns None without side effects if there is nothing applied yet or if the boundary is already snapshotted.

cross_asset_vectors_redrive_from_independent_oracle verifies the cross-asset golden corpus: it asserts every CROSS_ASSET_FAMILIES member has at least one vector, that no vector's family collides with a proto product-arm FAMILIES entry, that all vector ids are unique, and that each price is reproduced by a family-specific oracle (equity_bsm_price for equity_option; black76_price on forward for commodity_option with FUTURE/SPOT representation; crypto_linear_price or crypto_inverse_price for crypto_option). Markets must satisfy spot > 0 and vol > 0 and every expected price must be finite.

establish_stable_leader: a deadline-bounded polling helper that returns the index of the unique stable leader — it first awaits any leader, then confirms that exactly one leader holds that same term continuously for a 250 ms stability window before returning. If leadership changes or the term advances during the window, the search restarts. Guarantees the caller receives an index that was both unique and term-stable during the confirmation window.

`drive_session` is the long-lived async loop that multiplexes a streaming-price session. It selects over two branches: control frames from the caller (forwarded to the live gRPC stream) and inbound server frames (demultiplexed via `handle_frame`). When `handle_frame` signals `SessionFlow::Reconnect`, `reconnect_session` is called: it immediately fails all in-flight click waiters with `ClientError::Reconnected`, re-opens the gRPC stream, resets each subscription's `last_seq` to 0, re-sends all `Subscribe` frames, and emits a `StreamEvent::Reconnected` on each subscription channel.

The telemetry channel (`telemetry_channel(cap)`) is a bounded-ring lossy path: when the ring is full a `publish()` call returns `false` (drop), advances the producer's internal sequence counter, and increments `probe.dropped()`. The drain sees the resulting holes as `observed_gaps()` and `drain.producer_dropped()` exactly equals the count of rejected pushes. The total number of items drained equals `accepted` (not total published). Key assertion: `probe.dropped() == rejected`, `drained_total == accepted`, `drain.producer_dropped() == rejected`, and `drain.observed_gaps() > 0` when interleaved drops occurred.

gen_strategy constructs 5 multi-leg strategy golden vectors (straddle, strangle, risk-reversal, 2y-straddle, seagull) by summing independent GK prices: expected price = Σ sign(leg.buy) · leg.ratio · gk_price(leg.cp, spot, leg.strike, vol, t, r_dom, r_for). The oracle label is 'independent Σ side·ratio·GK(leg) of the vanilla closed form'. Tolerance is rel=1e-7/abs=1e-9, matching the vanilla gate.

DispatchError.fmt provides human-readable error messages for all CLI dispatch failure modes: BadPair emits the unknown pair; BadTenor delegates to the TenorParseError display; MissingStrike names the exotic family and states it requires an absolute strike; Invalid surfaces the validation message verbatim; Price/Surface/Risk/Linear delegate to their respective inner error types.

handle_unary is the single WebSocket unary-request dispatcher: it matches the JSON "type" field against every supported operation (price, request_quote, request_multi_dealer_quote, accept_quote, reject_quote, get_smile, mark_surface, scenario, list_positions, aggregate_risk, drill_risk, limit_status, all FIX-admin CRUD verbs, and all auth/desk CRUD verbs), decodes the payload with the codec layer, forwards to the appropriate tonic service, and returns a typed JSON response frame. Unrecognised types return an error frame with the literal text "unknown request type `{other}`" — there is no fallthrough to any service.

`mint_two_way` is the click-trade token issuance entry point: given a `TwoWayLine` (line_id, sequence, bid, offer), it first calls `ledger.clear_live()` to retire the prior sequence's tokens, then mints up to two `MintedToken` values — a Sell-side token bound to the bid (only if `bid > 0.0`) and a Buy-side token bound to the offer — both with `valid_until = now_nanos + validity_nanos`. Each token is registered in the `TokenLedger` before being returned. This guarantees a click always books the current quoted premium and never a stale one.

build_smile_and_outer orchestrates surface calibration for a MarketContext + MarketQuotes pair. It always calibrates the inner (25Δ) pillar via calibrate_pillar, optionally calibrates the outer (10Δ) pillar, then assembles a three-point Vanna-Volga MarketHedgeSmile anchored at [put_strike, atm_strike, call_strike]. If MarketHedgeSmile::try_new returns None (degenerate geometry), it surfaces CalibrationError::DegenerateQuote — the function never panics on quote-derived inputs.

`vannavolga_and_ssvi_agree_in_wings` asserts cross-family agreement: the vanna-volga (VV) smile built from a five-point EURUSD market and the best-fitting arbitrage-free SSVI parametric surface must agree to within 60 bp of implied vol at every 10Δ and 25Δ wing. The tolerance is deliberately set to 'desk-meaningful' (inside OTM bid-ask) rather than exact, because VV is a local 3-point construction and SSVI is a global 3-parameter form.

`gpu_path_cpu_kat_and_node_by_node` performs two checks: (1) a Sobol' KAT — the first 16 integer draws produced by `SobolSequence::point_u32` must match the GPU kernel's Gray-code XOR construction bit-for-bit, proving CPU and GPU consume the same quasi-random draws; (2) per-path payoff agreement — each GPU payoff must lie within `derived_path_bound_for_zmax(zmax[idx])` of the CPU payoff, where the bound is derived from the f32 inverse-normal precision at that path's maximum |z|.

seqlock_reads_are_always_consistent verifies the seqlock implementation's torn-read prevention guarantee under four concurrent reader threads and one writer: every non-zero PriceSnapshot read from Seqlock must satisfy delta_spot == request_id (as f64) AND vega == request_id * 2.0. Any violation indicates a torn read. The test uses a time-bounded spin (SPIN_CAP) checked every 4096 iterations to prevent unbounded wall-clock consumption on slow hosts.

CarryInputs::discount_df() is a pure accessor delegating to self.carry.discount_df(self.t) — no side effects, no mutation. For an FX Carry::FxRates carry this is byte-identical to VanillaInputs::df_dom (the FX two-rate discount), since the underlying Carry::discount_df reads r_dom verbatim. This is the generalized carry-tagged discount used by the cross-asset pricing seam (celnet-core CarryInputs / CarryPricer), proved byte-identical for FX by fx_carry_inputs_byte_identical (ADR-0008).

flipped_byte_in_final_record_with_intact_sync_is_interior verifies that a byte flip in the FINAL record's payload — positioned such that the sync word and the full CRC trailer are still present — is classified as CorruptInterior (not healed as a torn tail). The flip target is `bytes.len() - CRC_LEN - 2` (inside the payload, before the CRC). The sync-word format closes the ambiguity that the pre-sync format could not resolve.

Log.discard_prefix removes a committed prefix up to last_included_index from the durable log (for post-snapshot compaction). It is idempotent when last_included_index < base_index (already discarded). It validates the boundary term against the held entry in debug builds. It rewrites the log to a temp file and renames atomically, then shifts base_index = last_included_index + 1, drains the discarded terms from the cache, and records snapshot_index / snapshot_term for last_index / last_term fallback.

MarketHedgeSmile::new is the infallible constructor for the three-pillar vanna-volga benchmark smile. It delegates to try_new, which enforces: all strikes finite and strictly increasing with K1 > 0; all three vols finite and strictly positive; forward and t both finite and strictly positive. If any condition fails, new panics with a diagnostic message quoting the offending inputs. This means every successfully constructed MarketHedgeSmile instance is guaranteed to hold a well-posed pillar triplet (K1 < K2 < K3 > 0, σ1,σ2,σ3 > 0, F > 0, t > 0) — the precondition assumed by all downstream vanna-volga interpolation.

netting_set_marks_match_vanilla_closed_form asserts three structural contracts of the XVA netting-set layer: (1) NettedTrade::mark(t_obs, spot, r_d, r_f) equals notional × vanilla_ref(…, expiry − t_obs, …) for t_obs < expiry and is exactly 0.0 (bit-identical) for t_obs ≥ expiry, enforcing the maturity settlement boundary; (2) NettingSet::net_value(t, s) equals the plain algebraic sum of each constituent trade's mark, upholding additive netting; (3) NettingSet horizon equals the maximum individual trade expiry (here 2.0). The test uses tolerance 1e-12 rel / 1e-15 abs against vanilla_ref and bit-exact equality for the matured case, so a pricer bug that returns intrinsic value at τ = 0 is definitively caught.

check_greeks is an internal test oracle that verifies the full analytic Greek strip of the commodity equity-style pricer against numerical finite differences. It asserts: delta_spot and delta_forward agree with central differences on spot (h = 1e-4·S) to 1e-4 relative / 1e-7 absolute; delta_forward is derived as spot-FD divided by the carry factor e^{bt}; theta agrees with −∂V/∂t; discount_rho and carry_rho agree with FD bumps of r and b respectively; and second-order greeks (gamma, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color) are verified by differencing the first-order greeks. It also asserts that the rates sensitivity is tagged Carry (not Fx), failing loudly otherwise.

price_cross_asset routes equity, commodity, and digital-asset underlyings to their respective pricing leaves. Equity uses generalized-BSM with q=r−b; commodity uses Black-76/cost-of-carry; digital-asset selects linear or inverse-coin leaf by settlement_style. A delta-keyed strike on any cross-asset underlying is refused (delta is an FX-option construct). FX/Metal reaching this function is an internal contract break.

`plain_cliquet_equals_sum_of_legs` proves the cliquet decomposition identity: `cliquet_price_plain` must equal the sum of `forward_start_price` values over all consecutive schedule intervals, to within max(1e-10·|sum|, 1e-12), for 2, 4, and 8 equal periods over both calls and puts. This is the core correctness invariant of the cliquet pricer: a plain (uncapped, unflored) cliquet is a portfolio of forward-starting options.

bridge_correction_lifts_above_node_only verifies that the Brownian-bridge-corrected lookback MC price strictly exceeds the node-only MC price for the same floating-strike call. Both estimators use the same antithetic path set (60,000 pairs, 20 steps, seed 0xB81D) and the same CounterRng/Welford infrastructure. The invariant holds because the bridge correction accounts for the running extremum's continuous behaviour between discrete monitoring dates, which node-only sampling systematically underestimates.

futures_style_greeks_vs_finite_difference verifies the futures-style Greek strip against numerical finite differences across four diverse market scenarios (on-future, on-spot, and generic cost-of-carry inputs). It asserts price is bit-for-bit equal to the standalone futures_style_price; delta_spot, vega, delta_forward, theta, and carry_rho each agree with their central-difference approximation; discount_rho is identically 0.0 AND the FD bump of r also returns 0.0 (the price function has no r-dependence in futures-style, so bumping r produces bitwise-equal prices); and second-order greeks (gamma, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color) agree with FDs of the first-order outputs.

ADR / ROADMAP §6.5 plugin trust tiers (untrusted wasm guest = default, sandboxed + fuel-metered; wasmi chosen over wasmtime; abi_stable banned). `guest_store_limits() -> StoreLimits` is the single source of the deny-by-default guest RESOURCE policy and a pure builder (param-free, no side effects, no reads of mutable state): it caps memory_size=MAX_GUEST_MEMORY_BYTES, table_elements, memories, tables, instances to fixed maxima and sets trap_on_grow_failure(true) so a guest that tries to exceed its budget TRAPS (surfaced as HostError::ResourceLimit) rather than allocating. This is the trade-off behind the wasmi-over-wasmtime decision: wasmi is a pure-Rust, no-JIT, dependency-light interpreter whose StoreLimiter + consume_fuel give bounded CPU AND bounded memory with no native codegen attack surface — the deliberate cost is interpreter throughput, accepted because untrusted third-party plugins run here while the trusted first-party path is Tier-0 native (NativeModel::price), so the hot first-party path pays nothing for the sandbox.

The `dispatch_risk` function routes the four `RiskKind` variants (Aggregate, Drill, Positions, Limits) to the matching `risk::run_*` SDK calls, threading through a common `RiskCommon` (endpoint, numeraire currency, FX rates) built by `risk_common`. The `AggregateReq` carries VaR shock scenarios (`var_shocks: Vec<f64>`), a confidence level (`var_alpha: f64`), and a curvature risk weight (`curvature_risk_weight: f64`), confirming the CLI exposes the full FRTB-aligned risk query surface.

serve_loop spawns one detached worker thread per accepted TCP connection so that concurrent peers (all dialing one-shot RPCs) are served without head-of-line blocking. A spawn failure is non-fatal: the connection is dropped and the peer retries next round. The loop exits cleanly when the stop flag is set (Acquire) or the listener closes.

handle_stream_end maps the server-sent StreamEnd reason to one of three exclusive client-level actions: (1) Lagged — emits StreamEvent::Lagged{last_good} and sends a Resync, then returns SessionFlow::Continue (the session is not torn down); (2) Draining — returns SessionFlow::Reconnect, triggering a whole-session reconnect; (3) Unsubscribed, Expired, or unknown — removes the subscription from the registry so the caller's Stream ends with None, then returns SessionFlow::Continue. Only Draining escalates to a session-level reconnect.

install_snapshot_adopts_a_strictly_higher_term: when InstallSnapshot carries a term strictly greater than the node's current term, the handler durably adopts the higher term (`save(term, None)`) and clears the vote, demotes any non-Follower role to Follower, and returns AppendReply { term: new_term, success: true }. An equal-term install does NOT trigger this path (vote is preserved). The adopt guard is `term > my_term` (strict), killing `> with ==`, `> with <`, and `> with >=` mutants.

gen_digital restricts corpus generation to CashOrNothing rows only, emitting up to 3 per (settlement_style, option_type) key and capping the total at 6 vectors. AssetOrNothing rows are skipped because the wire/server digital is cash-or-nothing with an explicit payout; this keeps the oracle mapping exact. Terms include `style: 'CASH_OR_NOTHING'` and the `payout` field. Tolerance is rel=1e-6/abs=1e-8.

handle_request_vote enforces Raft vote-granting rules: a pre-vote never mutates state and grants only when term >= my_term AND log is at least as up-to-date AND the node has not heard from a leader within election_min (leader_silent). A real vote refuses stale terms immediately; on a higher term it steps down (persist.save(term, None)) before evaluating; it grants only when (voted_for is None OR voted_for == candidate_id) AND log_ok, and durably records the vote before replying. Granting a vote resets the election timer.

all_families_present_and_unique enforces structural completeness of the golden corpus: every proto product-arm family in FAMILIES must have at least one vector, no unknown family may appear, all vector ids must be unique, any MC vector (price_std_error present) must have std_error > 0 and belong to an MC_FAMILIES entry, and all markets and tolerances must be sane (spot > 0, vol > 0, rel/abs ≥ 0, price finite). This check runs before any numerical regression so a missing or malformed corpus fails fast.

event_codec_seam_roundtrips_a_domain_event verifies the EventCodec contract: user-defined encode/decode implementations over the raw Journal byte seam must produce bit-identical recovery. The test uses a 12-byte AcceptedMark codec (4 bytes tenor_days LE + 8 bytes f64::to_bits() LE), writes three marks, closes and reopens, then asserts `got.atm_vol.0.to_bits() == want.atm_vol.0.to_bits()` for every record — confirming that the determinism contract requires bit-exact serialisation of f64 fields via to_bits/from_bits, not lossy float comparison.

PricingModel::price_and_greeks has a canonical default implementation that returns PluginResult::Err(PluginError::Unsupported("model does not produce Greeks")) — models that advertise Greek support in their ModelDescriptor MUST override it. When overridden, the implementation is expected to compute price and the full carry-tagged CarryGreeks (delta_spot, delta_forward, gamma, vega, theta, rho_dom/rho_for, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color) in a single pass, sharing the d1/d2 intermediate block to avoid recomputation. FlatSmilePricer (the reference implementation) overrides price_and_greeks and computes all 13 Greeks analytically in one pass from the shared d1/d2/sqt/vsqt block.

futures_style_equals_equity_style_at_zero_rate_bitwise asserts a structural identity: when the discount rate r = 0.0, futures-style price and equity-style price are bitwise identical across all tested market scenarios. For the full greek strip the two flavors are also bitwise equal on every field except discount_rho: equity-style carries −t·V (a non-zero financing charge even at r = 0 because it prices the term structure), while futures-style has exact 0.0. This proves the two pricers share identical mathematics except for the margining adjustment to the discount rate sensitivity.

post_trade_check folds all per-scope limit checks into a `ScopeMonitor` carrying the worst `RagStatus` (Green→Amber→Red→Breach) and worst `EscalationStatus` (Clear→SoftBreach→HardBreach). The worst status is computed by `max` over all checks; any hard-breach check elevates escalation to `EscalationStatus::HardBreach`. This gives the post-trade monitoring layer a single summary signal per scope without discarding the per-limit detail.

equity_pde_and_american_price_on_the_carry_seam verifies the carry-seam (ADR-0008) for equity underlyings on three levels: (1) the 1-D PDE call price matches a hand-rederived generalised lognormal closed form (d1/d2 via cost-of-carry b=r−q) to within 5e-3; (2) the American call price is at least as large as the European call (early-exercise premium is non-negative for dividend-paying equity); (3) the rate-sensitivity strip from american_fd_greeks is tagged RateSensitivities::Carry (not Fx) with a positive carry_rho for the call, and both rates are finite.

establish_stable_leader (raft_snapshot) is the Raft snapshot test's convergence oracle: it polls the node array until exactly one node leads continuously for a 250 ms stability window without term change, returning the stable leader index. It is functionally identical to raft_election's await_stable_leader and is deadline-bounded; it is called to prime the cluster before each snapshot/restore operation.

record_booked_position records a vanilla position into the live risk store only for vanilla instrument fills (non-vanilla returns early). The signed notional is BUY=+abs_base, SELL=−abs_base; a quote-ccy notional is converted to base-equivalent at spot. Failure to record is best-effort and never fails the trade itself.

append_entries_rejects_stale_term_and_accepts_current: the AppendEntries handler enforces strict term ordering — a request whose term is strictly below the node's current durable term is rejected (AppendReply { success: false, term: my_term }), while a request at an equal or higher current term is accepted and demotes the node to Follower. The stale-reject guard is `term < my_term` (exclusive), so an equal-term heartbeat from a valid leader is never falsely rejected.

multi_dealer_trade::run enforces two post-trade price-integrity invariants after fanning an RFQ across the LP panel via `client.request_multi_dealer_quote`: (1) the best-offer price must be finite and the best-bid must be at or below the best-offer (`!(best_offer.price.offer.is_finite() && best_bid.price.bid <= best_offer.price.offer)` triggers an error), guaranteeing the touch is non-degenerate; (2) the execution's `traded_premium` must be bit-for-bit identical to the panel's best-offer price captured before `accept_dealer` is called (`execution.traded_premium.to_bits() != offer.to_bits()` triggers an error), enforcing that the booking is never a re-price. An execution id of 0 is also rejected as evidence of no booking.

append_entries_adopts_a_strictly_higher_term asserts the Raft protocol property that an AppendEntries RPC bearing a term strictly higher than the recipient's current term causes the recipient to step down to Follower and adopt that term, regardless of the log consistency check outcome.

decode_observable translates a wire MarketObservable tag + optional delta into a typed Observable: AtmVol, Spot, and Forward require no delta; RiskReversal and Butterfly both require a delta magnitude strictly in (0, 1) — a missing delta or a degenerate value (zero, negative, or ≥ 1) is rejected with Status::invalid_argument before returning. The enum value Observable::RiskReversal{delta} vs Butterfly{delta} is preserved exactly, so callers can distinguish the two wing observables.

celnet-cli is the single-binary CLI for the entire celnet FX-options platform. Its public contract is the `dispatch` function: given a parsed `Cli` value and a `Write` sink, it routes all 14 commands (Price, Surface, Exotic, Basket, Forward, Swap, Ndf, Perpetual, FutureOption, Convention, Risk/Aggregate/Drill/Positions/Limits, Stream, Rfq) to the appropriate domain modules and writes a human-readable report. `main` calls `dispatch`, locks stdout, and maps `DispatchError` to `ExitCode::FAILURE` with a stderr message — zero panics on valid input. New commands plug in by adding a `Command` variant, a corresponding `Args` struct via clap, and a dispatch arm.

The `concurrent_admits_never_exceed_cap` test stress-validates the lock-free CAS loop in `try_admit` under 16 concurrent threads each issuing 200 admission attempts against cap=8. It tracks the maximum observed `inflight` value via `AtomicU32::fetch_max` with `Ordering::Relaxed` and asserts `max_seen <= cap` after all threads join. It also asserts `inflight == Some(0)` after completion, confirming that every `Permit` dropped by threads releases its counter slot.

Journal::append guarantees single-write atomicity and per-record durability: the entire framed record (sync word + header + payload + CRC, built by frame_record into a single buffer) is written via a single write_all call so a crash produces either nothing or a detectable torn-tail prefix, never an interleaved partial frame. `sync_data()` is called before updating in-memory state (`end_offset`, `next_sequence`), so the sequence number is committed only after the record reaches stable storage. Payloads are bounded to MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN (64 MiB); exceeding that returns `JournalError::PayloadTooLarge` before any I/O.

`price_instrument` is the single dispatch function for all 24 product arms (Vanilla, Strategy, SingleBarrier, DoubleBarrier, Digital, Touch, VarianceSwap, VolatilitySwap, AsianOption, ForwardStart, Cliquet, Quanto, Tarf, Pivot, Accumulator, Lookback, American, Basket, WindowBarrier, FxForward, FxSwap, Ndf, PerpetualOption, ListedFutureOption). It enforces three routing invariants before dispatch: (1) expiry guard — every product except PerpetualOption requires `expiry_years > 0` and finite; PerpetualOption requires `expiry_years == 0` exactly (validated by `validate_perpetual_terms`); (2) asset-class routing — if the underlying decodes to a cross-asset class (equity/commodity/crypto), dispatch goes to the cross-asset leaf crates and LocalStochVol is refused with `PriceError::UnsupportedModel`; (3) carry guard — the FX path refuses a non-FX (cost-of-carry) `market.carry` arm with `PriceError::Domain`. The booking-model selector routes `LocalStochVol` products through `price_instrument_lsv` before the product match.

measure_conflation measures the producer overhead introduced by a stalled consumer using `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel` with bounded capacity: the receiver is held but never drained so the channel fills to `cap` and all subsequent `try_send` calls drop (last-value-wins conflation). The producer must never block — `try_send` is used exclusively. The function records per-publish latency in two HdrHistogram series (baseline: no channel; stalled: full channel), and captures `max_queue_depth` (the high-water mark of successfully enqueued items, bounded by `cap`).

read_full_or_short drives a Read source to full saturation, transparently absorbing every Interrupted error (via `continue` on `e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted`) and accumulating partial reads until the buffer is either fully filled (FillState::Full), returns nothing at the very first read (FillState::Empty — clean EOF at a record boundary), or returns fewer bytes than requested (FillState::Short — torn tail / truncation mid-record). A zero-length buffer is unconditionally Full without touching the reader. This three-way discrimination is the sole place that distinguishes a clean EOF from a torn tail, and the Interrupted retry is the guard that prevents a transient EINTR from being misclassified as a short/empty fill.

RFS stream protocol invariant: the first event on every new `Subscription` is always `StreamEvent::Snapshot` with `sequence == 1`. Subsequent events are `StreamEvent::Tick` with `sequence` strictly monotonically increasing (each tick's sequence equals `previous + 1`). A `GapDetected` event must never be surfaced on a healthy stream — the SDK transparently resolves gaps via resync. Source: `baseline` and `drive_ticks` in `rfs_workflow.rs`.

EgressGovernor::new enforces three non-negotiable preconditions before constructing the rate-limited egress ring: (1) capacity must be non-zero (ZeroCapacity error otherwise); (2) drain_rate_per_sec must be finite and positive (BadDrainRate error otherwise); (3) burst must be finite and >= 1.0 (BadBurst error otherwise). On success the token bucket is initialized to tokens = cfg.burst (full), so the very first drain call is allowed to emit up to burst frames without any wait. The capacity fields of the internal VecDeque and HashMap are pre-allocated to cfg.capacity to avoid resizing.

HostError::fmt provides the canonical human-readable rendering of every host-layer error variant — each variant produces a distinct, prefix-qualified message: 'invalid wasm module:', 'capability denied: import `…` is not granted', 'missing required export: `…`', 'guest trapped:', 'fuel budget exhausted', 'resource limit exceeded:', 'abi violation:', 'model error:'. These prefixes are stable operator-facing strings; log/alert tooling may parse the leading prefix to classify errors.

Consumer::try_recv_batch drains up to `out.len()` items from the ring into a caller-supplied `&mut [T]` slice in a single call, returning the number of items written. It delegates entirely to repeated `try_recv()` calls and stops on the first `RecvError::Empty`. The caller owns the output buffer; no allocation occurs inside the method. This is the preferred batch-drain API for throughput-sensitive consumers (e.g. the FX price-fanout path).

gpu_load_measures_a_real_sweep validates that the GPU batch load harness produces a self-consistent report: exactly two batch sizes (1 024 and 4 096 paths) are measured, both throughput figures (GPU path and CPU oracle) are strictly positive, the latency distribution is monotone (min ≤ p50 ≤ p99 ≤ p99.9 ≤ max), and on a headless host (no GPU adapter) the backend label must contain the substring "fallback" and the gpu/cpu ratio must lie in [0.2, 5.0) — confirming the CPU fallback produces an O(1) ratio rather than a claimed GPU speedup.

calibrate_leverage calibrates the LSV leverage surface L(S,t) by forward-sweeping a particle cloud under the QE variance scheme. At each calibration time step the leverage column at the new level is set to `σ_loc(S,t) / √E[v|S=S_node]` where `E[v|S]` is estimated by Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression over the cloud (`conditional_expectation` with bandwidth from `bandwidth(&ln_s)`). The initial column at t=0 sets `L(S,0) = σ_loc(S,dt) / √v₀` since the cloud is a point mass. The carry rate is read from the implied surface forward curve `carry_rate(iv, t0, t1, dt)` to stay carry-consistent with the surface.

Carry::forward_factor(t) is a pure function computing the outright forward factor e^{b*t} via libm::exp(self.carry_rate() * t), where b is the net cost-of-carry (carry_rate() == r_dom - r_for for Carry::FxRates, == b for Carry::CostOfCarry). Multiplying spot by this factor yields the forward F = S*e^{b*t}; it has no side effects and depends only on (self, t). For FX this reproduces VanillaInputs::forward bit-for-bit, the single forward-construction primitive shared by every carry-seam leaf (ADR-0008).

replay_from_compacted_equals_replay_from_full_bit_identical is the core compaction gate: it builds a full 12-delta log and an identically-seeded second log compacted at watermark=6 (with snapshot = sum of deltas[0..=6]), then asserts (1) rebuilt state from compacted log == rebuilt state from full log == independent sum of all deltas; (2) the compacted log's first record is a Snapshot carrying sequence==watermark; (3) residual data records (seqs 7–11) are byte-for-byte identical (same sequence numbers, same payloads) to the corresponding records from the full log; (4) next_sequence is unchanged by compaction.

price_single_barrier_lsv() rejects two product variants that the LSV ADI engine cannot correctly represent rather than mis-pricing them: (1) discrete-monitoring single barriers are rejected as `UnsupportedModel` (the ADI engine imposes a continuous Dirichlet wall), and (2) non-zero rebates are rejected. A non-positive or non-finite barrier is rejected as `Domain` error. Accepted payoffs use calibrate_leverage_for + reprice + lsv_greeks; the knock-in case is handled via in-out parity.

The architectural invariant test in_process_price_resolves_locally_without_any_router proves that the per-tick hot price path never requires the router/federation layer: it starts a plain in-process Edge (FleetTopology::InProcess, no CELNET_FLEET_BACKENDS env var, no fleet handle), issues a real PriceRequest over loopback gRPC, and asserts `greeks.price.is_finite() && greeks.price > 0.0`. Because there is no router, the ONLY way the call can succeed is via the Serve::Local arm — a regression that accidentally routes would fail with no forwarding target.

measure_batch times GPU dispatch for a single batch size using an open-loop injector with HdrHistogram CO-correction (clone_correct against the measured median) applied to a clone, so observed stalls only inflate the tail. It also runs an identical CPU-oracle sweep via `measure_throughput` and computes `gpu_over_cpu_ratio = gpu_throughput / cpu_throughput`, making the reported ratio self-contained and host-local. The function returns a `BatchPoint` capturing latency distribution, GPU throughput, CPU throughput, and the ratio.

stream_and_rfq_reject_a_contradictory_tenor_expiry_pair validates that when both --tenor (e.g. "3M") and --expiry-years (e.g. 1.0) are supplied with inconsistent values, both the `stream` and `rfq` CLI subcommands return DispatchError::Invalid with a message containing the word "contradicts", and this check occurs before any network round-trip.

reprice() prices an LsvPayoff (vanilla, knockout, or window barrier) by constructing an LsvModel calibrated from the current leverage surface and dispatching to the appropriate PDE pricer. For knock-in barriers it applies in-out parity under the SAME model: KI = vanilla − KO (computed at the same grid resolution), rather than directly pricing a knock-in PDE. Window-barrier expiry clamping (`start.min(expiry)`, `end.min(expiry)`) prevents the window from extending past maturity.

handle_frame is the sole dispatch point for every ServerStreamMessage variant on a live RFS/market-series session. It routes Snapshot/Update/Heartbeat/StreamEnd to per-subscription handlers that update the registry and deliver StreamEvents, routes Executed/StreamReject to the ExecuteWaiters one-shot table for click-to-trade resolution, and routes MarketSeriesSnapshot/MarketSeriesPoint to the separate SeriesRegistry — never cross-routing between the two registries. A missing subscription_id in any frame is silently discarded (SessionFlow::Continue) without poisoning the session.

Log.truncate_and_append implements safe log rewrite for AppendEntries conflict resolution: it (1) materialises the surviving physical prefix from the live journal, (2) appends the new tail entries encoded, (3) writes the combined sequence to a sibling temp file and fsyncs it, (4) atomically renames the temp over the live path (POSIX-atomic), (5) fsyncs the parent directory to make the rename durable, then (6) rebuilds the in-memory term cache to exactly match the rewritten file. The temp-write + rename sequence ensures the live log is never partially overwritten.

measure_publish_snapshot measures the wall-clock lag from a `StateHandle::publish` call until the state is visible to a concurrent lock-free reader, using a two-thread ping-pong: the publisher embeds an epoch into the spot field (spot = 1.10 + epoch × 1e-9) and the reader recovers the epoch by the inverse transformation, then stamps the visibility time via atomics. The publisher spins bounded (≤2 000 000 iterations) waiting for `seen_epoch >= published_epoch`, records the lag as `visible_ns.saturating_sub(publish_ns).max(1)`, and terminates the reader via a stop flag + join. The resulting `PublishSnapshotLag` captures HdrHistogram p50/p99/p99.9 in microseconds.

Baseline Storybook stories exist co-located with the 5 most important exported components under gui/src/components: Button, PriceTile, Panel, Sparkline, and GreeksStrip. Each story file (*.stories.tsx) uses the Meta/StoryObj pattern from @storybook/react, references only Aurora design tokens (CSS custom properties from --bg-*, --text-*, --bid, --offer, --space-*, etc.) — never raw hex or inline color literals — and is additive (the component files themselves are unmodified). The StatusBadge.stories.tsx scaffold story pre-existed; these 5 are the new lane-components deliverable.

The gpu_load binary runs a bounded GPU batch sweep and exits 0 on completion — it is a measurement/snapshot tool, not a pass/fail gate. It explicitly prints a disclaimer that absolute GPU throughput numbers are deploy-gated and not claimed from this host; on a headless host the run is labelled a completes-within-ceiling CPU-fallback check. The optional output path argument enables baseline snapshot refresh.

heston_table_loads_and_is_well_formed validates the frozen Heston oracle across all rows: all eleven numeric fields must be finite; model well-posedness constraints κ>0, θ>0, vol_of_vol>0, v₀≥0, ρ∈[−1,1] must hold; every price must satisfy 0 ≤ price ≤ max(spot,strike)+ε (no arbitrage vs intrinsic); both Call and Put option types must appear; and at least one row must have cos_valid=false, ensuring the Carr-Madan fallback path is exercised in the companion pricing test.

solver_strike_matches_independent_bisection verifies that the production Newton-based strike_from_delta solver and an independent derivative-free bisect_strike oracle agree to within (1e-7 relative, 1e-9 absolute) for all four delta conventions × both option types × three representative delta magnitudes (0.10, 0.25, 0.40). For premium-adjusted calls it restricts the bisection bracket to K ≥ K_max (the OTM monotone branch) to match the production branch selection. It also asserts the solved strike residual is below 1e-11 in absolute terms.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-qmc is the randomized quasi-Monte Carlo substrate for all path-dependent option pricing in celnet. Its public contract is: (1) `SobolSequence::new(dim)` builds a `dim`-dimensional scrambled Sobol sequence from the embedded Joe-Kuo direction-number table (up to MAX_DIM); (2) `BrownianBridge::new(m, t_total)` computes a bisection-order bridge plan for `m` uniform time steps; (3) `rqmc_estimate(bridge, budget, replications, base_seed, payoff)` drives the full RQMC loop — per-replication scramble seeds derived via splitmix, Sobol stream → inverse-normal → bridge build → payoff accumulation — and returns an `RqmcResult` with estimate + inter-replication standard error. A new pricing arm plugs in by passing a `FnMut(&[f64]) -> f64` payoff closure to `rqmc_estimate`; no other crate state is required.

`TenorParseError::fmt` produces diagnostic messages that teach the expected format: `Malformed` emits `"malformed tenor \`{s}\`: expected ON or <count><W|M|Y> (e.g. 1W, 3M, 1Y)"` and `BadCount` emits `"bad tenor count in \`{s}\`: need a positive integer"`. Both messages echo the bad input token so the user can self-correct without re-running.

`accept_loop` is the WebSocket connection lifecycle entry point: it runs a `loop { listener.accept().await }` and for each successful TCP accept, clones the shared `WsServices` handle and spawns an independent Tokio task calling `serve_connection`. Transient accept errors (e.g. fd exhaustion) yield via `tokio::task::yield_now()` and retry — they do not kill the listener. The listener is only stopped when the edge shuts down and aborts the task externally.

await_stable_leader polls a Raft node array until exactly one node holds the leader role continuously for a 250 ms stability window at constant term, returning its index. If the claimed leader loses leadership or its term changes within the window the search restarts. The function is deadline-bounded via assert_within_deadline and used as the Raft convergence oracle across all election and snapshot parity tests.

gpu_pv_grid / analytic_pv_grid produce a NodeScenarioGrid over a spot×vol Cartesian grid (ScenarioAxes). analytic_pv_grid uses the deterministic closed-form pricer (same GBM inputs as the GPU kernel, f32 axis values widened to f64 via f64::from to match GPU grid points exactly); gpu_pv_grid uses GBM Monte Carlo (PathSpec::gbm) with common random numbers, accumulating per-position variance conservatively as an upper-bound standard error. A non-FX/non-metal position returns None from fx_vanilla_inputs and is silently skipped in both paths — their grid kernels are named separate GPU workloads per docs/GPU-AT-SCALE-PLAN.md. on_gpu=true iff the ScenarioPricer is backed by a GPU device.

closed_form_vectors_redrive_from_independent_oracle is the master regression gate for all closed-form golden families. It iterates every loaded GoldenVector that has no price_std_error (i.e. is closed-form), re-derives the price from a code-disjoint oracle implementation matched to the family token, and asserts `is_close(recomputed, frozen, rel_tol, abs_tol)`. Families handled include: vanilla (Garman-Kohlhagen), strategy (Σ side·ratio·GK), single_barrier, double_barrier, digital, touch, variance_swap (σ²), volatility_swap (σ), forward_start, cliquet, quanto, american, fx_forward, fx_swap, ndf, perpetual_option (Samuelson perpetual), listed_future_option (Black-76 / undiscounted). Any unlisted family panics, preventing silent corpus drift.

handle_rpc is the top-level RPC demultiplexer: it routes AppendEntries, RequestVote, and InstallSnapshot to their handlers (all returning Some(reply)), answers StatusRequest inline (Some(Status{last_index, term})), and returns None for reply messages (AppendReply, VoteReply, Status) that are unsolicited on the serve path — preventing double-reply and infinite loops.

adversarial_bytes: a proptest strategy that generates three classes of byte vectors for decoder fuzz coverage — (1) pure random bytes (0–4096 bytes), (2) a structurally valid LogEntry frame with an optional single-byte bit-flip and optional truncation, and (3) a structurally valid AppendEntries wire Message with optional truncation. The union `prop_oneof![random, mutated_entry, mutated_message]` ensures the fuzz corpus is dominated by near-valid inputs (structurally valid but corrupt) that reach deeper decoder paths than pure noise.

Log::reconcile is the idempotent Raft log-reconciliation kernel: it skips any prefix of incoming entries already present with an identical term (pure append idempotency), then on the first divergent entry (same index, different term = conflict, or beyond the end = new tail) truncates the durable tail at that absolute index (translated to a physical position as cut_index - base_index) and appends the remainder. A debug_assert enforces that the cut never falls below the snapshot boundary — a committed, snapshotted prefix is never overwritten. Returns Ok(last_index) on success.

request_vote_prevote_requires_term_log_and_leader_silence: a pre-vote (pre_vote=true) is granted only when ALL three conditions hold conjunctively: (1) candidate term >= node term, (2) candidate log is at least as up-to-date, and (3) no leader heartbeat was received within the election-min timeout (leader_silent = elapsed >= election_min && role != Leader). A pre-vote never persists any state — voted_for and current_term are unchanged after a grant. A recently-contacted node (elapsed < election_min) refuses pre-votes to prevent disruption of a healthy leader (Ongaro thesis §9.6). The `&&` at line 1117 cannot be relaxed to `||`.

pending_execute_fails_promptly_when_session_reconnects establishes the guarantee that fail_all_waiters drains the entire ExecuteWaiters table atomically: every in-flight click-to-trade oneshot receives Err(ClientError::Reconnected) immediately when the session reconnects, and the table is empty afterwards with no waiter leaks across the session cutover.

RaftNode.compact_applied snapshots the applied state at exactly last_applied (the highest index known to have been applied to the state machine) and no further, preventing the snapshot boundary from racing ahead of application. It is a no-op (returns Ok(None)) when nothing has been applied yet.

`producer_loop` is the single-threaded price fan-out engine: it runs one dedicated OS thread per `PriceFanout` instance that (a) services all pending `SubscribeRequest` messages non-blocking (creating a `BroadcastRing` per new currency pair on first subscription, then handing callers a head-positioned consumer), and (b) drives all live `PairProducer` instances once per `PRODUCER_INTERVAL`. The thread parks for `PRODUCER_INTERVAL / 2` between iterations to avoid a busy-spin. When the subscribe channel disconnects the loop exits immediately. Slow consumers are not blocked: the ring conflates (overwrites) rather than back-pressuring.

RFQ attribution chain propagation: a quote requested with an explicit `Attribution::quoted_by(book, seat)` resolves to a `Quote` whose `attribution` field is `Some(_)` and names the maker (auto-pricer id or trader seat). The accepted execution (`Execution`) also carries `attribution: Some(_)`, proving the chain survives from request through quote through booking. Source: `rfq_carries_attribution_to_quote_and_execution`.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-fix is the FIX 4.4 session + FX-options dialect adapter. Its public contract has four layers: (1) Framing — FrameCursor::parse validates a raw byte slice as a well-formed FIX 4.4 frame (BeginString, BodyLength, CheckSum, MsgType present), returning a zero-copy cursor; FrameEncoder::finish assembles 8=/9=/body/10= and stamps the checksum; (2) Dictionary — validate(frame) checks required tags per MsgType and PossDupFlag conditional presence, returning MsgType or DictError; (3) Session — Session<S>::on_inbound dispatches admin (Logon/Logout/TestRequest/ResendRequest/SequenceReset) and delivers app messages (QuoteRequest/Quote/MassQuote/NewOrderSingle/ExecutionReport) through a SessionAction with seq-gap detection and FileStore/InMemoryStore persistence; Session::send_app stamps outbound sequence and stores for replay; (4) FX dialect — decode_strategy/decode_option decode multi-leg/single-leg option strategies from FrameCursor; inputs_for+price_leg bridge OptionDescriptor+MarketSnapshot into VanillaInputs for the pricer. Initiator::request_and_lift / Acceptor::run are the async TCP entry points. A new LP adapter adds a QuoteSource impl; a new message type adds a build_* function and a dictionary entry; the session layer is not modified.

batch_drain_matches_single_recv_and_conserves verifies that try_recv_batch delivers a zero-alloc slice-batched view of the ring that upholds the same three conservation laws as the single-item path: (1) the last delivered value equals PRODUCED-1 (convergence on latest), (2) c.received() + c.skipped() == PRODUCED (exact accounting), and (3) every batch is delivered in strictly ascending order with got.len() <= capacity (live-window bound). The key line is `assert_eq!(c.received() + c.skipped(), PRODUCED)` combined with the windows(2) strict-order check.

RiskEdge::federated_aggregate_risk() fans out to all reachable backends concurrently (latency bounded by the slowest, not their sum), then merges AdditiveRisk per (dimension, group) in deterministic endpoint-arrival order using `join_all` which preserves input order. The additive merge is commutative; the fixed order makes the result bit-reproducible across calls with the same backend set. Non-additive measures (VaR/ES, curvature) are re-gathered and re-derived once per group only when requested, not speculatively.

Journal::replay opens an independent read-only file handle (separate from the append handle) and iterates via read_one from offset 0. It yields both RecordKind::Snapshot (first, if present) and RecordKind::Data records to the callback f, in sequence order; it stops cleanly on Eof or TornTail and propagates CorruptInterior via `?`. The caller is responsible for interpreting a leading Snapshot record as the state baseline and subsequent Data records as incremental events. The replay is guaranteed byte-identical to the original append order because sequence monotonicity is enforced on every record at write time and re-validated on every read.

SmileModel::check_no_arbitrage provides a model-agnostic default static (butterfly) arbitrage check: it evaluates the undiscounted Black call price C(K) = F·Φ(d₁) − K·Φ(d₂) (via undiscounted_call, where d₁ = [ln(F/K) + 0.5v²t]/(v√t)) at each strike using the model's own implied_vol for that strike, then asserts second-difference C(Kᵢ₋₁) − 2·C(Kᵢ) + C(Kᵢ₊₁) ≥ −1e-9 (tolerance via is_close) over all consecutive triples. Requires forward > 0, t > 0, at least three strictly-increasing strikes. Returns PluginError::Unsupported("butterfly arbitrage") on negative density; PluginError::InvalidInput on grid/domain failures. A model that is arbitrage-free by construction may override with a cheaper proof.

SurfaceEdge::scenario prices an instrument on a Cartesian shock grid: each node's market context is built by applying the per-axis shocks (relative or absolute, by factor) to the base market, and the expiry is decremented by any FACTOR_TIME axis (theta roll), floored at f64::MIN_POSITIVE so the pricer stays in-domain. The grid is capped at 1,000,000 nodes to guard against memory exhaustion, and a missing or unrecognised smile_model tag is rejected before any pricing begins. When the topology is Distributed the request is forwarded verbatim to the instrument's pair-owning backend.

step_psor advances the American-option PDE one time step using a Projected Successive Over-Relaxation (PSOR) iteration. It forms the explicit RHS `v[j] + (1−θ)dt·L[v]` then applies the implicit operator `(I − θ·dt·L)` as a tridiagonal system. The Dirichlet boundary contributions are folded into the interior-end RHS entries before iteration. Each Gauss-Seidel update applies the SOR relaxation `v_new = v + ω·(gs_residual − v)` and projects `v_new ≥ g[j]` (exercise payoff) when `project=true`. Iteration terminates when `max_change < psor_tol` or `psor_max_iters` is reached.

admit_or_shrink is the strike-axis calibration guard that ensures every SVI slice admitted to the surface passes the no-arbitrage admission scan. It linearly interpolates between a flat-market baseline `(a_flat, 0, 0)` and the fitted `(a, c, d)` parameters using a scalar s ∈ [0,1], binary-searches for the largest s (up to ADMISSION_SHRINK_ITERS bisection steps) for which `well_posed_slice(...).map(passes_admission_scan)` is `Some(true)`, and returns that slice. The flat-market baseline (s=0) is admissible by construction, so the function never returns `None` due to FP pathology — only surfaces a caller error. This is the no-panic safety contract for the strike-axis front-end.

election_kills_leader_survivors_elect_and_progress_and_converge is the Raft leader-failure parity test for a 5-node cluster. It verifies four properties after killing the elected leader: (1) survivors elect a new stable leader in a strictly higher term; (2) the committed log prefix survives byte-identically on the new leader; (3) a fresh proposal commits on the new cluster; (4) all 4 survivors converge to byte-identical logs and to_bits-identical applied state that matches an independent single-node replay oracle.

round_trip_all_conventions asserts the full invertibility of the delta→strike→delta chain: for all four DeltaConventions × both OptionTypes × magnitudes {0.10, 0.25, 0.40}, strike_from_delta(conv, opt, target) must reproduce the target delta to (1e-7 relative, 1e-9 absolute) and the resulting strike must also round-trip back through a second call to the solver at the same tolerance.

ExtendedSurface::calibrate(pillars) fits an eSSVI surface in two passes: (1) per-pillar butterfly-projected damped fit via `fit_pillar(theta, quotes)` — each pillar is independently fit to (theta, rho, psi=theta·phi) parameters; (2) forward calendar sweep — for i≥1 each fitted slice is replaced by `prev.project_after(cur.theta, cur.rho, cur.psi)`, enforcing calendar monotonicity. The input pillars must be strictly increasing in theta (ATM total variance) and all theta > 0. The `ExtendedSlice::from_curvature(theta, rho, phi)` constructor enforces `theta > 0`, `|rho| < 1`, `phi > 0` and stores `psi = theta·phi`. The eSSVI closed-form butterfly and calendar conditions (`is_butterfly_free`, `is_calendar_free_with`) operate on these four parameters.

Fleet::connect_with_membership constructs a risk-federation Fleet: it iterates the supplied (endpoint, Replica) membership list, opens a gRPC client connection only for replicas whose health is Health::Up (Down replicas are added to the ReplicaSet but skipped for connection), and then validates the full ReplicaSet invariant (disjoint-cover) via ReplicaSet::new — any membership violation (overlap, gap, invalid partition) is rejected with Status::internal before the Fleet is returned.

`Client::aggregate_risk` and `Client::drill_risk` are the two entitlement-gated risk query entry points. `aggregate_risk` sends an `AggregateRisk` RPC built via `risk::aggregate_request(&AggregateQuery)` and decodes the response into a `RiskAggregate`; `drill_risk` drills one node into its children via `DrillRisk` RPC. Both calls pass entitlements through `principal_or_grant_all`: when no explicit `Entitlements` principal is provided, `Entitlements::grant_all()` is serialised — the authenticating gateway overrides this in production.

update_codec_round_trips_all_variants: the BookUpdate binary codec (encode → decode) is bit-exact across all three variants — Set (float value compared via to_bits()), Add (float delta via to_bits()), Remove (integer key). NaN and negative-zero are preserved correctly through the round-trip. A cross-variant decode (tag mismatch) panics, so the discriminant is encoded and checked faithfully.

PersistStore.open recovers durable Raft state (current_term, voted_for, commit_index) from a single file at the given path. A missing file is treated as a fresh node (PersistentState::default, term=0, no vote). A present but corrupt file falls back to default via unwrap_or_default. Any other IO error is propagated.

bucketed_risk computes three risk sensitivities independently: (1) bucketed vega via central-difference bump on vol with bump size VEGA_BUCKET_BUMP — only at the matching tenor pillar (others are exactly 0.0); (2) cross-gamma per factor pair via cross_gamma_value; (3) theta roll by reducing expiry by each horizon. Factor pairs must name two distinct factors.

rebuild is a test-local helper that applies the replayed Record stream to reconstruct an i64 running state: RecordKind::Snapshot sets state to the payload's i64 (overwrite), RecordKind::Data adds the payload's i64 (accumulate). This models the exact consumer contract the journal compaction guarantee must preserve — the rebuilt state from a compacted log must equal the rebuilt state from the original full log.

NodeCore.set_commit_index is monotone: it accepts a new commit only when new_commit > current commit_index (or when going from None to Some); it never rewinds. On advance it durably persists the new watermark via persist.save_commit_index before calling apply_committed, upholding the Raft safety property that committed entries are never lost across restarts.

The audit channel (`audit_channel()`) is unconditionally lossless under arbitrary concurrent producer load: every `record()` call on any clone of the `AuditSink` succeeds and exactly one `commit_blocking()` call on the `AuditDrain` eventually returns that record with a unique, gap-free monotone sequence in `[1, total]`. After all sinks are dropped and the drain is exhausted, `drain.committed() == drain.accepted()` exactly. The test verifies 8 threads × 4 000 records = 32 000 total with `BTreeSet` uniqueness + contiguous-range assertion (`seq[0]==1`, `seq[-1]==total`, `len==total`). This property distinguishes the audit channel from the telemetry channel, which is allowed to drop.

algorithmic_spot_date_matches_independent_walk verifies that spot_date_civil agrees exactly with an independent calendar walk across 27 currency pairs and every calendar day of 2024–2025 (~19,700 (pair, date) combinations). The test sweeps weekend/holiday/leap-day/year-end boundary cases and asserts the two implementations return identical (year, month, day) tuples — ensuring the production spot-date algorithm is bug-free on the full pair universe.

mc_survival is an independent test oracle for double-no-touch survival probability. It uses a reflected-Brownian-bridge continuity correction per step: `p_up = 1 − exp(−2(ln_u−prev)(ln_u−x) / (σ²dt))`, `p_dn = 1 − exp(−2(prev−ln_l)(x−ln_l) / (σ²dt))`, multiplied into a path-level survival weight `surv`. Each surviving path contributes `surv` (not a 0/1 indicator), making the estimator continuous-monitoring-unbiased rather than discrete-monitoring-biased.

gpu_greeks_reconcile_node_by_node verifies that the GPU pathwise-Greeks estimators match the CPU reference path-by-path within a derived tolerance that accounts for the f32 inverse-normal's tail sensitivity. For each path p, it re-derives the driving Sobol normal z using the same A&S erf-inverse as the oracle, then checks that all N_EST estimators satisfy |gpu - cpu| <= derived_greeks_bound_for_z. Strike-boundary indicator mismatches (estimator 3 difference > 0.5) are counted as 'flips' and tolerated only when flips < paths/200 (~0.5%), enforcing that GPU/CPU agree on path classification for the vast majority of paths.

LSV pricing on an unsupported product (e.g. `double_barrier` requested with `.with_lsv()`) returns `ClientError::Status` with code `InvalidArgument`, never a silent fallback to a different model. The error message names both `LOCAL_STOCH_VOL` and the product family (`double_barrier`). Source: `lsv_on_unsupported_product_is_invalid_argument`.

`digest_matches_independent_spec_bit_for_bit` pins the `PartitionKey::digest` output to a separately-authored oracle (`oracle_digest`) across seven combinations of pair × optional-tenant × optional-book (including zero, max u64 patterns, and None). Any change to shift amounts, fold/mix order, XOR constants, or tagged sentinel in `digest` / `tagged` / `fold64` / `mix64` will break this test bit-for-bit.

full_greek_set_against_finite_difference verifies that price_and_greeks returns a complete first- and second-order Greek set that agrees with central finite differences to within tight tolerances across four FX market regimes and both option types. Specifically: delta (1e-4 relative, 1e-7 absolute), vega, theta (sign-flipped ∂price/∂t), rho_dom, rho_for; and second-order gamma, vanna (∂delta/∂vol), volga (∂vega/∂vol), charm (∂delta/∂t), speed (∂gamma/∂S), zomma (∂gamma/∂vol), color (∂gamma/∂t). FX carry inputs must tag rate sensitivities as RateSensitivities::Fx{rho_dom, rho_for} — CostOfCarry inputs that tag as Carry cause a test panic.

RiskEdge::aggregate_risk gates every call with the readiness latch and authorization (RequiredAuthority::ReadAny), then routes to aggregate_risk_impl for the direct shard or federated_aggregate_risk for distributed mode. The two code paths are structurally identical in contract but differ in data source; no silent fallback exists between them.

`RiskError::fmt` surfaces all three error variants with distinct, human-readable messages: `Invalid(s)` prefixes `"invalid argument: "`, `Client(e)` delegates to the inner error's `Display`, and `Timeout(what)` yields `"timed out waiting for {what}"`. This is the only user-visible rendering path for risk-command errors.

gen_tarf generates 3 TARF golden vectors (put+full-gain, put+capped-gain, call+full-gain) using tarf_bank_pv_mc with MC_PAIRS antithetic pairs and family-unique seeds (0x7A1F_0000 + case_index). Vectors are stored as MC (price_std_error present). The oracle tag 'code-disjoint splitmix64 TARF bank-PV Monte-Carlo' makes the independence of the oracle explicit.

ScenarioPricer::map_readback is the scenario-specific variant of the GPU-to-host readback primitive. It follows the same bounded-deadline poll loop as the other map_readback functions but returns `Vec<f32>` (not widened to f64), because the scenario grid accumulates partial sums that are processed further in Rust before final conversion. The contract is identical in structure: exactly out_len f32 values or panic.
