priced_expiry_rejects_a_contradictory_or_out_of_domain_pair asserts three contracts on resolve_priced_expiry: (1) a tenor label that contradicts the supplied year-fraction (e.g. 3M label + 1.0Y) yields DispatchError::Invalid with message containing "contradicts"; (2) adjacent short pillars do not conflate (1W label + 14/365 y errs); (3) out-of-domain explicit expiries (0, negative, NaN) are typed refusals.

FixSession::on_new_order lifts a FIX D (NewOrderSingle) against the live quote book: it resolves the per-side tradable token from the named QuoteID (field 117) and the side byte (field 54), then calls ledger.try_book which enforces last-look. An unknown or forged QuoteID produces BookOutcome::UnknownToken; an already-consumed token produces AlreadyConsumed. A successful lift removes the quote from the live map for idempotency (a second lift of the same QuoteID will then fail as UnknownToken). Every outcome is reported via an ExecutionReport (ExecType 2=Fill or 8=Rejected).

run_drains_then_shuts_down_losslessly verifies the lossless-quiesce contract of PricingCore::run: after the stop flag is set, the run loop must drain ALL previously enqueued requests before returning. Concretely, N=1000 requests enqueued before the stop store must all be priced (return value == N) and all N responses must be readable in strict request-id order (0..N). The stop store happens-after all push calls, guaranteeing the final drain observes every enqueued request. The test uses a 10-second watchdog to detect any hang.

AuthEdge::login enforces brute-force protection before any hash work: an email locked out by the throttle (too many recent failures) returns Status::resource_exhausted immediately. For an absent or disabled user a dummy hash is still run through verify_async to ensure constant-time response and prevent user-enumeration via timing. A successful authentication issues a session token via the session store; a failed authentication records the failure and returns Status::unauthenticated with the generic message "invalid email or password" (no hint as to which field was wrong).

ScenarioPricer::price_scenario_batch computes a full spot-vol scenario grid for a given base PathSpec and PayoffKernel. It dispatches to the GPU pipeline when available, or to the exact f64 CPU oracle (Self::cpu_grid) when not — unlike the batch/path pricers, the CPU fallback here does NOT narrow to f32, so on CPU the results are full f64 precision. It validates the axes via axes.is_valid() (non-empty axes, grid <= MAX_GRID_NODES) before dispatch.

price_instrument_lsv dispatches to the local-stochastic-volatility pricer for Vanilla, SingleBarrier, and WindowBarrier products only; any other product returns PriceError::UnsupportedModel with model="LOCAL_STOCH_VOL". There is no silent fallback to the analytic engine.

unreachable_pillar_delta_surfaces_strike_inversion verifies that a pathologically large butterfly (σ_bf = 1e6) that makes the ATM premium-adjusted/forward delta mathematically unreachable at the 25Δ pillar propagates CalibrationError::StrikeInversion from market_strangle all the way through calibrate_pillar. This validates the error propagation chain: market_strangle errors are not swallowed.

`resolved_conventions_match_published_standards` asserts that the `pair_meta` registry for every pair in the `PUBLISHED` panel (>75 pairs) exactly matches a hardcoded reference table for spot_lag_days, premium_ccy, premium_style, ATM convention, option cut, settlement style, precious-metal flag, and NDF fixing/settlement — covering the G10+Scandi cross matrix, EM deliverables, EMTA NDFs, and metals.

PILLAR (CLAUDE.md guardrails 6 + 11 — IB-sized portfolios / many-instrument batch must rebuild surfaces within the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2 budget). `SurfaceBudget::architecture_1_2` is the authoritative encoding of the per-surface-rebuild p99 latency budget: a parameterless `const fn` returning `Self { p99_ns: 150_000 }` — the 150µs p99 surface-rebuild ceiling from ARCHITECTURE §1.2. Being a `const fn` over a literal it is pure and side-effect-free by construction (no allocation, I/O, or mutation); it has no WRITES edges. The surface_rebuild load harness (SurfaceReport::budget_breaches) measures each model's live rebuild p99 against exactly this struct, so the surface-scale pillar is reconciled against a single source of truth. SELF-INVALIDATING: editing the constant or signature shifts this anchor and flips the claim stale.

Consumer::try_recv implements the seqlock reader protocol with exact conflation (skip) accounting. On each call it: (1) loads `head` with Acquire; if `cursor >= head` returns `Empty`. (2) Computes `oldest_live = head - capacity`; if `cursor < oldest_live` fast-forwards cursor and accumulates `self.skipped += gap`. (3) Enters a spin loop: loads `stamp_before` (Acquire), checks it equals `want = seq << 1`; if not, re-derives the frontier and either laps forward, returns Empty, or spin-retries a transient mid-write. On a matching stamp, copies the payload via `slot.value.read()`, issues an `Acquire` fence (to prevent the aarch64 payload-load/stamp-recheck reorder), then re-checks `stamp_after`; a mismatch discards the copy and retries. On a clean double-stamp match, increments `cursor` and `self.received` and returns `Ok(value)`. The `skipped` counter records exactly the number of items conflated since construction.

The `unknown_replica_fails_closed` test verifies the fail-closed contract of `try_admit`: when a `ReplicaId` that was not registered at `InflightLimiter::new` time attempts admission, the limiter must return `Admission::Shed { replica, cap: 0 }` — it never admits an unknown replica regardless of load. `cap: 0` signals that no quota exists for that replica.

HotProbe.publish stamps each HotSample with a monotonically wrapping sequence number (self.seq = self.seq.wrapping_add(1)), stores it into the lock-free ring via rtrb push (which never allocates), increments shared.published on success via Relaxed atomic, and increments shared.dropped on ring-full — returning a bool to the caller indicating whether the sample was accepted. It never blocks or allocates.

The declared_minimum_memory_beyond_budget_is_rejected_at_load test asserts the memory-budget enforcement contract: a guest whose declared minimum linear-memory exceeds the host's resource cap is rejected with HostError::ResourceLimit during instantiation, not at call time. This ensures a hostile or oversized guest cannot OOM or hang the host process — the resource gate fires before any guest code executes.

read_full_or_short_retries_on_interrupted_then_fills pins the Interrupted-retry contract: when a ScriptedReader emits Ok([1,2,3]) then Err(Interrupted) then Ok([4,5]), read_full_or_short must return FillState::Full and leave buf == [1,2,3,4,5]. This asserts that the `continue` guard is necessary and sufficient; a 'guard → false' mutant would propagate the error and a 'guard → true' mutant would infinite-loop on any error.

measure_model follows a three-phase protocol for each smile model: (1) one-off cold calibration via `cold_calibrate` (timed but not §1.2-gated — it runs on a quotes change); (2) discarded warmup phase to fault buffers and warm caches; (3) timed open-loop injector of `recompute_marks` (the per-tick sticky-delta all-tenors mark recompute) with HdrHistogram CO-correction against the measured median. The returned `ModelRebuild` carries cold_calibration_ns, the CO-corrected latency distribution, and throughput_per_s.

barrier_and_digital_tables_load_and_are_finite asserts the CSV table invariants on load: (1) barrier table is non-empty; every row's {spot, strike, barrier, vol, t, price} are finite; price ≥ −1e-9 (non-negative modulo floating-point noise). (2) Digital table is non-empty; every row's {spot, strike, payout, vol, t, price} are finite; price ∈ [−1e-9, upper+1e-9] where upper = payout for CashOrNothing and upper = spot for AssetOrNothing. This test runs at compile time and catches corrupt or truncated CSV assets before any numerical regression.

`cliquet_clamped_mc` prices a capped/floored cliquet via antithetic MC with per-period local floors/caps and optional global floor/cap applied to the accumulated sum. Each period return is `max(cp·(S_k/S_{k−1} − moneyness), 0)` clamped by `[local_floor, local_cap]`; the sum is then clamped by `[global_floor, global_cap]` before discounting. The opening-spot scaling weights each leg's return by the period's opening spot, matching the plain-strip convention of `cliquet_plain_price`.

Edge::start_on_with_topology() is the single boot entry point: it wires all shared resources (one ReadinessGate, one SurfaceBook, one PositionStore, one SessionRegistry, one fleet connection pool if distributed) and propagates each Arc to every service edge before any listener is bound. Fleet dial failures surface at boot as io::Error, not deferred to first request. The WS mirror is started on the same shared service instances as gRPC — there is no second engine fork. The default admin credential is seeded on first run and logged as a security warning if a well-known password is in use.

FixLpAdapter::run_cycle encodes a Celnet RfqRequest into a FIX QuoteRequest (MsgType D) over a real TCP loopback session and lifts the response back to TwoWay. The FIX instrument block encoding is: tag 55 (Symbol) = 6-byte CCYPAIR (e.g. b"EURUSD"), tag 460 = b"4" (Product=CURRENCY), tag 167 = b"FXVO" (deliverable FX vanilla option), tag 201 = b"1" Call / b"0" Put, tag 947 (StrikeCurrency) = 3-byte quote currency bytes, tag 1194 = b"0" (European exercise). The strike tag uses push_strike which encodes strike as scaled integer + fractional decimal string. Returns Ok(None) when the LP returns a partial (bid-only or offer-only) or declines.

Session<S>::on_inbound is the FIX session state machine: it (1) calls FrameCursor::parse then dictionary::validate, propagating typed errors; (2) enforces CompID cross-check (tag 49 inbound = configured target, tag 56 inbound = configured sender) rejecting mismatches; (3) processes Logon/SequenceReset/Logout unconditionally outside seq-gap logic; (4) for ordinary messages detects a gap (seq > expected_in) and emits a ResendRequest(7=expected_in, 16=0) without advancing, or silently drops duplicates (seq < expected_in); (5) delivers QuoteRequest/Quote/MassQuote/QuoteCancel/NewOrderSingle/NewOrderMultileg/ExecutionReport to the caller via SessionAction::deliver; (6) handles TestRequest by echoing a Heartbeat with the TestReqID, and ResendRequest by replaying stored app messages gap-filling admin gaps. Returns SessionAction (outbound frames + optional delivered MsgType).

request_vote_refuses_stale_log_even_when_unvoted: RequestVote refuses a candidate whose log is stale (candidate's last-log-term < voter's last-log-term) even when the voter has not yet cast a vote in this term. The log-currency gate (`log_ok`) is applied conjunctively with `can_vote` — an unvoted state cannot override a staleness veto. This kills a `can_vote && log_ok` → `||` mutant that would erroneously grant a vote purely because no prior vote exists.

`orientation_inversion_is_non_contradictory` verifies that swapping base/quote via `CcyPair::new(cp.quote, cp.base)` produces a `pair_meta` that (1) preserves settlement, ATM, cut, precious-metal flag, and NDF fixing/settlement ccy; (2) flips `premium_adjusted` (because FOR↔DOM roles exchange); and (3) both orientations individually satisfy `is_self_consistent()`. This ensures the registry is orientation-aware, not orientation-agnostic.

decode_snapshot (exercised by decode_snapshot_seeds_history_oldest_to_newest) deserializes a MarketSeriesSnapshot wire message preserving insertion order of points: the resulting SeriesEvent::Snapshot carries points in oldest-to-newest order matching the original proto vec, with the observable type decoded, the snapshot sequence taken from the proto `sequence` field, and each point's value and sequence faithful to the wire.

gauss_newton_3 is a damped Levenberg-Marquardt (Gauss-Newton + L2 regularisation) solver for 3 parameters with per-parameter box constraints. Each iteration computes the Jacobian via forward finite differences (FIT_FD_H), forms J^T J and J^T r, augments the diagonal by λ (trust-region damping), and accepts a step only if it reduces the sum-of-squares cost. On acceptance λ is halved (min 1e-9); on rejection λ is multiplied by 4 and the step is skipped. The iteration runs for at most FIT_ITERS cycles and terminates early if the linear solve fails or λ exceeds 1e12.

ExoticInputs::carry_df() is a pure accessor computing the yield/foreign discount factor e^{-q*t} as exp(-self.carry.yield_rate() * self.t) — no side effects. Crucially it reads the yield rate q through Carry::yield_rate(), which for Carry::FxRates returns the STORED r_for verbatim; it must NEVER reconstruct q as discount_rate() - carry_rate() (r_dom - (r_dom - r_for) does not round-trip bit-for-bit). This keeps the foreign-leg discount e^{-r_for*t} byte-identical to the FX two-rate form on the exotics carry seam (ADR-0008 FX bit-identity).

election_safety_partitioned_minority_cannot_win enforces Raft §5.4 election-safety: a 1-of-5 partitioned follower with Pre-Vote enabled must never become leader and must never inflate its term beyond the value it held at partition time. The test isolates a follower by shutting down the other 4 nodes, then watches for 3 seconds (many election timeouts) asserting `role != Leader` at every check and asserting `term == term_before` at the end, confirming Pre-Vote prevents term inflation on rejoin.

GpuBackend::price_vanilla routes a single-instrument vanilla Monte Carlo pricing request to the GPU compute dispatch when a wgpu context is present, or recursively delegates to self.fallback.price_vanilla when not. The result is a Reduction struct (sum, sum-of-squares, path count) from which mean and variance can be computed. The recursion terminates at the CPU fallback backend which has no context.

write_node renders all additive measures (delta_numeraire with per-currency delta_vector legs, gamma, vega_numeraire, theta, vanna, volga, premium_numeraire) followed by optional non-additive measures (VaR@alpha, ES, curvature_spot) only when the server returned them. The output format is a fixed-column human-readable table with 10 decimal places for all numeric fields.

StochasticVolSmile::find_density_floor locates the first strike in the upward or downward direction from F at which asymptotic_density goes negative, scanning in steps of 0.02·F for up to 400 iterations. It returns that strike, or 2h (lower bound 2e-3·F) if the step would cross it, ensuring the returned value is always positive. If no negative-density crossing is found within the scan budget it returns F*1000 (upward) or F*1e-3 (downward) as a sentinel far outside any practical strike range.

Session::handle_client_message() is the per-connection RFS multiplexer: it dispatches each ClientStreamMessage variant to its typed sub-handler and upholds two invariants — (1) an Unsubscribe removes the subscription and sends a StreamEnd(Unsubscribed) reply, (2) a Resync is silently ignored if the subscription_id is unknown (no error sent). A client heartbeat is accepted and discarded (liveness only). Returns false only if a sub-handler signals the connection should close.

install_snapshot_rejects_stale_term: InstallSnapshot with a sender term strictly below the node's durable term is rejected without touching any state — the reply reports the node's own current term and success=false, and snapshot_index() remains None. The guard is `term < my_term` (exclusive), killing `< with ==`, `< with >`, and `< with <=` mutants.

Clock::advance() atomically adds `delta_nanos` to the manual clock source using `fetch_add(Ordering::AcqRel)` and returns the post-add value. On a system clock it is a no-op that returns `now_nanos()`. The AcqRel ordering guarantees that any thread that subsequently calls `now_nanos()` with Acquire sees the fully incremented value.

Carry::discount_rate() is a pure const accessor returning the numeraire/discount rate r used in e^{-r*t}: the stored r_dom verbatim for Carry::FxRates and the stored r verbatim for Carry::CostOfCarry. No side effects, no allocation, no Carry construction — a plain field read by match. This is the single asset-class-agnostic source of the discount rate on the carry seam; every leaf (vanilla/exotics/surface/risk and the crypto/equity/commodity leaves) reads r through here rather than matching on Carry or Underlying (ADR-0008 carry-seam architecture, docs/adr/ADR-0008-multi-asset-carry-architecture.md). For FX, discount_rate() == r_dom exactly, which underpins the FX df_dom byte-identity.

FrameReader::next_frame is the async TCP ingress gate: it reads from the inner AsyncRead in 4096-byte chunks into an internal Vec<u8>, searches for a complete FIX frame boundary (10=xxx<SOH> trailer), and enforces a hard MAX_FIX_MESSAGE_BYTES inbound size cap before extending the buffer. Exceeding the cap returns ErrorKind::InvalidData (tearing down the connection in the Acceptor run-loop). EOF mid-frame returns UnexpectedEof; clean EOF on an empty buffer returns Ok(None). A complete frame is drained from the buffer and returned as Vec<u8> ready for FrameCursor::parse.

The surface_rebuild binary enforces the §1.2 ABSOLUTE surface-rebuild budget (per-tick all-tenors recompute p99 ≤ 150 µs per model) by calling `report.budget_breaches()` and exiting non-zero with a per-model diagnostic if any ceiling is exceeded. The cold from-broker-quotes calibration cost is reported but explicitly not §1.2-gated (it runs on a quotes change, not every spot tick).

`basket_mc` prices basket, best-of, and worst-of options via antithetic-variate MC with Cholesky-correlated log-normal legs. Correlated normals are produced by multiplying the iid normal vector z by the lower-triangular Cholesky factor L (corr_z = L·z), one lower-triangular inner product per leg per path. The three aggregation modes (Basket: weighted sum, BestOf: max, WorstOf: min) share the same path simulation loop, selected by the `BasketKind` discriminant.

FixSession::on_quote_request mints the same keyed-MAC two-way tokens (mint_two_way against the shared ledger and minter) that the RFS stream uses, so a FIX lift authenticates through the identical token ledger as a WebSocket click-to-trade. The wire QuoteID(tag 117) carries the BUY token; the SELL token is stored alongside in self.live for bid-leg booking.

The `entitlements` helper in the `risk` module implements a three-state entitlement model: (1) no `--grant` and no `--deny` flags → returns `None`, which the SDK interprets as grant-all (parity with GUI/SDK/Excel clients); (2) one or more `--grant` flags → `Entitlements::scoped()` base with each grant added; (3) `--deny` flags alone → `Entitlements::grant_all()` base with denies layered on top. This ensures the CLI never silently over-restricts access when no flags are provided.

The `ShardRiskSource` trait is the abstraction seam for in-process vs distributed shard access. It exposes three methods: `shard_ids` (sorted replica list — doc: 'fan-in summation order is reproducible'), `shard_additive` (cheap net-Greeks + vega-ladder path; doc: 'callers must NOT rely on `.positions`/`.leaves` being populated'), and `shard_constituents` (full position-retaining roll-up for non-additive re-gather; doc: 'heavier O(positions); call only when a non-additive measure is needed'). `fan_in_additive_over` uses `shard_additive`; `gather_firm_node_over` uses `shard_constituents`; both fold via `merge_additive` over `shard_ids()` order. A shard not found in the source returns `FleetError::ShardUnavailable`.

dispatch() is the WebSocket frame router: it parses raw JSON, extracts a `type` discriminator, and routes stream-control messages (`subscribe`, `modify`, `unsubscribe`, `resync`, `execute`, `heartbeat`, `market_series_subscribe`, `market_series_unsubscribe`) to the shared RFS driver via `rfs_in_tx`, while all other message types are dispatched synchronously as request/response RPCs via `handle_unary`. Returns `false` only when the outbound channel is closed (connection gone), never on a business-logic error — malformed frames receive a typed error reply and the connection remains open.

lagged_stream_end_emits_distinct_lagged_event_and_resyncs verifies that a LAGGED StreamEnd does not tear down the session: it produces exactly one StreamEvent::Lagged{last_good} on the subscription channel and one Resync control message (with the correct sub_id and last_sequence) on the relay channel, and the returned SessionFlow is Continue.

drive_one_update guarantees that sequence always strictly advances past the last delivered sequence (debug_assert seq > sub.delivered). On a successful try_emit the subscription's sequence, delivered, last_market, and replay buffer are all updated atomically; on a drop (channel full but not closed) sub.sequence is NOT advanced so no gap or stale token leaks. Every HEARTBEAT_EVERY sequences an additional Heartbeat frame is attempted.

RiskEdge::limit_status_impl aggregates the entitled+scoped cube and checks every limit in the scope against the numeraire-expressed node. Worst RAG and hard_breach flag are derived by scanning all utilization records; a Hard-enforcement limit in breach sets hard_breach=true. Non-additive exposures (VaR/ES) are computed only when spot shocks are supplied; default alpha is 0.99 when not specified.

pre_trade_check walks every scope in the resolved `ScopePath` (up to 7: Trader→Book→Desk→CcyPair→Location→Entity→Firm), skipping scopes with no registered limit. For each registered limit it applies the incremental trade to a clone of the current `NodeAggregate`, calls `exposure_of` then `LimitSpec::classify`, and accumulates `LimitCheck`s. The final `PreTradeDecision` is: `Reject` if any hard breach, `Warn` if any soft breach (and no hard), otherwise `Accept`. The node_at and nonadditive_at closures are caller-supplied, so the engine is pure given those inputs.

two_consumers_same_pair_see_identical_ordered_ticks verifies the PriceFanout broadcast contract: two independent subscribers on the same currency pair receive ticks that are strictly monotonically increasing in tick_seq (no duplicates, no reordering), each tick's spot matches the deterministic spot oracle for that sequence number bit-for-bit, and for any tick_seq in the overlap range between the two consumers the spot value is bit-identical across both (same published broadcast value).

append_entries_commit_advances_only_with_a_present_log_and_real_commit verifies that commit_index is NOT advanced when the leader_commit field refers to an entry not yet present in the follower's log — i.e. the follower only advances its commit to min(leader_commit, last_new_index), preventing application of entries that were not yet replicated.

Session::handle_series_subscribe refuses a series subscription with Status::failed_precondition if the observable is not derivable from live state (observe returns None — degenerate wing case), rather than opening a series that can never emit. The opening MarketSeriesSnapshot with sequence=1 is sent with a blocking await before the series is registered in self.series.

`non_psd_correlation_is_a_domain_error` asserts that `price_basket` returns `Err(CorrelationError::NotPositiveDefinite)` when given a correlation matrix with an off-diagonal entry > 1 (here ρ=1.01), and panics if any other result is produced. This ensures the Cholesky decomposition path is guarded and invalid correlations never silently produce garbage prices.

partition_is_disjoint_cover verifies the disjoint-cover property of the fleet's partition scheme: given a book of N distinct position IDs and a replica set, partition_facts produces a reducer such that (1) every fact appears exactly once across all shards (no drop, no duplication — reducer.total_facts() == facts.len()); (2) each shard's fact count matches the independently-computed HRW natural-owner count for that replica; (3) the number of non-empty shards equals the number of replicas that own at least one fact. This guarantees that the risk aggregation layer receives a complete, non-overlapping partition of the book.

`accumulator_client_pv_mc` prices a barrier-knock-out accumulator from the client's perspective under two monitoring regimes. Under `Discrete` monitoring each fixing is a hard knock-out: if S_k ≥ barrier the path terminates. Under `Continuous` monitoring a Brownian-bridge survival probability `1 − exp(−2·ln(B/S_{k−1})·ln(B/S_k) / (σ²dt))` is accumulated per segment, weighting each coupon. The coupon at each fixing is `S_k − pivot` (above pivot) or `−leverage·(pivot − S_k)` (below), scaled by notional and per-fixing discount factor.

FixSession::serve drives the full FIX session I/O loop: it splits the stream into read/write halves, reads frames via FrameReader, records every inbound frame to the fix_monitor before processing, records every outbound frame after generating it, writes each response in order, and breaks the loop when the session state reaches Disconnected AND at least one outbound message has been sent (next_outbound > 1), ensuring the FIX logout handshake completes before the TCP connection drops.

LsvModel::run_path advances one MC path under the calibrated LSV model and returns the terminal spot and window-barrier survival probability. Each step applies the QE variance update `qe_variance_step(var, v, dt, u_var)`, reads the leverage interpolated from the calibrated surface at `(s_prev, t0)`, then computes `log_spot_increment(var, v, v_next, dt, lev, z_perp)`. Antithetic paths are generated by reflecting both uniforms about ½ for negative `s`. Window-barrier monitoring uses the reflected-bridge survival `bridge_survival(ln_s, ln_next, ln_h, lev, v, dt, up)` multiplied into `window_survival` only for steps whose midpoint falls inside the active window `[start, end]`.

The RFQ lifecycle is encoded as four sequenced wire messages sharing an idempotency_key string: QuoteRequest (client idempotency_key + Instrument + Conventions + optional correlation_id/surface_version/AttributionRecord) → Quote (quote_id + TwoWayPrice + Greeks + resolved_strike + epoch_nanos + valid_until_nanos) → QuoteAccept (quote_id + idempotency_key + Side + lp_id, the lp_id field doubles as the multi-dealer LP selector) / QuoteReject (quote_id + reason) → Execution (execution_id + quote_id + traded_premium + epoch_nanos). The multi-dealer path extends Quote to MultiDealerQuote (dealers: Vec<DealerQuote> ordered best-offer-first, best_bid_lp_id, best_offer_lp_id); QuoteAccept's lp_id field carries the chosen LP.

`asian_arithmetic_mc` prices an arithmetic-average-rate option via antithetic-variate Monte Carlo with SplitMix64 / Welford online accumulation. Each antithetic pair shares the same normal draw vector z but simulates S under +z and −z, halving variance relative to a plain MC. The path is simulated in log-space (ln S_k = ln S_{k−1} + drift + σ√dt·±z_k) for numerical stability. Returns an `McEstimate{price, std_error}` with std_error computed by the Welford online algorithm.

measure_fan_out measures broadcast fan-out spread across N subscribers using N sync_channel<u64> channels (one per subscriber). Each subscriber blocks on recv (no busy-spin), so N readers on a core-constrained host sleep until the producer fans an epoch — they never starve each other. The delivery window per round is max_stamp − fan_start across all N subscribers, recorded into a 1ns–1s HdrHistogram at 3 significant figures. The FanOutSpread result carries p50/p99 window (µs) and p99.9 (µs); it is gated by fleet_slo arm 3 in bench_gate against the committed loopback baseline at the configured tolerance.

celnet-fanout provides a lock-free, allocation-free, single-producer / multi-consumer (SPMC) broadcast ring for `T: Copy` values. The public contract is: `BroadcastRing::new(capacity)` allocates once (rounding capacity up to the next power-of-two, minimum 2); `BroadcastRing::producer()` / `into_producer()` vends the unique `Producer`; `Producer::subscribe_from_start()` / `subscribe_from_head()` vend arbitrarily many independent `Consumer` handles (cheaply cloneable via `Arc` ref-count). After construction, the hot path (`publish` + `try_recv`) is zero-alloc and lock-free for all consumers. A new downstream arm plugs in by calling `producer.subscribe_from_start()` (to replay buffered history) or `subscribe_from_head()` (to start from 'now'), then polling `consumer.try_recv()` in its own thread.

`independent_business_day_predicate_agrees_with_library` cross-validates the standalone `independent_is_business_day` calendar oracle against the production `is_business_day_civil` for every calendar day in 2024 and 2025 across five pairs (USDMXN, EURGBP, EURNOK, XAUEUR, XAUUSD). No disagreement is tolerated — this proves the parity oracle and production library share the same holiday table for spot-date computation.

american_fd solves the American/Bermudan option pricing LCP via a Crank-Nicolson/Rannacher PSOR finite-difference scheme on an exponentially-spaced log-spot grid. It applies Rannacher smoothing (full implicit θ=1) for the first grid.rannacher_steps time steps then switches to Crank-Nicolson (θ=0.5) for the remainder. For Bermudan-exercisable layers it solves the PSOR LCP (V ≥ intrinsic g) via step_psor; for between-date layers it runs the plain European implicit step. Far-field boundary conditions are applied before each step via FarField::apply, with the early-exercise floor only on exercisable layers. Returns the price interpolated at the current spot from the FD grid.

serve_connection accepts a WebSocket connection under hard transport caps (limits::transport_config) and gates the session on readiness before any frames are processed. The connection multiplexes two concerns: inline request/response RPCs dispatched via handle_unary, and the streaming RFS session driven by the shared run_session driver. Frames exceeding MAX_CONTRACT_MESSAGE_BYTES are refused with a typed error frame and a RFC 6455 1009 close before the parser sees them.

drain_loop() is the governed vendor-feed egress pump. It upholds three contracts: (1) it never busy-spins — the only await that can park is `rx.recv()`, (2) a burst of ready updates is coalesced into the ring governor before the next drain, conflating per-key rather than flushing one-at-a-time, (3) on channel close it performs a bounded final flush (at most 4096 `yield_now` iterations) to drain the pending ring, never hanging.

MultiStepPathPricer::path_payoffs returns one discounted path payoff per path for a multi-step Asian/path-dependent instrument, dispatched to GPU when available, else CPU (with the same f32-narrowing: `f64::from(p as f32)`). It enforces both spec.paths in 1..=MAX_PATHS and spec.steps in 1..=MAX_STEPS before dispatch, ensuring the GPU buffer dimensions are always valid.

price_basket prices a multi-asset basket option via scrambled Sobol QMC with Brownian bridge construction and Cholesky correlation. It runs cfg.replications independent scrambles (each a fresh SobolSequence::stream seed via derive_seed) of cfg.budget paths. Across-leg correlation is applied per step by Cholesky::apply to independent per-step normals before passing to bridge.build — this propagates ρ through the full path covariance. The inter-replication variance of rep_means is the std_error denominator, requiring ≥2 scrambles. Rejects non-PSD correlation matrices (cholesky returns CorrelationError). Scratch buffers (u, z_step, x_step, z_corr, path, w_terminal) are reused across paths — zero per-path allocation in the hot loop beyond the Sobol point.

arc_swap_state_observed_without_locking verifies that StateHandle::load is lock-free and always returns a coherent MarketState snapshot: under a writer spinning spot values from 1.10 to 2.0, every load() result must satisfy spot.is_finite() && spot > 0.0, and the derived forward() value must also be finite and positive. This confirms the ArcSwap-backed state handle provides atomic whole-struct visibility with no tearing between spot and its derived fields.

`strike_surface(pillars, max_vol_error)` is the multi-tenor surface assembler for the strike-axis front-end. It iterates over `(StrikeSliceContext, StrikeQuoteSlice)` pillars in order, calls `fit_strike_slice` on each, and gates on `max_vol_error`: if any pillar's `fit.max_vol_error` is non-finite or exceeds `max_vol_error`, it returns `Err(CalibrationError::NoConvergence)` immediately (failing fast, not partially-populated). On success it pushes each `TenorPillar::new(fit.slice, ctx.forward(), ctx.t)` into a `Vec` and wraps them in `VolSurface::new(SmileModel::Parametric, tenor_pillars)`. Callers must supply pillars in strictly-increasing `t` order; the `VolSurface` constructor enforces this and returns an error if violated. The `surface_gates_bad_pillar` test confirms the early-exit: a deliberately hostile quote set causes `strike_surface` to return `Err(CalibrationError::NoConvergence)` rather than yield a partially-fit surface.

fx_carry_pricer_is_bit_identical_to_direct asserts that FxPricer (the trait-based carry pricer) produces results bit-identical to the direct free functions price() and greeks() for every row in the frozen golden CSV (>100 rows). The check covers all 14 Greeks in the full strip: price, delta_spot, delta_forward, gamma, vega, theta, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color, rho_dom, rho_for. Rate sensitivities must be reported as RateSensitivities::Fx{rho_dom, rho_for} — the Carry variant is an error.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-exotics/src/rng.rs: CounterRng is the exotics Monte-Carlo path RNG, a CPU-side 4×32/10-round counter-based CBRNG (Salmon et al. 2011). Its contract: given (seed, stream, path, step) it delivers an infinite, reproducible, bit-identical sequence of f64 uniforms in (0,1) via next_u01(), with one block() call per 4 draws. The counter partition (path/step/draw) and key partition (seed/stream) guarantee that each logical Monte-Carlo coordinate maps to a unique, non-overlapping sub-stream — enabling embarrassingly-parallel pricing where any path or step can be drawn independently and out of order on CPU or GPU with identical output. Verified by KAT (block_matches_published_known_answer_vectors), moment convergence (uniform_moments), open-interval guarantee (uniform_in_open_unit_interval), and stream-collision absence (distinct_paths_do_not_collide_in_first_block, distinct_coordinates_differ).

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-exotics/src/stochvol.rs: provides a complete, allocation-free Heston/stochastic-volatility Monte-Carlo step for FX exotic pricing. The seam is: (1) VarianceParams holds the five CIR/Heston parameters (v0, κ, θ, ξ, ρ) plus Feller-condition introspection (satisfies_feller / feller_ratio = 2κθ/ξ²); (2) qe_variance_step advances the variance by one step using Andersen's (2008) QE scheme — exact conditional moments, two-branch (squared-Gaussian / exponential-atom), degenerate-limit guard — consuming one CounterRng uniform; (3) log_spot_increment constructs the corresponding log-spot increment using the broadband (γ1=γ2=½) stochastic-integral substitution and full-truncation, consuming one independent normal z_perp; (4) step_uniforms extracts the canonical (u_var, u_spot) pair from the counter-RNG address (seed,stream,path,step). Tests verify non-negativity of QE output (qe_is_non_negative), conditional mean convergence (qe_matches_conditional_mean), exact branch formulas (qe_branches_match_hand_derived_scheme), log-spot formula (log_spot_increment_matches_hand_derivation), zero-xi determinism (zero_vol_of_var_is_deterministic), and Feller detection (feller_condition_detection).

AuthEdge::create_user enforces creation invariants before writing: email must pass valid_email, display_name must be non-empty, password must pass check_password_strength, the desk (if set) must already exist, and no user with the same email may exist. Argon2 hashing is performed off the lock (async worker) before the write lock is taken. The new user is written via persist_and_commit, which atomically updates the in-memory store and durably persists it.

SocketTransport::next_frame implements a length-prefixed binary framing protocol with a fixed 13-byte header (1-byte opcode | 8-byte little-endian sequence | 4-byte little-endian body length) followed by a variable-length UTF-8 JSON body. A clean EOF (UnexpectedEof) returns Ok(None) signaling the feed closed normally. Any other read error, UTF-8 violation, JSON parse failure, or unknown opcode (not OP_SNAPSHOT or OP_DELTA) returns Err. The sequence number is transmitted as u64 LE and the body length as u32 LE. This contract must be respected by both the vendor feed sender and the resilient subscriber loop that calls this method.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-plugin-host is the Tier-2 wasmi sandbox host for user-supplied pricing models. Its public contract has two seams: (1) ModelRegistry, which accepts native Rust models via register_native / load_wasm and routes price/price_and_greeks calls to any registered model by ModelId; (2) WasmModel, which loads and validates a .wasm blob against a strictly-enumerated capability surface (exactly five math imports: celnet_math::{exp, ln, sqrt, norm_pdf, norm_cdf}), metered per call by a FuelBudget. A new model arm plugs in by implementing the HostModel trait (descriptor + price + price_and_greeks) and calling ModelRegistry::insert or load_wasm.

gen_listed_future_option emits 4 Black-76 listed-future-option vectors covering EQUITY_STYLE (discounted) and FUTURES_STYLE (undiscounted) margining across call and put. The spot field in the market struct IS the futures price, and r_dom = r_for = r so that the GBM carry b = r_dom − r_for = 0 (the futures-measure martingale carry). Tolerance is rel=1e-9/abs=1e-9 — the tightest in the corpus — because Black-76 via libm::erf is reproduced to near-ULP. Oracle names cite Haug (2007) and annotate the at-parity and undiscounted-parity degeneracy.

`structural_invariants_hold_for_every_covered_pair` verifies six structural contracts for every published pair: (1) `is_self_consistent()` holds; (2) NDF pairs carry USD settlement and the restricted EM leg is not the settlement ccy; (3) precious-metal pairs have the metal as base, premium in the quote (fiat) ccy, `premium_adjusted=false`, and a loco-London lease leg; (4) `premium_adjusted` exactly tracks `premium_style.is_premium_adjusted()`; (5) `premium_ccy` is one of the two pair legs.

gate_b_partitioned_minority_makes_no_false_progress: an isolated leader (1 of 3 nodes, both peers shut down) cannot advance the commit index beyond the last quorum-committed boundary, regardless of locally-accepted proposals. After isolating the leader and proposing 3 entries, a 2-second sleep confirms commit_index remains unchanged and applied_bits reflects only the truly-committed prefix (oracle_bits of 2 entries). This enforces Raft's safety invariant: a minority partition must never commit.

The wire protocol uses a 4-byte big-endian length-prefix framing (MAX_FRAME_LEN = 64 MiB). read_frame_or_idle performs a non-blocking first-byte read: a WouldBlock/TimedOut on the length prefix returns FrameRead::Idle (the peer is live but has nothing to send — used by the tick loop to distinguish idle heartbeat intervals from real I/O); any subsequent read after the first byte uses a blocking read with the prior timeout restored. Frames above MAX_FRAME_LEN are rejected with WireError::FrameTooLarge before the body is read. The Message enum carries seven variants: AppendEntries, AppendReply, RequestVote (with pre_vote flag implementing the Ongaro §9.6 Pre-Vote optimisation), VoteReply, InstallSnapshot, StatusRequest, Status.

handle_install_snapshot enforces four sequential guards before installing: (1) reject stale term without touching state; (2) adopt a higher term (persist.save) and become Follower; (3) decode and reject a corrupt snapshot (success=false, leader retries); (4) reject a mismatched RPC header vs snapshot boundary. Only on all guards passing does it call install_snapshot; IO failure replies success=false. A successful reply reports match_index = max(log.last_index, last_included_index) so the leader advances next_index correctly even if the follower's retained tail already extends past the boundary.

LegBuilder::field populates multileg leg fields from FIX repeating-group tags: 612→strike (float), 624→side (LegSide byte), 623→ratio (float), 1358→option_type (put/call), 609→SecurityType (settlement). Unknown tags are silently ignored. Malformed values return a typed DialectError rather than silently defaulting.

dialect_decode_reprices_against_golden verifies that the round-trip encode→FrameCursor::parse→decode_option→price_leg reproduces QuantLib-derived vanilla option prices to within 1e-9 absolute error on at least one and up to 200 well-conditioned golden rows (t>0.05, vol>0.03). This test is the numerical correctness gate for the FIX dialect decode path.

Session::handle_execute enforces a four-outcome token contract via the shared last-look ledger (try_book): AlreadyConsumed → UnknownToken → Expired → Booked. Only on Booked does a trade proceed; the token is atomically marked consumed so any replay of the same Execute is returned as AlreadyConsumed, never double-booked. Idempotency keys are also checked: a retry carrying a key already booked returns the identical Executed without re-booking (`sub.execute_idempotency.get(&e.idempotency_key)`).

normalize() enforces a three-layer convention contract before accepting any vendor quote: (1) delta convention must match the resolved canonical record for the pair/tenor; (2) ATM convention must match; (3) the premium_in_foreign flag must be internally consistent with the declared delta convention (via declared_is_premium_adjusted) AND agree with the resolved premium_style. A mismatch on any dimension returns a typed NormalizeError (DeltaConventionMismatch / AtmConventionMismatch / PremiumFlagInconsistent / PremiumStyleMismatch) rather than silently accepting a mis-priced slice. The foreign rate is re-derived as r_for = r_dom − ln(F/S)/t so the forward F = S·e^{(r_dom−r_for)·t} is reproduced exactly from the feed's spot and outright.

Calibration::calibrate must be deterministic (fixed targets → bit-identical model), route numerics through celnet_core::math, reject ill-posed inputs with PluginError::InvalidInput (non-positive forward/t, empty targets, all-zero weights), and return PluginError::DidNotConverge if the iteration budget is exceeded or PluginError::CalibrationFailed if it converges outside tolerance. The reference FlatSmileCalibration implementation fits a constant vol as the weighted mean vol̄ = Σwᵢvᵢ / Σwᵢ in exactly one iteration (iterations=1), returning rms_residual = √(Σwᵢ(vᵢ−v̄)²/Σwᵢ) and max_residual = max|vᵢ−v̄|. CalibrationReport carries (iterations: u32, rms_residual: f64, max_residual: f64).

core_load::measure times the `greeks` function (full vanilla price + delta + vega + gamma) using an open-loop injector with HdrHistogram coordinated-omission correction: the raw histogram is cloned via `clone_correct(median)` so that stalls can only inflate the tail, never hide it. The deterministic `sweep_inputs()` corpus covers varied spot/vol/strike so the optimizer cannot constant-fold calls. Both warmup and timed phases use `std::hint::black_box` on inputs and outputs to prevent dead-code elimination. Throughput is computed as `timed_samples / elapsed_s`.

gate_b_bare_majority_commits: a 3-node cluster with one non-leader shut down (2/3 nodes = bare majority) continues to commit new entries. After committing one entry with full quorum, the test removes a non-leader, then drives two more proposals through the surviving pair, verifying each reaches commit_index and that all survivors converge to oracle_bits-identical applied state over the original 3-entry workload.

ResilientSubscriber::run_until implements a two-level reconnect loop for resilient vendor feed consumption. Outer 'reconnect loop: on each iteration it checks the stop predicate, calls source.connect() to obtain a fresh transport, resets all per-slice state to awaiting_snapshot=true / last_seq=None, and re-subscribes the full connection group. Inner loop: reads frames from transport.next_frame(); on a sequence gap it increments resyncs and issues transport.request_snapshot() for the affected key, falling back to reconnect on any transport error. Both a clean end-of-stream (Ok(None)) and any transport read error cause a reconnect. The stop predicate is tested at both loop levels so callers can trigger a clean exit without cancellation.

calibrated_surface_is_no_arb_across_stress_grid verifies that the eSSVI calibrator produces arbitrage-free surfaces under a full stress scenario grid. It checks two independent no-arbitrage conditions: (i) Breeden-Langer implied density ≥ -1e-6 on every calibrated slice across a fine strike grid (numerical butterfly-free); (ii) total variance is calendar-monotone pointwise (w(k,θ₂) ≥ w(k,θ₁) - 1e-9 for each pillar pair). Zero violations must be recorded across all scenarios, with non-vacuity asserted (≥20 slices, ≥12 calendar pairs).

projected_is_always_butterfly_free asserts that ExtendedSlice::projected(θ, ρ, ψ) returns a butterfly-free slice with finite positive ψ and finite ρ for all combinations of 5 valid θ values with 8 ρ values (including NaN, ±extremes) and 8 ψ values (including NaN, Infinity, and large values). The projection must clamp/project any out-of-domain input before constructing the slice.

`gpu_pv_grid` upholds three contracts verified by this test: (1) PV scales exactly linearly with notional — doubling positions doubles PV to 1e-9 relative tolerance under identical CRN bitstream; (2) standard error adds in quadrature — two independent equal-variance positions produce `std_err_combined = √2 × std_err_single` to 1e-12; (3) reproducibility — identical seed produces bit-identical `pv` and `std_err` arrays. Non-FX (equity) positions in the portfolio are silently skipped without perturbing FX grid values.

gen_pivot generates 4 pivot-TRA golden vectors covering dead-band (P > K call), overlap (P < K call), put dead-band, and the degeneracy law row (P == K == degenerate TARF). For the degeneracy row it runs both pivot_tra_bank_pv_mc and tarf_bank_pv_mc with distinct seeds and asserts that prices agree within 6 combined standard errors at generation time — a code-disjoint cross-check burned into the corpus before freezing. The oracle tag is 'code-disjoint splitmix64 pivot-TRA bank-PV Monte-Carlo'.

federated_drill_risk fans out a DrillRiskRequest to all reachable serving backends concurrently via join_all, then merges the responses using additive summation across shared group keys (BTreeMap keyed by group id, merge_node_additive for existing entries) and a union of positions (last writer wins per position_id). The child ordering in the response preserves the order in which group ids were first seen across backends, making the result deterministic and bit-reproducible across calls with the same backend order.

celnet-integration is the vendor-feed ingestion seam: it provides a linear pipeline (parse JSON vendor message → normalize to NormalizedSlice → multi-source blend to BlendedSlice) exposed as the `pipeline` function, plus stateful components (ResilientSubscriber, EgressGovernor) for live feed subscription and downstream price delivery. A new feed arm plugs in by producing VendorSmileMessage JSON and supplying its domestic rate; the normalize/blend/egress stages are shared and convention-validated for all arms. The three deployment modes (Standalone, Edge, Relay) are encapsulated behind EdgeBuilder.

mc_scenario (WGSL compute shader, scenario.wgsl @workgroup_size(256)) prices a full spot×vol scenario grid in a single GPU dispatch using common random numbers (CRN): each path p draws one shared normal z via counter_normal(p, 0, 0) (Philox CBRNG keyed by path index alone), then each grid node (i,j) applies its shocked GBM parameters (spot = base_spot*spot_mult[i], vol = base_vol+vol_bump[j]) to that same z, so prices across the grid are coupled by CRN variance reduction. The workgroup performs a two-level parallel reduction (payoff + payoff² into shared scratch arrays, then a halving stride loop, writing (sum, sum_sq) per workgroup-block per node to group_sums). The CPU oracle ScenarioPricer::cpu_grid replicates this exactly — drawing normals once and iterating over nodes — verified by `gpu_grid_reconciles_with_cpu_oracle` and `grid_is_monotone_in_spot_under_crn`.

LogEntry.decode verifies a CRC32 over all bytes up to (but not including) the trailing 4-byte CRC field before accepting an entry. Layout: [8-byte term][8-byte index][4-byte payload_len][payload_len bytes payload][4-byte CRC32]. Returns EntryError::Truncated for short frames, EntryError::Crc on checksum mismatch. A valid entry's payload is a freshly allocated Vec — it does not alias the input slice.

fit_pillar fits an eSSVI ExtendedSlice to a set of (log-moneyness k, total-variance w) anchor points with θ pinned. It uses deterministic damped coordinate descent over 80 rounds with 8 candidate moves per round (±step on ρ and ψ, including diagonal steps); every trial is projected through ExtendedSlice::projected to guarantee butterfly-freedom. The step shrinks by 0.5 whenever no candidate improves cost; it terminates early when both steps fall below 1e-9. The ATM point (k=0) is skipped because w(0) = θ exactly for any (ρ, ψ). When there are no off-ATM quotes it returns the flat projected seed directly.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-rfq is the concurrent multi-dealer RFQ engine. Its public contract is: (1) MultiDealerEngine::new(sources: Vec<Box<dyn QuoteSource>>) assembles an arbitrary panel of LP adapters behind a single async trait; (2) MultiDealerEngine::request(&self, request, deadline, now_nanos) -> Result<RankedPanel, PanelError> fans out in parallel to every source with a hard per-source timeout, drops non-responders and timeouts, applies last-look staleness filtering, ranks best-bid and best-offer independently with deterministic tie-break, and returns a RankedPanel carrying all rows + per-side winner ids. New LP adapters plug in by implementing QuoteSource::lp_id + QuoteSource::request; the engine itself is not modified.

install_snapshot_rejects_header_boundary_mismatch: InstallSnapshot validates that the RPC header's declared (last_included_index, last_included_term) exactly matches the encoded snapshot's own boundary — a mismatch (forged header) causes success=false without mutating the log. The guard is a conjunction (`||` → `&&` and `!=` → `==` mutants on the boundary-equality check at line 1057): both index AND term must agree. A correctly-matching header is accepted and snapshot_index() advances.

greeks_match_finite_difference verifies that the analytic digital option Greeks (delta, gamma, vega) from digital_greeks agree with central finite-difference estimates to tight tolerances. Delta is checked to 1e-4 relative / 1e-6 absolute with spot step 1e-5·S; gamma to 5e-3 / 1e-4 (second-order FD is noisier); vega to 1e-4 / 1e-6 with vol step 1e-5. The test covers CashOrNothing and AssetOrNothing styles for both calls and puts across three representative parameter sets.

TermStructure::total_variance interpolates and extrapolates ATM-anchored total variance in business time τ = clock.business_time(t). Before the first pillar it scales the first pillar's total variance by τ/τ₁ (constant forward variance, i.e. proportional to business time). After the last pillar it extrapolates at the last inter-pillar forward-variance rate (rate = max((w_last − w_prev)/(τ_last − τ_prev), 0)). In the interior it interpolates linearly in τ: w = w_lo + frac*(w_hi − w_lo). Per-pillar total variance is evaluated at the given log-moneyness k through the pillar's own total_variance(k) method.

fitted_parametric_slices_are_butterfly_free asserts that the output of build_model_smile for Parametric, ParametricSurface, and ExtendedSurface models passes slice.is_butterfly_free(0.6, 1e-6) on a standard benign quote fixture (σ_ATM=0.10, RR=−0.006, BF=0.0025). This is the production gate confirming that the parametric calibration path always produces no-arbitrage slices.

RFQ last-look enforcement: calling `RfqHandle::accept` after the 5-second validity window has lapsed returns `ClientError::Status` with gRPC code `DeadlineExceeded`. No booking occurs. The clock is advanced programmatically via `Clock::manual`, confirming the server enforces temporal validity of each quoted price. Source: `accept_after_last_look_is_rejected`.

Acceptor::on_quote_request prices an inbound FIX QuoteRequest via decode_option + price_leg and registers the resulting live quote in self.live with a validity window (valid_until_tick). Bid = mid − half_spread, offer = mid + half_spread. The live map entry is keyed by a monotonically minted QuoteID, enabling the last-look check in on_new_order. A convention/dialect decode error silently suppresses the response (no quote sent).

interior_crc_corruption_is_surfaced_not_healed verifies the headline behavior change over the marker-less format: a byte flip inside the payload of an interior record (record index 2 of 6, at offset 2*record_len + SYNC_LEN + HEADER_LEN + 1) leaves the sync word intact and the full frame body present, causing Journal::open to return Err(JournalError::CorruptInterior { at_sequence: 2, reason }) where reason contains 'interior'. The old format would have silently truncated to that point; the per-record sync word makes the distinction decidable.

`validate_non_deliverable_underlying` enforces a whitelist invariant: only a `WireUnderlying` carrying the `Fx` oneof arm is valid as the underlying of a non-deliverable forward (NDF). It returns `Ok(CcyPair)` on success (delegating currency-code validation to `CcyPair::try_from`), and `Err(WireError::WrongUnderlying { product_family: "non-deliverable forward", underlying: <arm> })` for `Metal`, `Equity`, `Commodity`, and `DigitalAsset` arms — each with a distinct `underlying` label. A missing `ref` (unset oneof) yields `WireError::MissingField { field: "Instrument.underlying" }`. The metal arm comment explains the rationale: metal pairs are deliverable (loco-London) and must never be accepted as NDF underlyings.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-risk-fleet is the distributed risk-aggregation crate. Its public contract: (1) `partition_facts` / `partition_facts_with` route a flat `[RiskFact]` slice into a `FleetReducer` by HRW-based partition key `(pair, tenant)`, failing closed on an empty replica set; (2) `FleetReducer` exposes `fan_in_additive` (additive Greek/vega-ladder fan-in), `gather_firm_node` (constituent re-gather for non-additive measures), `firm_var_es`, `firm_var_es_sensitivity`, and `firm_curvature_spot`; (3) the `ShardRiskSource` object-safe trait + `fan_out_aggregate_over` / `fan_in_additive_over` / `gather_firm_node_over` extend the same fan-out/fan-in pattern to distributed backends (returning `FleetError::ShardUnavailable` on an unreachable shard); (4) `fan_out_aggregate` / `fan_out_aggregate_over` are the one-shot entry points that produce a `FleetAggregate` (firm node + VaR/ES + curvature-spot + shard_count). `FleetTopology::parse` selects `InProcess` vs `Distributed` at startup from a `(mode, backends)` string pair.

price_perpetual refuses two degenerate domains with PriceError::Domain rather than pricing to NaN: (1) non-positive strike; (2) negative discount rate (no finite value). A CALL with carry > discount_rate also has no finite value and surfaces as Domain via the leaf's typed error. The rho bijection rho_dom = discount_rho + carry_rho, rho_for = −carry_rho is applied; theta and charm are identically zero by the time-homogeneous nature of the perpetual claim.

VendorTransport::next_frame implements the vendor-feed binary framing protocol: each frame has a 13-byte header (1 opcode byte + 8-byte LE u64 sequence + 4-byte LE u32 body length), followed by a UTF-8 JSON body parsed as VendorSmileMessage. An UnexpectedEof on the header read signals clean stream end (Ok(None)). OP_SNAPSHOT and OP_DELTA are the only valid opcodes; any other opcode returns an InvalidData error.

`put_call_parity_both_methods` verifies that both the Carr-Madan FFT pricer and the COS (Fourier-cosine) pricer satisfy put-call parity C − P = S·e^{-r_f T} − K·e^{-r_d T} to within 1 × 10^{-10} across a 3×2×3 sweep of strikes, maturities, and Heston parameter sets. A violation at any node falsifies the Feller condition or the quadrature accuracy target.

slow_consumer_conflates_forward_with_exact_skip_accounting is a real-time integration test that verifies two invariants of PriceFanout under a slow consumer: (1) delivered ticks are strictly monotonically increasing in tick_seq (no torn or invented values), and (2) exact skip accounting holds: `received + skipped == cursor − start_head` — every produced tick the consumer has passed is accounted for as either received or skipped, with no loss and no double-counting.

`raftnode_compact_then_boot_recovery_is_exact` verifies the full Raft compaction + crash-recovery cycle: after compacting at an interior boundary (last/2), `retained_log_len` shrinks, the applied state is unchanged, and after shutdown+reboot the recovered node re-converges to `commit_index == last` and its applied bits match the independent oracle — proving recovery from (snapshot + retained tail) is exact and no entry is double-applied.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-server is the runtime edge that owns the entire server-side lifecycle: WebSocket accept loop, gRPC service handlers (pricing, risk aggregation, quote, session, FIX admin), the multi-product pricer, and all supporting services (access control, price fan-out, click-trade, readiness drain). Its public contract is the unversioned celnet-proto gRPC + WebSocket JSON codec seam. A new product arm plugs in by adding a branch to `price_instrument` and a codec round-trip in `ws/codec.rs`; a new service plugs in by wiring into `WsServices` and calling `authorize_caller` at its entry point.

The multiplexed RFS (rate-for-stream) channel uses a single bidirectional gRPC stream (StreamService::StreamSession). Client-to-server messages (ClientStreamMessage oneof) are: Subscribe (subscription_id + Instrument + throttle_nanos + optional correlation_id/surface_version/AttributionRecord), Modify (re-baseline in place, no re-subscribe needed), Unsubscribe, Resync (last_sequence — server-assisted gap recovery), Execute (token + idempotency_key, click-to-trade via TradableToken), Heartbeat, and the market-series sub-family (MarketSeriesSubscribe/Unsubscribe). Server-to-client messages (ServerStreamMessage oneof) are: Snapshot (sequence=1 + full Greeks + TradableTokens), Update (sequence delta, Greeks, TradableTokens), StreamEnd (Reason::Lagged for slow consumers), StreamReject (Reason enum: Expired/UnknownToken/AlreadyConsumed for token-execution failures), Executed (click-to-trade confirmation), Heartbeat (carries telemetry: conflation_drops, server_price_p50/p99/p999_nanos, surface_version), MarketSeriesSnapshot/MarketSeriesPoint.

dictionary::validate is the FIX 4.4 message-content gate: given a parsed FrameCursor it (1) resolves MsgType from tag 35 bytes via MsgType::from_bytes, rejecting unknown types; (2) checks that every tag in required_tags(mt) is present (skipping tag 35, already guaranteed by the framer); (3) enforces the conditional PossDupFlag rule: PossDupFlag(43)=Y requires OrigSendingTime(122) to be present; (4) iterates all fields and for each known tag runs type_ok(spec.field_type, value) — unknown/custom tags are tolerated per the single-contract guardrail. Returns MsgType on success, DictError::UnknownMsgType / MissingRequired{tag} / BadType{tag,field_type} on failure.

SessionRegistry::validate() checks a session token against the live registry using the edge clock. An expired token (`expires_nanos <= now`) is eagerly removed from the map and returns `None` — there is no zombie-token window. A present, non-expired token returns `Some(user.clone())` without removing it (the token remains valid until its expiry). An absent token returns `None` without an error.

Blotter example integration guard: three vanilla-call subscriptions opened over a single `StreamSession` each deliver a finite-offer snapshot followed by at least one strictly-advancing tick (sequence > snapshot sequence), proving the multi-subscription blotter pattern streams live moving prices. Source: `example_stream_blotter_path_streams_moving_lines`.

`perpetual_engine_matches_independent_bisection_oracle` verifies `perpetual_price` against a bisection-based oracle across 10 parameter cases covering continuation, intrinsic-only, zero-carry, negative-carry, and the boundary condition σ→0. Both the engine and oracle must refuse a call with b>r (returning `Err(PerpetualError::CallCarryExceedsDiscount)` and `None` respectively), and agreeable cases must match to 10^{-10} absolute / 10^{-12} relative.

fx_vanilla_inputs(inputs) is a pure (side-effect-free) lowering from the generalized CarryInputs to the FX leaf's VanillaInputs. It accepts only FX-family underlyings (Underlying::Fx | Underlying::Metal — a metal's lease rate is modelled as the FX foreign rate) carried by Carry::FxRates, and typed-rejects every other underlying (Equity/Commodity/DigitalAsset) or a Carry::CostOfCarry carry with CarryPriceError rather than silently mis-pricing under FX arithmetic. The rate mapping is a verbatim field copy of (r_dom, r_for) — no recomputation — so the resulting forward/df_dom/df_for are byte-identical to CarryInputs::forward/discount_df (proved by fx_carry_inputs_byte_identical; ADR-0008 metals byte-identity).

`aggregate_nodes` converts a `Cube` (position risk store) into a wire-serialisable `Vec<WireRiskNode>`, either as a single firm-level aggregate (`dim == None` → `cube.firm_aggregate`) or grouped by a specific `DimensionId` (`cube.group_by`). The vega grid is constructed from the caller-supplied `pillars`. Each `NodeAggregate` is converted to wire via `node_to_wire(resolver, nonadditive)`, which collapses non-additive Greeks to the numeraire and may return `failed_precondition` if a required FX rate is missing.

The conformance harness `assert_conforms` verifies the SDK price against golden oracle vectors using a two-tier tolerance protocol: (1) For Monte-Carlo products (vectors carrying `price_std_error`), the gate is `|got - want| ≤ K_STDERR × (oracle_se + server_se)` — a combined-stderr band. (2) For closed-form products, the gate is `|got - want| ≤ tol.abs + tol.rel × max(|got|, |want|)`. For `window_barrier` vectors no closed form exists, so structural invariants are asserted instead: price finite, non-negative, strictly ≤ the unbarriered vanilla, within the documented wide flat-GBM model band. Source: `assert_conforms` in `conformance.rs`.

map_readback (in path.rs, pathwise.rs, and batch.rs) is the GPU-to-host synchronisation primitive. It initiates a non-blocking `map_async(Read)` on the readback buffer, then drives the wgpu device event loop with `poll(Poll)` until the async callback fires or a bounded deadline (GPU_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT) expires. On timeout it panics with a diagnostic message; if the callback channel disconnects without delivering a result it also panics. On success it casts the mapped bytes from f32 to f64 element-wise (widening with no rounding), unmaps the buffer, and returns the widened values. The contract: the call either returns exactly n f64 values (f32-widened) or panics — it never silently truncates or returns partial data.

ResilientSubscriber::ingest_frame() enforces strict-monotone sequencing per subscription key: a Snapshot unconditionally establishes the baseline (last_seq = seq, awaiting_snapshot = false); a Delta is accepted only when seq == last_seq + 1, returns FrameOutcome::Duplicate for seq ≤ last (never delivered out of order), and triggers FrameOutcome::Gap + awaiting_snapshot=true for seq > last+1 (a hole), gating all subsequent deltas until the next Snapshot re-syncs the key. Deltas arriving before any Snapshot (awaiting_snapshot=true initial state) are also treated as Gap.

gauss_newton_4 is the 4-parameter analogue of gauss_newton_3 with a caller-supplied projection closure instead of per-parameter box clamps. The Jacobian columns are computed via 4 forward-difference residual evaluations per iteration; the normal equations J^T J + λI are solved via solve4. Step acceptance/rejection and trust-region damping follow the identical λ protocol as gauss_newton_3.

Initiator::drive processes one inbound FIX frame through the session state machine, writes all generated outbound frames, and returns the application-layer MsgType to deliver. It detects the logon-mirror case (no deliver in action) by observing a LogonPending→Active state transition and surfacing MsgType::Logon to the caller, so the initiator loop can treat the logon confirmation uniformly.

apply_full evaluates the full 2D LSV (Local-Stochastic-Volatility) differential operator at every interior node and writes the result to `out`. For each (i,j) interior point not on a dead barrier slice: x-direction contribution is `½L²v·U_xx + (b−½L²v)·U_x` (centred differences); v-direction is `½ξ²v·U_vv + κ(θ−v)·U_v`; cross term is `ρξLv·U_xv` (4-point cross-difference). The operator output is `out[c] = a0 + a1 + a2 − r·U`. Boundary rows and dead nodes are left as zero (handled by Dirichlet/ADI sweeps).

ADR (plugin-host sandbox = wasmi, fuel-metered; chosen over wasmtime) — the error-taxonomy side. `map_instantiation_error(e: &wasmi::Error) -> HostError` is the pure, total classifier (reads only the borrowed wasmi error, mutates nothing; its only allocations are the returned short() strings) that lowers a wasmi LOAD/instantiate fault into the host's stable error enum: TrapCode::OutOfFuel -> FuelExhausted, TrapCode::GrowthOperationLimited -> ResourceLimit, "resource limiter denied" -> ResourceLimit, an unknown/missing import -> CapabilityDenied (deny-by-default capability surface), everything else -> InvalidModule. This mapping is the concrete embodiment of the wasmi decision: it depends on wasmi's specific as_trap_code()/TrapCode vocabulary, so the host error contract is defined in terms of the chosen interpreter's fault model — the trade-off being that swapping engines would re-write this seam, accepted because wasmi's pure-Rust trap codes give deterministic, panic-free, hang-free fault classification (no JIT codegen failure modes to model).

degenerate_variance_reprices_vanilla verifies that the 2-D LSV ADI solver recovers the Black-Scholes price when the variance process degenerates to a constant (ξ=0, mean-reversion κ=1, long-var=σ², v0=σ²) and the leverage surface is identically 1. For 3 strikes (90, 100, 115) and both calls and puts the ADI price must agree with the closed-form Garman-Kohlhagen vanilla price to within 3e-2. This is a mandatory regression gate for the 2-D solver.

hot_pricing_loop_allocates_zero verifies the zero-allocation guarantee of the hot pricing path: submitting 4096 PriceRequests through the wait-free request ring, draining them through PricingCore, and consuming all 4096 responses must result in exactly zero heap allocations (alloc count before == alloc count after). The path uses a closed-form pricer and wait-free rings — no dynamic dispatch or allocation is permitted in steady state.

gen_touch pins ONE_TOUCH oracle prices via discounted first-passage-density quadrature (oracle::one_touch_at_hit_price) rather than the QuantLib at-expiry CSV, because the CSV records the deferred-rebate product while the server's ONE_TOUCH pays at hit. The code comment documents the specific historical defect: a structural-copy closed-form oracle froze +28%-wrong at-hit literals (e.g. H=105 flipped value 0.0561744… vs correct 0.04378…). For all other touch kinds (NO_TOUCH, DOUBLE_NO_TOUCH, DOUBLE_ONE_TOUCH) the QuantLib at-expiry CSV price is used directly. Maximum 8 vectors are emitted, 2 per kind.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-commodity-vanilla is the commodity/futures-options analytics leaf on the carry seam. Its public contract is (CommodityInputs, OptionType, Margining) → (price f64 | CarryGreeks) with two distinct margining modes dispatched through greeks_with_margining: EquityStyle (discounted Black-76, used for physically-settled exchange options) and FuturesStyle (undiscounted Black-76, used for CME-style daily-margined contracts). The crate exposes two smart constructors — CommodityInputs::on_future (sets b=0, spot:=future price) and CommodityInputs::on_spot (sets b=r−convenience_yield) — that encode the standard cost-of-carry reparameterization. New arms plug in by calling greeks_with_margining or price_with_margining with the appropriate Margining tag; no switch is needed anywhere else in the pricing stack.

QuoteEdge::accept_quote enforces four hard invariants before booking: (1) readiness gate; (2) idempotency-key must match the originating RequestQuote key — a mismatched key is accept_key_mismatch, not a re-price; (3) a previously rejected quote cannot be accepted; (4) last-look deadline: now > valid_until_nanos → deadline_exceeded. A BUY lifts the offer; a SELL hits the bid. In a distributed topology, accepts are routed to the same backend that issued the quote via quote_owners map.

Snapshot.decode verifies structural integrity before accepting a snapshot: layout is [8-byte last_included_index][8-byte last_included_term][8-byte state_len][state_len bytes of BookState][4-byte CRC32 over all preceding bytes]. It rejects any byte-length mismatch, arithmetic overflow in offsets (checked_add), or CRC32 mismatch with SnapshotError::Malformed before decoding BookState.

request_vote_real_grants_then_refuses_a_second_candidate: the RequestVote handler upholds Raft's one-vote-per-term invariant — after granting a durable vote to the first up-to-date candidate, a different candidate in the same term is refused. The `can_vote` predicate is `voted_for == None || voted_for == Some(candidate_id)` (line 1140); granting to candidate A sets voted_for=Some(A), making the predicate false for any distinct B. The `&&` connective at line 1142 (`can_vote && log_ok`) is not collapsed to `||`.

Session::drive_market_series() samples each active market-series subscription subject to a per-series throttle window: a sample is skipped if `now - last_emit_nanos < throttle_nanos`. If a live observable produces no derivable value (`Ok(None)`), the sample is silently skipped rather than emitting a stale or fabricated point. On a full outbound channel the tick is dropped (conflatable) rather than back-pressuring the driver loop. Sequence numbers are incremented only on successful delivery.

exotic run dispatches the full ExoticSpec union to the correct analytic or Monte-Carlo engine. MC-carrying products (Cliquet, Tarf, Pivot, Accumulator, discrete Lookback, American with lsm_paths>0) are handled before the closed-form match and always return ExoticResult with std_error=Some. Closed-form products return std_error=None. WindowBarrier and the LSM/discrete arms reaching the closed-form match are statically unreachable().

PILLAR (CLAUDE.md guardrails 6 + 11 — many-instrument surface rebuild must stay inside the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2 p99 budget). `SurfaceReport::budget_breaches` is the pure, deterministic detector over a multi-model surface-rebuild report: it reads only `&self`, iterates the measured per-model `latency.p99_ns`, filters those exceeding `budget.p99_ns`, and returns a freshly-allocated `Vec<BudgetBreach>` (each carrying the static model name, the "p99" metric, the measured ns and the ceiling). No `&mut`, no I/O, no shared/global mutation — allocating the returned Vec is not an externally-observable side effect; it has no WRITES edges. Determinism guarantees a per-model p99 regression past the §1.2 surface budget is flagged reproducibly. SELF-INVALIDATING: a write or comparison change shifts this anchor and flips the claim stale.

degenerate_high_rr_quote_is_rejected_cleanly enforces the contract that any quote where |RR| > σ_ATM — making it impossible to maintain strictly-positive wing vols — is rejected as Err(DegenerateQuote|NoConvergence), never a panic, and never an Ok carrying a pillar with non-positive wing vol. The proptest reduction case (put_vol ≈ −0.0107) is hardcoded as a regression fixture: if calibrate_pillar returns Ok for that quote, the test asserts put_vol > 0 && call_vol > 0.

DrillReq.query constructs a DrillQuery from node + child_dimension + numeraire, then optionally applies: entitlement policy (if grants/denies non-empty), .children() flag (if include_children), and .positions() flag (if include_positions). The builder order is fixed and the query is passed by value at each step.

`NetGreeks::add_leaf` accumulates all eleven fields independently and exactly (bit-for-bit IEEE addition). The `Add` operator is equivalent to sequential `add_leaf` calls on two accumulators. Adding a negative-weight leaf genuinely subtracts (no accidental `abs` inside). The test uses exact powers-of-two weights (1.0, 0.25, −0.25) so floating-point accumulation is exact and bit-equality assertions are valid.

Determinism rule (docs/INTERFACES.md §"Determinism rules baked into the interfaces": "Transcendentals via rust-lang/libm (correctly-rounded) for bit-identical cross-platform results"). `celnet_core::math::exp` is the canonical e^x transcendental wrapper: it is `pub fn exp(x: f64) -> f64 { libm::exp(x) }` — a pure (side-effect-free, no WRITES) total delegation to the correctly-rounded rust-lang/libm routine rather than std's platform libm, so every consumer (e.g. norm_pdf, Carry::forward_factor/discount_df via libm::exp) gets a single deterministic, cross-platform-identical exponential. The whole pricing core routes through this one wrapper so f64 results are byte-reproducible regardless of host C library.

Session::drive_tick conflates per-subscription: for each active subscription it drains the ring (all try_recv in a tight loop) and keeps only the most recent market tick, then calls drive_one_update at most once. Lagged subscriptions skip pricing and receive a lag-notification instead. A closed outbound channel causes the entire drive to return false (connection gone).

ClientError::fmt provides distinct, human-readable Display messages for every error variant: Transport wraps the underlying transport error; Status formats the gRPC status code and message; MissingField names the absent proto field; Wire wraps the wire-decode error; StreamClosed identifies an unexpected RFS stream termination; Reconnected explains that a blue-green cutover interrupted an in-flight click-to-trade and instructs the user to re-click; InvalidEndpoint formats the bad URI. No variant produces an empty or generic message.

PersistStore.save_commit_index is strictly monotone: it computes advanced = max(stored, new) and never writes a value that is lower than the already-stored commit_index. This upholds the Raft invariant that a committed watermark is never rewound even if the caller passes a stale or None value.

fx_calibration_bits_are_frozen is the golden-pin regression test for the full FX surface calibration pipeline. It runs computed_pins() to derive a 2×5×5 table (2 quote sets × 5 models × 5 strike ratios) of f64 bit-patterns representing implied vols, then asserts exact bit equality against a hardcoded PINS constant. Any change to the calibration algorithm, numerical constants, or model parameters will cause a detectable bit-level drift.

SnapshotStore.load reads the snapshot file from disk and decodes it via Snapshot::decode. A missing file returns Ok(None) (valid absence). A present but corrupt file returns Ok(None) via .ok() (silently discarded). Any other IO error is propagated. Callers must treat None as 'no snapshot' and not as an error.

`inner_linear_solution_matches_cramer_rederivation` verifies the correctness of `inner_solve`'s WLS solution against an independent Cramer's-rule re-derivation (`cramer3`). For the ETH-fixture the test constructs the 3×3 normal-equation matrix and right-hand side by hand (accumulating the same sufficient statistics `sy,sz,syy,syz,szz,sw,syw,szw` independently), solves via `cramer3`, and asserts that the `inner_solve`-produced `(a, c, d)` matches the Cramer solution element-wise to floating-point equality. The `cramer3` helper uses the full 3×3 determinant formula — a fully independent algebra path — making this a cross-check that the WLS accumulator and the `solve3` call in `inner_solve` are consistent.

celnet-rates provides a complete OIS discount-curve stack: (1) Curve — log-linear DF interpolation with piecewise-constant instantaneous forward and constant-forward extrapolation, (2) bootstrap_ois — sequential single-pillar bootstrap to par via Brent root-finding, (3) ois_par_rate / ois_pv / ois_annuity — closed-form OIS pricing identities, (4) usd_sofr_ois_schedule — ACT/360 accrual / ACT/365Fixed pay-time USD SOFR schedule builder, (5) pv01 / ois_risk — analytic PV01 and finite-difference DV01 + key-rate ladder. The crate is pure Rust with no external numerical dependencies; the Curve is Arc-backed (cheap clone, shared snapshot).

deep_wing_solves_exercise_bracketing verifies that strike_from_delta correctly handles extreme far-wing targets — tiny OTM deltas (0.005, 0.01, 0.02) and deep-ITM call deltas (90%–97% of the discount-factor cap) — across four market regimes (low vol, high vol, long T, negative carry) and both unadjusted conventions. It asserts (1) the round-trip delta matches to (1e-9 relative, 1e-11 absolute), (2) OTM call strikes sit above the forward and OTM put strikes below, and (3) deep-ITM call strikes sit below the forward. This exercises the dynamic bracket-expansion logic inside strike_from_delta.

drain_bounded is a loom-harness helper used in exhaustive model-checking of seqlock correctness. For up to `attempts` tries it calls try_recv on a Consumer<(u64,u64)> and asserts two invariants on every delivery: (1) the two halves of each Pair are equal (torn-read detector: `assert_eq!(a, b, "TORN READ")`), and (2) sequence values are strictly increasing (`assert!(a > prev)`). It returns (received, skipped) for the caller to verify conservation. Because it runs inside loom's exhaustive interleaving engine, these assertions cover every possible CPU reordering of the seqlock read protocol.

compare_to_baseline (fleet_slo) checks 8 named latency metrics (federation.direct.p99, federation.federated.p99, publish_snapshot.p99, publish_snapshot.p99.9, conflation.stalled_p99, fan_out.window.p99, fan_out.window.p99.9, federation.added_p99) as relative regressions: ceiling = max(baseline, 0.001) × (1 + tolerance). A degenerate zero baseline is floored at 0.001 to avoid dividing meaning out of near-zero values. Returns a Vec<FleetBreach> (empty = pass); caller bench_gate arm 3 exits non-zero on any breach.

redrive_touch is the touch oracle dispatcher for the selfcheck gate. ONE_TOUCH vectors are re-derived by oracle::one_touch_at_hit_price (independent first-passage quadrature) because the QuantLib touch CSV is the at-expiry deferred-rebate product, not the at-hit product the server prices. All other touch variants (NO_TOUCH, DOUBLE_NO_TOUCH, DOUBLE_ONE_TOUCH) look up the verbatim QuantLib CSV price by matching all market fields and the appropriate barrier fields (barrier for one-sided, lower+upper for double). Failure to find a matching row panics, preventing silent pass on a stale corpus.
