`apply_shock` produces a copy of `WireMarketContext` with one market factor shifted by `step`: Spot → `m.spot = adjust(spot)`, Vol → `m.vol = adjust(vol)`, RateDom → `m.with_r_dom(adjust(r_dom()))`, RateFor → `m.with_r_for(adjust(r_for()))`. The Time axis is a no-op in `apply_shock` — theta roll is handled by the calling scenario loop's expiry roll instead. `adjust(x)` is `x*(1+step)` for relative shocks and `x+step` for absolute shocks.

build_json_subscriber constructs a tracing-subscriber JSON formatter with flattened events, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps, env-filter-driven level filtering, and optionally span context and source location — all controlled by LogConfig. init_json_subscriber installs it as the process-global default (returning SubscriberInstallError if already set). AuditRecord.emit writes a structured `tracing::info!` event at LogClass::Security level carrying request_id, idempotency_key, tenant, instrument, op, premium, and sequence fields, coupling the audit trail to the structured log stream.

The unknown_model_id_is_not_found test asserts the ModelRegistry fail-closed contract: querying any model ID that was never registered returns Err(HostError::Model(PluginError::NotFound('model id'))), never Ok(_). An empty registry has no models and a fresh registry starts empty, so no ambient model authority exists at construction.

ois_risk computes parallel DV01 and a key-rate ladder by finite difference: it re-bootstraps the curve once with all quotes bumped +ONE_BP (parallel DV01), then once per quote with only that quote bumped +ONE_BP (key-rate sensitivities), each time computing the PV change relative to the base curve. The key-rate ladder entries sum to the parallel DV01 (verified by test key_rate_ladder_sums_to_parallel_dv01) because the curve interpolation is log-linear (additive in ln-DF space) and each pillar's bump propagates independently.

ReadinessGate::await_drained() uses a notification-before-recheck pattern to avoid lost wakeups: it arms a `Notify::notified()` future BEFORE the second in-flight count check, ensuring any decrement that races with the arm is visible. The function returns `true` if in-flight reaches zero within the deadline, `false` on timeout (with a final count check to avoid a spurious false negative). It never panics.

CAPABILITY — celnet-limits is the risk-limit enforcement crate for the celnet FX-options platform. Its public contract provides: (1) a `LimitTree` keyed by `LimitScope` that stores hard/soft `LimitSpec` caps per Greek/risk metric; (2) `pre_trade_check` for synchronous pre-trade gate logic (Accept/Warn/Reject) across the full 7-level scope hierarchy resolved by `ScopePath::resolve`; (3) `post_trade_check`/`check_scope` for post-trade monitoring and escalation; (4) `NonAdditiveExposure` for scenario-based VaR/ES/stop-loss metrics that cannot be aggregated additively. A new limit type plugs in by adding a `LimitMetric` variant and a corresponding arm in `exposure_of`.

QuoteEdge::request_quote enforces request-matched idempotency: an existing key is returned verbatim only if the stored instrument+conventions match; a key reused for a different payload returns idempotency_conflict (invalid_argument). A double-check-under-write-lock pattern prevents a concurrent first-quote race from escaping. Distributed mode forwards the request to the pair-owning backend and records quote_id → replica so subsequent accept/reject route home.

numeraire_pillar_vega groups leaves by pillar (preserving first-seen order via linear scan), converts each group to Numeraire via Numeraire::from_leaves, and returns each pillar's vega_numeraire. A missing or unconvertible premium-currency rate surfaces as Status::failed_precondition via convert::numeraire_status.

The capability_denial_unknown_import_fails_to_load test asserts the host's zero-ambient-authority guarantee: a guest module that imports any function outside the GRANTED_IMPORTS set is rejected at load time with HostError::CapabilityDenied, and the payload must name both the forbidden module ('forbidden_host') and the function ('now'). No further execution occurs — an unknown import never silently resolves.

InflightLimiter::try_admit(replica) enforces a per-replica in-flight cap using a lock-free CAS loop on an AtomicU32 counter indexed by replica slot. If the current counter >= cap the request is shed immediately (Admission::Shed{replica, cap}); otherwise it atomically increments and returns Admission::Admitted(Permit). Permit::drop() decrements the counter with saturating_sub(1) via a CAS loop, preventing counter underflow on double-release. An unknown replica id fails closed (returns Shed with cap=0). The cap is never exceeded under concurrent admits.

`StrikeQuoteSlice::new(quotes)` enforces four preconditions at construction time (panics on violation): (1) `quotes.len() >= MIN_STRIKE_QUOTES`; (2) every strike is finite and positive; (3) every vol is finite and positive; (4) strikes are strictly ascending (checked via `windows(2).all(|w| w[0].strike < w[1].strike)`). After construction the slice is immutable; the quotes field is accessible via `.quotes()`. These guards mean any `StrikeQuoteSlice` accepted by `fit_strike_slice` carries a valid, sorted, strictly-positive input set — the solver never needs to handle degenerate orderings.

When all CAP currency slots of a CurrencyExposure are occupied by distinct currencies, adding a new distinct currency returns false and leaves the map unchanged — overflow is reported, never silent. However, netting into an already-occupied currency (calling add with an existing ccy) still succeeds (returns true) and the stored amount increases correctly, even after the array has reached capacity. This invariant is verified by exhaustive fill of CAP synthetic currencies followed by an overflow attempt and a successful net-in check.

`authorize` is the primitive entitlement gate: given `AccessMode`, an optional `EntitlementPrincipal`, a resource name, and a correlation id, it returns `Ok(())` if the principal is present and well-formed, or if mode is `Permissive` and principal is absent. It returns `Err(Status::unauthenticated)` if mode is `Enforce` and principal is absent (`PrincipalAbsent`), and `Err(status)` for a malformed principal. Every decision is emitted as an `AccessAudit` record regardless of outcome.

`StrikeSliceContext` is the asset-class-blind per-tenor context for the strike-axis calibrator. It holds `(spot: f64, carry: Carry, t: f64)` where `Carry` may be `FxRates`, `CostOfCarry`, or any other variant — the seam is intentionally agnostic (doc: 'any Carry is accepted — the seam is asset-class-blind'). `forward()` computes `spot · carry.forward_factor(t)` (pure, libm-backed). `total_variance(vol)` computes `vol² · t` (pure). The `context_forward_is_carry_seam_bits` test asserts bit-identity between `StrikeSliceContext::forward()` and the equivalent `MarketContext::forward()` computation, establishing that the strike front-end and the FX delta front-end share the same carry-seam forward price.

The gpu_gate binary is the relative regression gate: it loads a committed JSON baseline (default path `benches/gpu_baseline.json`), re-measures with the same CI-sized sweep (`GpuLoadConfig::ci()`), calls `compare_to_baseline` with a configurable tolerance (default expressed in the source constant `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE`), and exits 0 iff `breaches.is_empty()`, else exits 1 and prints each breached metric with its measured vs. bound values. It never claims absolute GPU throughput — the header explicitly labels the run as a ratio/relative-regression gate.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-proto is the single, unversioned wire contract for the entire Celnet platform (ADR-0007: one clean current contract, no schema_version, no N/N-1 negotiation). It exposes five logical message families — vocabulary (enums + value messages mirroring celnet_types one-to-one), instrument (a unified Instrument oneof covering vanilla, Strategy, SingleBarrier/DoubleBarrier/WindowBarrier, Digital, Touch, VarianceSwap, VolatilitySwap, AsianOption, ForwardStart, Cliquet, Quanto, Tarf, Pivot, Accumulator, Lookback, AmericanOption, BasketOption, PerpetualOption, ListedFutureOption), quote (RFQ lifecycle: QuoteRequest → Quote → QuoteAccept/QuoteReject → Execution), stream (multiplexed bidirectional RFS via StreamService::StreamSession carrying ClientStreamMessage/ServerStreamMessage), and surface (GetSmile/MarkSurface/Scenario workflows). Seven gRPC services are generated: PricingService, QuoteService, StreamService, RiskService, SurfaceService, FixAdminService, AuthService. All message types implement prost::Message; build.rs uses protox (pure-Rust compiler, no system protoc) + tonic-build with skip_protoc_run() for hermetic, reproducible code generation. New arms plug in by evolving celnet.proto and updating every dependent in the same change — zero mixed-version windows.

The fleet_slo binary entry point enforces a hard outer wall-clock deadline over the full measurement: it wraps the async `measure` call in `tokio::time::timeout(config.wall_clock_cap + 30 s, …)`, converting a timeout into a descriptive error rather than a hang. It selects a lighter `FleetSloConfig::ci()` workload when `--ci` is passed (matching the committed baseline), and optionally writes the JSON report to a path argument for baseline refresh.

The RFS click-trade contract enforces a strict last-look window: a `Subscription::execute` call on a line whose token has aged past the server's validity window (currently 1 second for RFS ticks) always resolves to `ExecuteOutcome::Rejected`, never `ExecuteOutcome::Booked`. The server checks token freshness and retires consumed tokens — a stale or double-click can never book. Source: `stale_click_token_is_rejected_not_booked` advances the manual clock by 5 s past the token mint, then asserts the `ExecuteOutcome` is `Rejected {..}`.

ADR-0007 (one clean unversioned contract — engine hot-upgrade handoff, ENCODE side; the inverse of dec_cut). `enc_cut(v: Cut) -> u8` is the pure, total encoder of the expiry-Cut discriminant into the single handoff byte image: NewYork1000->0, Tokyo1500->1, with no wildcard arm, so adding a Cut variant is a compile-time break rather than a silent mis-encode. It reads only its `Cut` argument and writes nothing (pure: no side effects, no allocation). Because there is exactly ONE current contract (guardrail 9: no schema_version, no N/N-1 negotiation), enc_cut/dec_cut are a fixed mutually-inverse codec pair consumed by serialize_state/restore_state — a hot-upgrade deploys a single uniform version with no mixed-version window, so the byte mapping needs no version tag. This is the decision/trade-off: a tagless 1-byte discriminant (cheapest, deterministic) is sound precisely because the unversioned-contract rule removes any back-compat obligation.

Initiator::request_and_lift is the async FIX RFQ client protocol driver: over an AsyncRead+AsyncWrite stream it (1) sends a Logon and awaits the mirror Logon before proceeding; (2) sends the caller-supplied QuoteRequest via Session::send_app; (3) on receipt of a Quote, records bid/offer/quote_id into InitiatorResult; under LiftOffer/HitBid policy it immediately sends a NewOrderSingle; (4) on receipt of ExecutionReport while awaiting_exec, records fill result and exits. LiftPolicy::Observe exits after the quote without sending an order. All outbound frames are sequence-stamped by the underlying Session.

recover(path) -> Result<(MarketState, BookState), RecoveryError> is the crash-recovery entry point: it opens the on-disk journal at `path`, replays all events via replay_into_state() (which dispatches each decoded payload to BookState::push for BookLine events or records the last MarkState), and returns the final (MarketState, BookState) pair. Recovery fails with RecoveryError::NoMarkedState if the journal contains no MarkState record (nothing to price against). DurableBook::mark(&mut self, market: MarketState) appends an encoded MarkState record to the journal; on replay the last mark seen wins (last_mark_wins test: two marks at spot=1.10 and 1.25, recover returns spot=1.25 bit-identical).

price run resolves the strike from a StrikeSpec (Outright: identity; Delta: solves for the strike matching the target delta under the given convention; Atm: selects the ATM convention strike), then computes the full Greek vector and convention delta in one consistent call, returning a PriceResult that bundles strike, greeks, convention_delta, and delta_convention. All three strike-resolution paths use the same market.inputs(strike) template.

A live click within the validity window produces `ExecuteOutcome::Booked` at exactly the stamped token premium — no re-pricing occurs between the client click and the booking. Specifically, `booked.traded_premium == line.price.offer` (for a BUY/lift) to the bit. The streamed mid is bounded by the GK price evaluated at `spot ± STREAM_BUMP` (0.05%), proving the line carries real Garman-Kohlhagen numbers, not a stub. Source: `taker_click_trades_a_streamed_line_within_the_window`.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-gpu is the wgpu-backed GPU/CPU Monte Carlo pricing substrate. Its public contract is: (1) PathSpec::gbm(spot,vol,t,r_dom,r_for,paths,steps,seed) constructs a GBM path spec with drift = r_dom − r_for; (2) GpuBackend::price_vanilla(&spec, &payoff) dispatches one workgroup-256 compute pass per path, reads back two f32 partials (sum, sum_sq) per workgroup via a bounded-poll GPU_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, widens to f64 via pairwise_sum, and returns a Reduction (price = discount * sum/paths, variance); (3) ScenarioPricer prices a full spot×vol Cartesian ScenarioAxes grid in a single dispatch (workgroups = x_blocks × total_nodes) using common random numbers; (4) PathwiseGreeksPricer::estimate returns a GreeksEstimate with five simultaneous estimators (call_price, pathwise_delta, pathwise_vega, digital_price, lr_digital_delta); (5) GpuBackend::gpu_context() returns None when no wgpu adapter is available, triggering automatic transparent CPU fallback. New pricing arms plug in by constructing a PathSpec and calling the relevant Pricer — the GPU dispatch path is not modified.
merge_vega_ladder accumulates vega-ladder buckets by pillar key: matching pillar sums vega, absent pillar is appended. The operation is additive and preserves first-seen pillar order.

decode_strategy(frame, leg_tenor) decodes a FIX 4.4 NewOrderMultileg/QuoteRequest body into a StrategyPackage: it reads NoLegs(555) to learn the leg count, then walks every field in the frame treating LegSymbol(600) as a leg-group delimiter (FIX repeating-group convention without a dedicated group parser). Each LegBuilder accumulates strike, put/call, ratio, side, and other leg fields; build() calls leg_tenor(i) to resolve the tenor. Rejects if declared count ≠ actual legs built, or any leg has an invalid field. The leg_tenor callback is the caller's hook for resolving tenors from out-of-band context (e.g. the QuoteRequestView tenor fields).

SurfaceEdge::mark_surface calibrates each broker-quote set to a smile, assigns a single fresh version number for the entire mark batch, and deposits every tenor slice under that version in the surface_book. In distributed mode it routes to the pair-owning backend so the marked surface is visible to later Price calls that resolve to the same shard. At least one broker quote is required; an empty set is refused.

Journal::compact performs a crash-safe log replacement via a 5-step atomic protocol: (1) materialize residual records (sequence > watermark) from the live log; (2) build the fresh image in memory as frame_snapshot + residual data records; (3) write the image to a sibling `.tmp` file and fsync it; (4) atomically POSIX-rename the tmp over the live path then fsync the parent directory to make the rename durable; (5) re-open the now-compacted log to refresh cursor state. A crash after the rename but before the fsync leaves the new file durable on any filesystem that guarantees rename atomicity. A crash before the rename leaves the old log intact (the tmp is removed on next open). The watermark must not exceed `last_sequence()`; compacting an empty log or with an over-claiming watermark returns `JournalError::CorruptInterior`.

BatchPricer::price_batch prices a batch of independent vanilla instruments in parallel on the GPU (or via the CPU oracle narrowed to f32 per element). The output slice has exactly insts.len() f64 values, each equal to f64::from(f32_price). It enforces 1 <= insts.len() <= MAX_BATCH. The CPU fallback uses `cpu_batch_with_as_erf` (the same A&S erf-based Black-Scholes as the shader) so GPU and CPU outputs are f32-grade identical by construction.

NodeCore.apply_committed replays log entries from last_applied+1 through commit_index (inclusive) in index order, applying each decoded BookUpdate to the in-memory state machine (self.applied.apply). It advances last_applied entry-by-entry so that a partial replay on crash is resumable from the correct position. Entries that fail to decode are silently skipped (the BookUpdate::decode error is lost), so the state machine tolerates corrupt payloads without stalling.

lsv_run dispatches exotic specs to the LSV PDE/MC engine with two key contracts: (1) vanilla and single-barrier (non-rebate) are always supported; (2) for knock-in single barriers, KI = vanilla_PDE − KO_PDE (in-out parity is applied in the LSV model, not analytically); (3) window barriers support both PDE (default) and MC (when mc_pairs>0); (4) products without a local-vol formulation (digital, touches, swaps, asian, cliquet, quanto, tarf, pivot, accumulator, lookback, american) return a clear unsupported error string.

start_election implements the two-phase Pre-Vote + Real-Vote protocol: (1) it solicits hypothetical-term pre-votes without mutating durable state; only if pre_grants+1 >= majority does it (2) durably bump the term and self-vote via persist.save, then solicit real votes. A single-node cluster wins immediately on its self-vote without network RPCs. If the term moved during pre-vote the real phase is skipped. All solicitation happens outside the mutex; the mutex is held only for state reads and writes.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-parity is the competitive-parity verification harness: a pure integration-test crate (zero public pricing surface, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) whose 19 numbered rows prove the claims in docs/CAPABILITIES-VS-COMPETITION.md are continuously *true*, not merely asserted. Every row exercises the production crates (`celnet-vanilla`, `celnet-exotics`, `celnet-surface`, etc.) through their public APIs exactly as a downstream consumer would. A regression in any row makes `cargo nextest run -p celnet-parity` fail, so the competitive matrix cannot silently rot — new product arms plug in by adding a new row to the map in lib.rs and a corresponding test file under tests/. The crate carries no runtime code; its only output is a pass/fail gate over the production crates.

`gpu_greeks_node_by_node` verifies that the `PathwiseGreeksPricer` (GPU or CPU fallback) produces per-path Greek estimators within a derived tolerance of the CPU reference: for each path the bound is `derived_greeks_bound_for_z(z)` sized by that path's LR estimator z (f32 inverse-normal tail sensitivity); indicator flips at the strike boundary are tolerated only when fewer than 1% of paths are affected.

The `Smile` trait is the decoupling seam between vol-surface construction and all pricing consumers. `Smile::implied_vol(&self, strike, forward, t) -> Vol` returns the arbitrage-aware Black implied vol at a given (strike, forward, t); implementations MUST be arbitrage-aware per the doc contract. `Smile::atm_forward_vol(&self, forward, t) -> Vol` is a provided hot-path convenience that defaults to `self.implied_vol(forward, forward, t)`. `FlatSmile` is the canonical degenerate implementation — it returns `Vol(self.vol)` for every (strike, forward, t) and is used as the test oracle and flat-surface building block throughout the platform. `flat_smile_is_constant` asserts vol is unchanged off-ATM. The engine (`celnet-engine::PricingCore`) and exotic pricers (`celnet-exotics`) depend only on `&dyn Smile` — never on a concrete surface model — so SABR/SVI/VV models are swappable without touching pricing code.

double_barrier_prices_match_quantlib asserts that the celnet double-barrier pricer agrees with the frozen QuantLib oracle to REL=1e-6 and ABS=1e-8 across all 432 grid rows. It additionally asserts both DoubleBarrierKind::KnockOut and KnockIn are present in the oracle, preventing a silently-truncated test grid from hiding missing coverage.

ADR (GPU abstraction = wgpu baseline + CPU-SIMD fallback, CUDA optional) — the wgpu side. `GpuBackend::label(&self)` is a pure accessor (reads only &self, mutates nothing; its only allocation is the returned String): it reports the live wgpu adapter identity — `self.context.backend_name` when a GPU context was acquired — and otherwise falls back to "<cpu label> (fallback)" by delegating to the inner CpuBackend. It is the wgpu-side twin of CpuBackend::label (cl_555e1a46705ef9aa) within the shared `PricingBackend` trait: both implement the same simulate_paths/reduce_payoff/price_vanilla contract behind one interface, with Philox path index i fixed across backends so results reconcile modulo the f32/f64 element type. DECISION/RATIONALE: the GPU strategy is wgpu (Metal/Vulkan/DX12) as the open, permissively-licensed baseline chosen OVER a CubeCL/CUDA-first design — wgpu keeps the runtime dependency set fully open-source and portable across the M4/Metal dev box and Linux/Vulkan CI, with an optional CUDA backend behind the same trait and the f64 CPU path always available as oracle and fallback. label() encodes exactly that runtime selection: a concrete adapter name when wgpu binds a device, the "(fallback)" CPU identity when none is present — so the same single-trait code runs portably whether or not a GPU adapter exists. (Guardrail: no commercial products; open GPU stack with wgpu first-class. Metal lacks f64, so cross-backend agreement is asserted to f32 tolerance, never bit-identity.)

`ranked_weights_match_independent_rendezvous_spec` verifies two properties of `PartitionMap::ranked_into` over 50 key seeds × 6 replicas: (1) every replica's weight equals `oracle_weight(oracle_seed(id), digest)` = `mix64(fold64(mix64(id), digest))` exactly; (2) the output slice is sorted in strictly descending weight order with lowest-id tie-break (`w[0].weight > w[1].weight || (w[0].weight == w[1].weight && w[0].id.0 < w[1].id.0)`). This pins both the weight formula and the sort comparator.

perpetual_rejects_a_call_with_carry_exceeding_discount enforces that when the cost-of-carry b exceeds the discount rate r (specifically r_for=-0.005, r_dom=0.02 → b=r_dom-r_for=0.025>r_dom), a perpetual call CLI invocation returns DispatchError::Invalid with the exact message "a perpetual call with carry exceeding the discount rate has no finite value". The same market inputs for a put succeed and produce output containing "perpetual put" and "price".

resolved_convention_strike_delta_round_trip verifies that for seven major FX pairs (EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, NZDUSD) × three tenors (3M, 1Y, 2Y), the market-convention delta and strike solver round-trip: strike_from_delta using the pair's resolved DeltaConvention followed by convention_delta must recover the original target to (1e-7 relative, 1e-9 absolute) for call deltas {0.25, 0.10} and put deltas {−0.25, −0.10}. This ensures the celnet-conventions resolution and the solver are jointly consistent.

PositionStore::upsert() records or updates a booked vanilla position (fact) keyed by position_id. If a fact with the same position_id already exists it is replaced in-place (update semantics, not append); otherwise it is appended. The u32 handle space is range-checked and returns `invalid_argument` if exceeded. The `exotic` field in the stored FactMeasure is always `None` for the vanilla path — exotic legs must use `upsert_exotic`.

PricingCore::run() is the engine's main loop: it spins on drain() (budgeted batch pop from the rtrb request ring) until the AtomicBool `stop` is observed Relaxed-true, then performs a final quiesce loop calling drain() until empty (bounded by ring capacity), ensuring every request enqueued before stop was set is priced and pushed to the response ring before returning. The loop calls std::hint::spin_loop() on idle (zero-priced drain) to hint the CPU without parking — preserving the sub-microsecond re-observation of `stop`.

price_window_barrier_lsv prices a window barrier option under the LSV model with two configurable engines: when mc_pairs > 0 it uses Monte-Carlo (LsvModel::price_window_barrier_mc) for the headline price and PDE Greeks via lsv_greeks, populating std_error; when mc_pairs == 0 it uses the ADI PDE engine (reprice) for the headline and lsv_greeks for Greeks, with std_error = None. The window constraint 0 ≤ window_start < window_end ≤ expiry_years is validated before pricing; an out-of-range BarrierSide tag or non-finite/non-positive barrier value is rejected as a domain error.

`arb_report` produces a static arbitrage health report for a calibrated smile over a symmetric 9-point strike grid `forward * (0.80 + 0.05*(i-1))` with bump `h = forward * 0.01`. Butterfly-arbitrage-free is declared when `min_density >= -1e-6` AND `min_butterfly >= -1e-6`; calendar-arbitrage-free when `max_vertical_increase <= 1e-6`. The report always carries a typed `smile_model` field (the authoritative provenance enum) alongside the human-readable note string.

relay_session routes a distributed stream session to the pair-owning backend by buffering all inbound messages until the first pair-bearing one, resolving the owner via fleet.owner_of_pair, then opening one upstream StreamSession. Buffered messages are replayed in order before live forwarding begins. The pump task drives client→backend; this task drives backend→client. The session cannot be opened until the pair is known — an inbound stream that closes before any subscription ends cleanly.

american_fd_greeks_byte_identical pins all 14 Greeks of the FX American put pricer (space_steps=300, time_steps=150) to exact IEEE-754 bit patterns: price, delta_spot, delta_forward, gamma, vega, theta, vanna, volga, charm, speed, zomma, color, rho_dom, rho_for. For FX inputs the rate sensitivities must be tagged RateSensitivities::Fx; any other tag is a hard failure. This ensures cross-platform and cross-compiler reproducibility of the finite-difference American solver.

Journal::open provides crash-safe recovery: it scans the file front-to-back (sync-word, CRC, strict sequence monotonicity); detects a torn tail (short sync-word read, wrong sync word bytes, or body-short CRC-position) and heals it by truncating the file to `scan.good_end_offset` followed by `sync_data()`; then calls `sync_parent_dir` once to make the directory entry durable (covering first-create and any truncation). Interior corruption — an intact sync word with a complete body whose CRC fails, or a non-monotonic sequence on a CRC-valid record — is surfaced as `JournalError::CorruptInterior` rather than silently healed. After recovery the append cursor is positioned at `good_end_offset` and `next_sequence` is seeded from the scan result.

handle_append_entries implements the five-step Raft §5.3 follower protocol: (1) reject if leader term < current term; (2) adopt a higher term and revert to Follower; (3) reject on log-matching failure (matches_prev); (4) idempotently reconcile entries via Log::reconcile (skip identical prefix, truncate conflicting tail, append new tail); (5) advance commit_index to min(leader_commit, last_log_index) and durably persist the watermark. Every reply carries the follower's current term so a stale leader observing a higher term can step down.

request_vote_grants_at_an_equal_term_when_unvoted: the stale-term guard for RequestVote is a strict less-than (`term < my_term`), NOT less-than-or-equal — an equal-term candidate that is unvoted and has an up-to-date log is granted. The `< with <=` mutant (line 1126) would wrongly treat the equal-term candidate as stale; this test kills it. The vote is durably recorded after the grant.

tick_loop is the Raft timer driver: when the node is Leader it calls replicate_round then sleeps for exactly one heartbeat interval (via wait_or_wake); when Follower or Candidate it checks whether now >= election_deadline and calls start_election if so, otherwise sleeps for min(remaining, heartbeat). The stop flag is checked on every iteration under Acquire ordering, so the loop terminates within one heartbeat of shutdown.

The surface workflow encodes three request-response pairs: (1) GetSmileRequest (pair + tenor_years + conventions) → Smile (SmilePoint vector on delta axis + BrokerQuoteSet with ATM/RR/BF at 25Δ and optionally 10Δ + ArbReport with butterfly_arbitrage_free, calendar_arbitrage_free, worst_density, SmileModel tag); (2) MarkSurfaceRequest (pair + Vec<BrokerQuoteSet> + conventions + optional SmileModel) → MarkSurfaceResponse (surface_version + Vec<Smile> + epoch_nanos); (3) ScenarioRequest (Instrument + base_market + multi-axis ShockAxis grid with Factor enum: Spot/Vol/Time/RateDom/RateFor, each axis carrying relative bool + steps Vec<f64>, plus optional RiskBucketRequest for VegaBucket/CrossGamma/theta-roll decomposition) → ScenarioResponse (ScenarioPoint vector + optional BucketedRisk).

mc_double_ko is a test-only MC oracle for double-knock-out pricing that applies the Broadie-Glasserman-Kou continuity correction: both corridor walls are shifted inward by `β·σ√dt` (β ≈ 0.5826, the negated Riemann-ζ(½)/√(2π) constant) before path simulation, reducing the discrete-monitoring over-survival bias to O(1/√steps). The generator is a splitmix64 hash → Box-Muller; paths are walk-and-discard with log-space boundary checks.

The wire_load binary entry point enforces a hard outer wall-clock deadline: it spawns the live edge via `start_ready_edge()`, runs `run_load` against it, shuts down the edge with a 5 s grace period, and wraps the entire async block in `tokio::time::timeout(config.wall_clock_cap + 30 s, …)`, guaranteeing the process always terminates even if the edge is unresponsive. CI selects `LoadConfig::default()` (the lighter gate-sized workload); non-CI selects `LoadConfig::published_proof()`.

WasmModel::load enforces a two-phase capability gate before any guest code runs: (1) it iterates module.imports() and returns HostError::CapabilityDenied for any import not in GRANTED_IMPORTS, naming the offending "module::name" precisely; (2) it seeds the wasmi Store with the per-call FuelBudget BEFORE instantiate_and_start so that any module (start) function is fuel-bounded (an infinite start traps as FuelExhausted, not a hang). Each subsequent price/price_and_greeks call refuels back to the full budget via WasmModel::refuel, so start-time consumption does not eat into a later call's SLA.

GpuBatchReport::print_summary prints the GPU batch harness results with an honest headless/GPU split: when `is_gpu` is false it labels the run as a CPU fallback and states the gpu/cpu ratio is expected to be ~1.0; when `is_gpu` is true it labels the throughput as a ratio/relative-regression signal, not an absolute throughput claim. The summary includes per-batch-size throughput (kpaths/s for GPU and CPU oracle), the gpu/cpu ratio, and dispatch p50/p99/p999 in microseconds.

`SettlementCentre::is_holiday(date)` is the exhaustive holiday-dispatch switch for all 12 supported settlement centres: UnitedStates, Target2, UnitedKingdom, Japan, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, NewZealand, Mexico, SouthAfrica, Norway, Sweden. Each arm delegates to a dedicated per-jurisdiction function (e.g. `is_japan_holiday` handles the full Japan rule-set including citizens' holidays, equinox days, and transfer holidays). Adding a new currency's settlement centre requires adding a new `CentreId` variant and a new arm here — the exhaustive match makes omission a compile error.

Fleet::reachable_serving() enforces a fail-closed coverage guarantee: every replica declared `Up` must have a connected backend channel, and every replica declared `Down` must have a declared hot standby that is itself `Up` and a connected backend. If any replica is uncovered (Down with no reachable standby), the call returns `Status::unavailable` rather than serving a partial aggregate. Only after full coverage is confirmed does it return the set of Up, connected backends for fan-out.

measured_throughput_above_floor verifies that the lock-free seqlock publish hot path does not regress catastrophically. It measures the best raw publish rate across 8 bursts of 2,000,000 items each (with one draining reader, making it a real broadcast), then asserts raw_per_sec > 1e6/s. The floor is intentionally set as a catastrophic-regression bound only: an accidental lock, alloc, or syscall would drop throughput by 1–2 orders of magnitude (to ~1e4–1e5/s) and trip this floor, while mere scheduling contention from parallel test execution cannot. The actual uncontended rate (tens of millions/s) is reported via println but not gated.

calibrate_pillar solves for the smile-strangle volatility (σ_ss) that makes the model broker-strangle price equal the market broker-strangle price to tolerance PRICE_REL_TOL * |target|. It enforces a positivity floor ss_floor = 0.5*|RR| − σ_ATM and rejects any quote whose reprice root lies below that floor as CalibrationError::DegenerateQuote, ensuring that every Ok(CalibratedPillar) has strictly positive put and call wing vols. A pathological butterfly that drives δ-inversion surfaces as CalibrationError::StrikeInversion. Non-convergence within MAX_ITERS bisection steps returns CalibrationError::NoConvergence. The bracket collapses only if the residual at the midpoint is genuinely within tolerance — the bracket cannot shrink to a passing result for a degenerate quote.

decode_option decodes a FIX frame into an OptionDescriptor and enforces four dialect invariants: (1) tag-460 (Product), if present, must be b"4" (CURRENCY); (2) tag-167 (SecurityType) must be FXVO or FXNO; (3) tag-947 strike currency, if present, must equal the pair's quote currency, defaulting to it when absent; (4) the decoded settlement style must agree with the FX-convention-resolved settlement for the pair/tenor — a mismatch returns DialectError::SettlementMismatch. Strike must be strictly positive.

One `StreamSession` can multiplex many concurrent `Subscription`s with distinct subscription IDs — four subscriptions (one risk-reversal + three vanilla calls) opened over a single session each receive a strictly-sequenced, independent stream with no gap surfaced. Subscription IDs are guaranteed unique across all concurrent subs on the same session. Source: `market_maker_streams_many_instruments_over_one_session`.

PositionStore::upsert_exotic() records or updates a booked exotic leg. Unlike `upsert`, the stored FactMeasure carries the full `ExoticLeg` in the `exotic: Some(leg)` field (the real Greek set and additive roll-up carrier), with the vanilla position used only for vega-pillar bucketing metadata (never priced through the vanilla path). The same in-place-replace-or-append semantics and u32 handle-space guard apply.

resolved_atm_strike_is_consistent verifies that atm_strike_from_inputs produces a geometrically correct ATM strike for each pair's resolved AtmConvention. For AtmForward, K_ATM = F to 1e-12. For DeltaNeutralStraddle, the call + put delta (in the pair's convention) sums to 0 to 1e-9 absolute, and the sign of K_ATM relative to F matches premium-adjustment: K_ATM < F for premium-adjusted conventions, K_ATM > F for unadjusted.

EquityLeaf::lower produces a leaf-level EquityInputs whose carry() value equals the generic CarryInputs.carry b field (Carry::CostOfCarry), and the r field is forwarded exactly. The downstream AssetPricer::price_greeks dispatch via EquityLeaf is bit-for-bit identical to calling celnet_equity_vanilla::greeks directly on the lowered inputs: price, delta_spot, and both RateSensitivities::Carry components (discount_rho, carry_rho) match to the bit. Equity positions always yield the RateSensitivities::Carry variant, never any other.

adversarial_journal_bytes is a proptest strategy that generates three classes of adversarial byte sequences for fuzzing Journal::open: (1) pure random bytes (0..4096); (2) structurally valid journal images with optional single-byte flip and/or truncation — reaching torn-tail and intact-sync-bad-CRC corners that pure noise rarely hits; (3) snapshot-shaped buffers starting with the exact SYNC_WORD (b"CLNJRNL\0" LE) + SNAPSHOT_MARKER (u32::MAX) + a 7 watermark + an attacker-controlled inner_len (any u32) + a random tail, to specifically exercise the read_snapshot inner-length-bound path. Journal::open must not panic or produce UB on any of these inputs.

resolve_caller resolves a caller from a session token and/or an asserted principal. A missing or blank token produces an anonymous ResolvedCaller (user=None). A non-blank token is validated against SessionRegistry; an invalid or expired token returns Status::unauthenticated — the error message explicitly names re-authentication via AuthService.Login.

invariants_hold_on_known_good_markets is the testkit's comprehensive no-arbitrage gate: for every market in reference_markets() it asserts put-call parity, price within bounds, both intrinsic lower bounds, strike convexity (both option types, bump = 5% of strike), spot monotonicity, vol monotonicity, and strike monotonicity. Maturity monotonicity is checked conditionally — only for the option type in its correct carry regime (Call when r_dom >= r_for, Put when r_for >= r_dom). This conditional gate prevents false failures on out-of-regime inputs while still exercising the constraint where it is theoretically valid.

atm_strike_matches_convention_closed_form verifies that MarketContext::atm_strike(vol) matches the closed-form convention formula: AtmForward → K=F; DeltaNeutralStraddle with spot/forward-unadjusted delta → K=F*exp(+0.5σ²t); DeltaNeutralStraddle with premium-adjusted delta → K=F*exp(−0.5σ²t). It also asserts atm_total_variance = σ²t and atm_std_dev = σ√t to 1e-15 tolerance.

premium_adjusted_call_reachability_boundary_is_exact verifies the precise ±1e-12 reachability margin logic for premium-adjusted call conventions (both SpotPremiumAdjusted and ForwardPremiumAdjusted). A target at dmax − 5e-13 (just inside the margin) must solve and round-trip to (1e-7 relative, 1e-9 absolute); the solved strike must satisfy K ≥ K_max (confirming OTM-branch selection). A target at dmax + 1e-6 (outside the margin) must return Err(DeltaSolveError::Unreachable). This test is structurally designed to catch a sign-flip mutant on the margin comparison at line 162:37.

asian_payoff (WGSL, path.wgsl) prices an Asian (arithmetic-average) option on the GPU using Brownian-bridge reconstruction: it draws m Sobol coordinates (dimension j=0..m), maps each to a standard normal z[j] via inv_norm_cdf, then reconstructs the Brownian path via W(t_l) = sum_k bridge_a[l*m+k]*z[k] (a linear map uploaded from celnet-qmc's bridge matrix A). The GBM log-price at monitoring date t_l is ln_spot + (drift − 0.5σ²)t_l + σ·W(t_l). The arithmetic average of exp(ln_S) over l=0..m is then used in the payoff max(sign*(avg−strike), 0). The bridge matrix A is the Brownian-bridge factor that concentrates low-discrepancy variation in early (high-importance) Sobol dimensions.

The real_socket_sink_bounded_and_lossless_in_information test verifies three joint invariants of the EgressGovernor over a real loopback TCP socket under a 2000-update, 16-key, 1µs-per-tick workload: (1) Memory bound — the pending map never exceeds capacity (32 keys) at any point; (2) Newest-wins delivery — for every key delivered to the sink, the received sequence number equals the highest sequence produced for that key (confirming that conflation discards stale, not fresh, updates); (3) Full accounting — offered == delivered + dropped_total with dropped_total > 0, proving the governor is genuinely lossy (conflation occurred) and that no update is silently lost outside the two buckets.

Multi-dealer last-look: `MultiDealerHandle::accept_dealer` for a panel row whose `valid_until_nanos` has passed returns `ClientError::Status(DeadlineExceeded)`. The SDK-visible `DealerPanelRow::last_look_remaining(now_nanos)` reflects this: `Some(_)` before the window and `None` after. The clock advance (6 s) ages every row simultaneously. Source: `accept_after_panel_row_last_look_is_refused`.

Session::handle_subscribe validates instrument, conventions, and baseline market before opening a price-tick ring subscription. A subscription without a resolvable FX pair is refused as invalid_argument rather than opened as a line that can never tick. The opening snapshot is sent with a blocking `await` so the baseline is never dropped; only after the send succeeds is the Subscription inserted into self.subs.

scenario_grid_gpu_unbatched is a Criterion/Divan micro-benchmark that exercises the GPU backend across a full risk scenario grid: it prices every combination of (spot multiplier × vol bump × portfolio position) unbatched through `GpuBackend::price_vanilla`, accumulating into a `black_box` sink to prevent dead-code elimination. Inputs are constructed via `celnet_core::carry::fx_vanilla_inputs` from the position's tagged inputs, so the bench exercises the real FX two-rate carry path. The `ItemsCount` counter is set to `n_spot * n_vol` nodes so Divan reports per-grid-node throughput.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-types is the single shared-types crate for the entire celnet platform. Its public contract is: (1) the cross-asset instrument taxonomy (Underlying enum covering Fx/Metal/Equity/Commodity/DigitalAsset variants); (2) the canonical vanilla-option input record VanillaInputs (spot, strike, vol, t, r_dom, r_for) with libm-backed discount-factor and forward helpers; (3) the unified Carry enum (FxRates|CostOfCarry) with carry_rate/forward_factor/discount_df accessors that every analytics leaf consumes; (4) the full Greeks struct (14 first/second/third-order sensitivities); (5) the RateSensitivities enum (Fx rho_dom/rho_for | generalized discount_rho/carry_rho); (6) OptionType (Call/Put) with sign/flip; (7) PremiumStyle (PA/PU) with is_premium_adjusted/flip_orientation; (8) FixingSource enum (6 EM fixings with canonical code() strings). New analytics arms plug into the platform by consuming these types; the crate itself has zero pricing logic.

logon_heartbeat_gap_resend_gapfill_over_socket is the end-to-end FIX session protocol integration test. It verifies over a real loopback TCP socket: (1) logon mirror brings both sides to Active; (2) a deliberate sequence gap (seq 3 never sent, seq 4 sent) triggers a ResendRequest(begin=3) from the acceptor; (3) a manual GapFill SequenceReset advancing to seq 5 resolves the gap; (4) the acceptor's expected inbound sequence reaches 6 after recovery. The entire exchange is bounded by a timeout.

`NodeScenarioGrid::reconciles_to_analytic` compares every `(i,j)` node of a Monte Carlo grid against `analytic_pv_grid` reference, returning `Err((i, j, deviation, band))` at the first node where `|MC_pv − analytic_pv| > k × std_err + abs`. On success it returns `Ok((worst_deviation, worst_std_err))`. The acceptance band is linear in `std_err`, allowing the caller to choose coverage factor `k` (e.g., 3σ) plus an absolute floor `abs`.

BroadcastRing::new rounds the requested capacity up to the nearest power of two (minimum 2) via `capacity.next_power_of_two().max(2)`. Inner::new asserts `capacity.is_power_of_two()` and stores `mask = capacity - 1` for branchless slot index computation `idx = seq & mask`. All slots are pre-allocated in a `Box<[Slot<T>]>` with stamps initialized to `UNWRITTEN` (a sentinel that no valid even stamp can equal). The cache-padded `head: CachePadded<AtomicU64>` is initialized to 0 and is the single shared coordination point between producer and all consumers.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-core is the zero-IO, zero-alloc pure-domain foundation layer of the celnet pricing platform. Its public contract is three seams: (1) the `Smile` trait — the abstraction between surface-construction (`celnet-surface`: Vanna-Volga/SABR/SVI) and all consumers that need an implied Black vol at a given strike; (2) the `CarryPricer` trait — the object-safe pricing seam that each asset-class leaf implements to price against `CarryInputs` (containing an `Underlying` + `Carry` tag) with `price(opt, inputs) -> Result<f64, CarryPriceError>` and `price_greeks(opt, inputs) -> Result<CarryGreeks, CarryPriceError>`; (3) the `math` module — deterministic libm-backed transcendental wrappers (`exp`, `ln`, `sqrt`, `norm_cdf`, `norm_pdf`) that guarantee bit-identical f64 results across platforms. The crate is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` with zero runtime dependencies beyond `celnet-types` and `libm`. A new asset-class arm plugs in by implementing `CarryPricer`; a new surface model plugs in by implementing `Smile` — neither requires changes to this crate.

digital_prices_match_quantlib_all_flavours asserts that the celnet digital pricer agrees with the frozen QuantLib oracle to REL=1e-9 and ABS=1e-11 across all 192 grid rows (4 flavours × 48 market scenarios). It also enforces structural completeness: both CashOrNothing and AssetOrNothing settlement styles must be present for both Call and Put option types, guarding against a silently-truncated oracle.

snapshot_interior_crc_failure_is_surfaced verifies the snapshot analogue of the data-record discrimination: a leading snapshot record whose body is complete (snapshot bytes + CRC trailer fully present) but whose CRC fails is classified as CorruptInterior, not healed as a torn tail. The flip target is `SYNC_LEN + 4 + 8 + 4 + 1` (one byte inside the snapshot payload, after SNAPSHOT_MARKER, watermark, and snap_len fields).

Scoped-principal no-leakage guarantee: a `Principal::scoped()` principal with a single `grant(Rule::on(DimensionId::Desk, 1))` prunes facts to exactly those whose `Book → Desk` hierarchy resolves to desk 1. The resulting `entitled_cube` delta sum equals the sum of desk-1 facts only, and is strictly different from the full-firm total (desk-2 magnitude does not leak), verified by `scoped_principal_pruned_before_aggregation_no_leakage`. A `scoped()` principal with no grants admits nothing, verified by `scoped_principal_with_no_grants_admits_nothing`.

install_capabilities registers exactly the five math host functions onto a wasmi Linker under the module name "celnet_math": exp, ln, sqrt, norm_pdf, norm_cdf. Each wrapper applies abi::canonicalize to both the input and the output — NaN is normalized in both directions at the host/guest boundary. is_granted is the pure allowlist predicate that checks a (module, name) pair against the GRANTED_IMPORTS static slice; it is the single enforcement point used both at load-time pre-check and at link-time.

`calendar_for(pair) -> BusinessCalendar` applies the FX convention that cross pairs (neither leg is USD) get a three-centre calendar (base + quote + USD); USD-leg pairs get a two-centre calendar (base + quote only). A date is a business day only when ALL constituent centres are open — the intersection semantics enforced by `BusinessCalendar::is_business_day` (`self.centres().all(|c| !c.is_non_business(date))`). `with_centres` de-duplicates centre IDs inline so repeated entries (e.g. USD appearing twice in a USD-leg pair after the cross guard) never produce duplicate checks.

hot_pricing_under_concurrent_publish_allocates_zero verifies that the zero-allocation guarantee of the hot pricing drain path holds even while a concurrent publisher thread continuously calls StateHandle::publish with new MarketState values. The pricing thread must acquire zero heap memory (ALLOCS before == after) during the 4096-request drain window, regardless of how many publish calls interleave. Additionally, a deterministic reclamation proof shows that a superseded Arc<MarketState> is freed on the reading thread (at least one dealloc) when the reader next validates its cached pointer — confirming reclamation happens on the reader, not the publisher, and is not subject to timing races.

CounterRng uses a (stream, path, step, draw) counter partition so that the 128-bit block counter is [path as u32, path>>32 as u32, step_base, draw]. key0 = seed as u32, key1 = (seed>>32) ^ stream. Each call to refill() produces a fresh 4-word block by invoking block(counter, key0, key1) and increments draw with wrapping_add(1). Consequently: (a) any two CounterRng instances with distinct (seed, stream, path, step) tuples draw from non-overlapping block streams; (b) re-constructing with the same (seed, stream, path, step) reproduces every variate bit-for-bit (no platform or scheduling dependence), which the test same_seed_same_sequence_bit_identical asserts.

touch_table_loads_and_is_well_formed validates the frozen touch oracle: all seven numeric fields (spot, rebate, vol, t, r_dom, r_for, price) must be finite; price must satisfy −ε ≤ price ≤ rebate × df.max(1.0) + ε where df = exp(−r_dom × t), bounding option value by the discounted rebate; single-touch kinds (OneTouch, NoTouch) must carry exactly one barrier and no corridor; double-touch kinds (Dnt, DoubleTouch) must have no single barrier and a valid corridor 0 < L < U; all four kinds must appear in the grid.

TelemetryDrain.drain processes at most `budget` HotSamples per call from the lock-free ring, calling `account` (gap-detection) on each sample's sequence number before forwarding to the sink closure, and returns the count actually drained. The budget bound makes drain safe to call from a time-critical event loop without unbounded latency.

converged_params_are_pinned_benign pins the exact bit-pattern of calibrated parameters for all four fitted SmileModel variants (StochasticVol, Parametric, ParametricSurface, ExtendedSurface) on the 'benign' FX quote fixture. For StochasticVol it asserts bits of alpha, rho, nu, and that forward = context.forward() and t = context.t exactly. For the three parametric variants it asserts bits via BENIGN_SVI/SSVI/ESSVI and additionally asserts sl.forward = context.forward() and sl.t = context.t. This is the determinism regression gate for the calibration pipeline.

closed_form_matches_independent_mc verifies that forward_start_price (closed form) agrees with an independent antithetic Monte Carlo (400,000 antithetic pairs) for 3 market configurations × 3 (t₁, T) pairs × 3 moneyness levels × 2 option types (54 cases). The tolerance is tol = 4·SE + 1e-4 where SE is the MC standard error, providing an honest comparison that accounts for both MC noise and near-zero deep-OTM values.

compaction_keeps_sequences_globally_monotonic_across_appends verifies that multiple compaction cycles interleaved with appends never rewind or reuse sequence numbers across the whole observable history. After compact(4) then appends at seqs 10/11/12, then compact(11), then an append at seq 13, a full reopen-and-replay asserts: (a) the leading Snapshot appears at position 0 and nowhere else; (b) every Data record's sequence is strictly greater than the previous Data record's sequence; (c) next_sequence after reopen is 14.

cost_of_carry implements the ADR-0008 carry guard: it refuses an absent carry arm with PriceError::Domain (no silent fallback to b=r). A Generalized arm produces Carry::CostOfCarry { r, b: g.b }; an Fx two-rate arm derives b = discount_rate − r_for. Both arms produce the same forward S·e^{b·t}.

Log.entry_at_physical reads the journal from disk on every call (no caching), returns the p-th physical record decoded as a LogEntry, or None if the position is beyond the end. A corrupt payload causes ok() to discard the decode error, returning None rather than propagating it.

Producer::subscribe_from_start creates a Consumer with `cursor = 0`, enabling replay of all still-buffered history up to the ring's capacity. Producer::subscribe_from_head creates a Consumer with `cursor = head` (loaded with Acquire), skipping all already-published items and starting from the next publish. Both constructors share the same `Arc<Inner<T>>` reference without any allocation of new ring storage. Consumer::clone is also provided (`in_degree=293`), cloning the Arc reference and copying the current cursor and counters — enabling fan-out to N independent downstream consumers from a single subscription point.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-engine is the hot-path FX-options pricing engine: it exposes PricingCore as the single entry point for pricing vanilla options against a live smile surface, publishes top-of-book results atomically via a seqlock (PriceSnapshot), persists position state through DurableBook/journal (crash-recoverable and bit-identical on replay), and supports lock-free hot market-state reloads via StateHandle (arc-swap). A new pricing arm plugs in by: (1) constructing a PricingCore with an initial MarketState; (2) calling run() with an rtrb SPSC request/response ring; (3) publishing updated MarketState ticks into StateHandle::publish() from a separate thread with no locking; (4) opening a DurableBook for journal-backed crash recovery via recover().

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-risk-cube is the risk-aggregation and regulatory-capital crate. Its public seam is the `Cube` (upsert/group_by), three non-additive VaR/ES lenses (historical full-reprice, sensitivity Taylor, curvature), and the FRTB Sensitivity-Based Method assembler (`assemble_capital`). A new asset arm plugs in by: (1) implementing `CarryPricer` for repricing, (2) calling `Cube::upsert` with `RiskFact` objects, and (3) supplying `SbmParams`/`CurvatureBucket` slices to `assemble_capital`. The additive greeks layer (delta, vega ladder) and the non-additive layer (VaR, ES, curvature CVR) are kept strictly separate — additive fields roll up linearly across all assets; VaR/ES are computed per-node by quantile reduction over a shared `quantile_var_es` kernel used identically by both the historical full-reprice path and the sensitivity Taylor path.

Carry::discount_df(t) is a pure function computing the numeraire discount factor e^{-r*t} via libm::exp(-self.discount_rate() * t). It has no side effects and no state mutation — its output depends only on (self, t). Because discount_rate() reads r_dom verbatim for Carry::FxRates, the FX discount factor produced here is byte-identical to VanillaInputs::df_dom (the FX two-rate form), preserving FX bit-identity across the carry seam (ADR-0008). CarryInputs::discount_df and ExoticInputs::discount_df both delegate to this method.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-linear is the linear-products leaf of the celnet pricing platform: it prices FX outright forwards, FX swaps (two-legged near+far), and non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against the shared carry seam. Its public contract is three modules — forward (outright PV + greeks), swap (two-leg PV + swap points), ndf (cash-settled NDF via Ndf struct + FixingSource) — all built over the single validated input type LinearInputs::outright / LinearInputs::with_far. A new instrument arm plugs in by constructing a LinearInputs (validated via LinearInputs::validate: positive notional, non-negative settle times) with the appropriate Underlying + Carry tags, then calling pv / greeks (forward), swap::pv / swap_points (swap), or Ndf::new + Ndf::pv (NDF). The crate has no I/O, no allocation in its hot path, and no state beyond the immutable inputs struct.

fx_carry_context_is_byte_identical_to_two_rate_form asserts that MarketContext::new with Carry::FxRates{r_dom, r_for} produces byte-for-byte identical forward() and template(strike, vol) values as the VanillaInputs two-rate constructor across 4×4×4 combinations of (r_dom, r_for, t). This pins the forward = spot*exp((r_dom − r_for)*t) computation as the canonical link between the surface context and the vanilla pricing layer.

pivot_matches_independent_oracle cross-validates the production Pivot-TRA pricer (pivot_tra_price_cv) against an independently derived oracle (oracle_price) using separate random streams and 1,500,000 oracle paths. The tolerance is 4·(prod.std_error + ose) + 1e-9, providing a statistically robust agreement gate. Three moments are checked: price, expected redemption fixing index (tolerance 0.05 fixings), and expected overshoot. The oracle independently rederives the two-level piecewise-linear cash-flow rule, documenting a sign correction to the §3.2 indicator literal.

misplaced_snapshot_record_is_surfaced_as_interior_corruption verifies that a CRC-valid snapshot record appearing anywhere other than the first position is treated as interior corruption (not silently swallowed). A forged log of data@0 followed by a forge_snapshot(0, ...) frame must yield Err(CorruptInterior) with a reason containing 'snapshot'.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-conventions is the single authoritative registry for all FX-options market conventions. Its primary public contract is `resolve(pair, tenor) -> ResolvedConvention`: for covered pairs it returns a `ConventionRecord` sourced from a static `PairProfile` (tagged `ResolutionSource::PairProfile`); for any unknown pair it falls back to a region-derived default (tagged `ResolutionSource::RegionDefault`). Callers plug into the registry by calling `resolve` or `pair_meta`; the `ResolutionSource` tag lets consumers distinguish authoritative per-pair data from region defaults.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY (celnet-xva): the crate computes the three standard counterparty-risk valuation adjustments — CVA (credit), DVA (debit/own-credit), and FVA (funding) — for a synthetic netting set of vanilla FX options. The pipeline is: (1) ExposureProfile::simulate drives spot under risk-neutral GBM with Sobol low-discrepancy normals, reprices each NettedTrade via celnet_vanilla::price, nets within the set, and reduces across paths to EPE(t_k)/ENE(t_k) profiles; (2) SurvivalCurve (flat or piecewise-constant hazard) supplies survival probabilities S(t) = exp(−Λ(t)); (3) compute_xva aggregates over the time grid to produce XvaResult {cva, dva, fva}. The public seam is (XvaInputs → compute_xva → XvaResult), where XvaInputs borrows an ExposureProfile plus counterparty/own SurvivalCurves and LGDs. The crate is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and explicitly out of scope are collateral/CSA, wrong-way risk, and live credit-curve wiring — those are deploy-gated extensions.

Determinism rule (docs/INTERFACES.md §"Determinism rules baked into the interfaces": transcendentals via rust-lang/libm for bit-identical cross-platform results). `celnet_core::math::ln` is the canonical natural-logarithm transcendental wrapper: it is `pub fn ln(x: f64) -> f64 { libm::log(x) }` — a pure (side-effect-free, no WRITES) total delegation to the correctly-rounded rust-lang/libm `log` routine (note libm::log == ln, not log10). Routing every ln(·) (e.g. log-moneyness ln(F/K) in d1/d2) through this one libm-backed wrapper keeps the f64 CPU-canonical result identical across hosts, never std's platform-dependent ln.

`RollRule::adjust` implements the four standard date-roll conventions as a pure match over `RollRule`: Unadjusted (identity), Following (forward to next business day), Preceding (back to previous), and ModifiedFollowing (forward unless the result crosses a month boundary, in which case fall back to preceding). The ModifiedFollowing branch is: `let fwd = following(cal, date); if fwd.month() != date.month() { preceding(cal, date) } else { fwd }`. This is the canonical roll used by all week/month/year/IMM/BrokenDate tenor arms in `expiry_for_tenor`.

The `strike_axis_oracle.rs` integration suite verifies four independently-grounded properties of the new strike-axis pipeline: (1) `eth_exact_svi_grid_round_trips` — `fit_strike_slice` on an ETH-fixture grid produced by the reference SVI formula recovers all five SVI parameters to ≤1e-4 relative error and reproduces `w(k)` to ≤1e-7 on-grid and off-grid, confirmed against the independent `svi_w_reference` oracle; (2) `fd_density_nonnegative_and_agrees_with_durrleman` — the Breeden–Litzenberger finite-difference density is ≥−1e-7 at 49 strikes and Durrleman's `g(k)` (`is_butterfly_free`) agrees the same slice is butterfly-free; (3) `decreasing_total_variance_pair_is_flagged` — a two-tenor surface where `w₁=0.8²·(7/365)>w₂=0.3²·(28/365)` (calendar arbitrage) is correctly flagged by `arbitrage_report` with `min_calendar_increment < 0` and `is_arbitrage_free(1e-6) == false`; (4) `cross_path_canary_agrees_then_disagrees` — when the same parametric FX smile is sampled onto a strike grid and re-fit via the strike path, total variances agree to ≤1e-7 everywhere; bumping one quote makes the strike fit diverge while the FX path remains bit-frozen (the two calibration paths are independent).

Acceptor::on_new_order implements last-look semantics: a NewOrderSingle/Multileg is filled only if its QuoteID exists in self.live and self.tick <= lq.valid_until_tick. A successful fill removes the QuoteID from self.live (idempotency: a duplicate lift of the same QuoteID is rejected). Fill price is offer_px for BUY (SIDE_BUY) and bid_px for SELL. Both fill and reject paths emit an ExecutionReport.

Cube::group_by partitions facts by any DimensionId (Trader, Book, Desk, Underlying, etc.) in first-seen order, routing each RiskFact to either the vanilla positions slice or the exotic_legs slice based on fact.measure.exotic. accumulate_fact ensures every leaf (vanilla and exotic) contributes to net_greeks and vega_ladder regardless of routing, so additive Greeks roll up correctly across mixed vanilla/exotic nodes. The fx_pair_group_value encodes the Underlying dimension key as a 48-bit big-endian ASCII packing of the 6-character currency code (e.g. EURUSD → 0x455552555344), with metal pairs (XAUUSD) packing through the same projection — group keys are stable u64 values, always < 2^48.

StateHandle::publish(&self, state: MarketState) replaces the engine's live market state lock-free via arc-swap (self.inner.store(Arc::new(state))). StateHandle::load(&self) -> Arc<MarketState> reads it (self.inner.load_full()). PricingCore::price() calls self.reader.load() on every request, so a market-state update published from any thread is immediately visible to the pricing hot path on the next request with no locking and no stale read. The test hot_reload_observed_without_locking confirms: after publish(st2) with a higher spot, the next core.price() returns a higher call price.

Session::handle_modify re-baselines a subscription in place at sequence+1 without creating a new sub: it clears live tokens (clear_live, so prior tradable tokens are retired) but preserves consumed-token records so a replayed Execute is still rejected as AlreadyConsumed. The pair's fan-out ring is re-subscribed before the mutable borrow of the sub to avoid a double-borrow.

gen_double_barrier emits up to 6 knock-out corridor vectors, skipping knock-in rows (only DoubleBarrierKind::KnockOut is selected). The server's primal double-barrier path is KO; this ensures the corpus pinpoints that path. All vectors fix rebate=0.0 and monitoring=CONTINUOUS. Tolerance is rel=1e-5/abs=1e-7, reflecting that the QuantLib reflection-series double-barrier formula converges less tightly than the single-barrier analytic.

Message.encode serialises all seven Raft wire message variants to a compact little-endian byte stream with a one-byte discriminant tag (0=AppendEntries, 1=AppendReply, 2=RequestVote, 3=VoteReply, 4=StatusRequest, 5=Status, 6=InstallSnapshot). For AppendEntries it length-prefixes each entry with a 4-byte u32 payload length. For InstallSnapshot it length-prefixes the snapshot blob with a 4-byte u32. The encoding is the exact inverse of Message::decode.

serve_replay implements a two-phase replay protocol for the vendor-feed gap-resync test harness: it awaits a CTRL_SUBSCRIBE byte, plays back the pre-gap frame sequence, then (if a resync script is present) awaits a CTRL_RESYNC byte before playing the snapshot + recovered-tail sequence. After all scripted frames are exhausted it blocks indefinitely on an idle read until the peer closes, ensuring frames are delivered exactly once and the subscriber's pump does not reconnect and re-replay.

`lookback_discrete_mc` prices floating and fixed lookback options using Brownian-bridge extremum simulation (Beaglehole–Dybvig–Zhou 1997 / Glasserman 2003): for each sub-interval [t_{k−1}, t_k] a uniform U is drawn alongside the normal step, and the segment extremum is `exp(½·(ln_prev+ln_next ± √((ln_next−ln_prev)² − 2σ²dt·ln U)))`. This eliminates the O(1/√n) under-sampling bias of a naive node-max. Floating payoff = S_T − S_min (call) / S_max − S_T (put); fixed payoff = (S_max − K)⁺ / (K − S_min)⁺.

PILLAR (CLAUDE.md guardrails 6 + 11 — the latency budget in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2 is enforced, not aspirational). `CoreReport::budget_breaches` is the pure, deterministic detector that turns a measured hot-core latency profile into the set of budget violations: it reads only `&self` (the measured `latency` p50/p99/p99.9 and the `budget` ceilings), forms the three (metric, measured_ns, ceiling) tuples, and returns a freshly-allocated `Vec<BudgetBreach>` containing exactly those percentiles where measured > ceiling. No `&mut`, no I/O, no shared/global mutation — allocating the returned Vec is not an externally-observable side effect; it has no WRITES edges. Determinism is the load-bearing property: the same measured profile against the same budget always flags the same breaches, so a CI gate cannot non-reproducibly hide a regression past the §1.2 envelope. SELF-INVALIDATING: introducing a write or changing the comparison shifts this anchor and flips the claim stale.

payload_too_large_is_rejected verifies the append size gate: appending a payload of exactly MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN+1 bytes yields Err(JournalError::PayloadTooLarge { len }) with len == MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN+1, and leaves the journal in a clean state such that a subsequent append of b"ok" succeeds and is assigned sequence 0 (nothing was written for the rejected append).

`pivot_engine_matches_code_disjoint_golden_oracle` verifies `pivot_tra_price_cv` against a code-disjoint MC oracle (`oracle::pivot_tra_bank_pv_mc`) across all four combinations of {Call/Put} × {FullGain/CappedGain} and two strike/pivot configurations. Agreement condition: |engine.price − oracle.price| < 4·(engine.std_error + oracle.std_error) + 1e-9, using both engines' own Monte-Carlo standard errors to set the comparison band.

WingDensity::from_params constructs a discretised risk-neutral density for a StochasticVolSmile over a strike grid of CELLS cells spanning [max(F − 16σ√t·F, 1e-6·F), max(F + 16σ√t·F, 3F)]. The raw density is sampled at cell midpoints via risk_neutral_density, clamped to ≥ 0, normalised to unit mass, then rescaled so the discrete mean equals F exactly (martingale correction via λ = F/μ). The invariant mass > 0 is debug-asserted.

celnet-replog is the replicated-log substrate for the celnet platform: it implements a self-contained Raft consensus engine (RaftNode) that replicates a BookState key→f64 price book across a cluster of N nodes. The public seam is: RaftNode::boot/boot_on (start node + background threads), RaftNode::propose (leader-only append of a BookUpdate), RaftNode::wait_for_commit (poll until a proposed index is committed), RaftNode::compact/compact_applied (snapshot + log truncation), RaftNode::applied_state/applied_bits (read the committed applied state). A new consumer arm plugs in by: (1) calling boot_on with a TcpListener, journal path, peer SocketAddrs, cluster_size, and RaftConfig; (2) proposing BookUpdate entries only from the leader (propose returns None if not leader); (3) reading the committed BookState via applied_state after wait_for_commit confirms durability.

Message.decode deserialises all seven Raft wire message variants (tags 0–6) from a length-prefixed byte slice using a Cursor that tracks remaining bytes. An unknown tag returns WireError::Malformed. AppendEntries (tag 0) caps entry pre-allocation at 1024 (`n.min(1024)`) to bound memory use on malformed/hostile frames.

gate_c_leader_failover_elects_new_leader_no_committed_loss: in a 5-node cluster, killing the current leader causes survivors to elect a new leader at a strictly higher term, and the new leader's committed prefix is byte-identical to the killed leader's (zero committed-entry loss). The new leader can immediately accept and commit a fresh proposal, and all four survivors converge to the same to_bits-identical applied BookState.

backstop_close maps a WebSocket capacity error (oversized frame) to a typed WS 1009 close frame and returns None for any other error kind, implementing the protocol requirement that oversized messages generate a 1009 close rather than an opaque disconnect.

lapped_consumer_conflates_with_exact_skip_accounting verifies the single-threaded lapped-consumer contract: when 1000 items are published to an 8-slot ring without any reads, a subsequent drain must (1) converge on the latest item (assert_eq!(*got.last().unwrap(), PRODUCED-1)), (2) satisfy received + skipped == PRODUCED exactly, (3) deliver at most `capacity` items (the live window), and (4) deliver them in strictly ascending order. This is the canonical unit-test for the ring's skip-accounting arithmetic.

RaftNode::boot_on performs snapshot-aware crash recovery in a strict three-phase order (Raft §7): (1) if a durable snapshot exists, seed BookState and watermarks (last_applied, commit_index) from it and adopt its (last_included_index, last_included_term) boundary on the Log so absolute indices over the discarded prefix remain correct; (2) replay only the retained committed tail strictly above the snapshot boundary up to the durable commit watermark; (3) entries above the watermark are NOT applied on boot — the leader re-drives their commit via AppendEntries. The commit watermark is durably persisted (PersistStore), so a restarted node knows exactly which prefix is committed and the applied state is to_bits-identical to a full-log replay.

ADR-0007 (one unversioned contract — engine hot-upgrade handoff, decode side). `restore_state(bytes)` is the single deterministic DECODER of the engine handoff byte image and the exact inverse of `serialize_state`: it is a pure function of its borrowed `&[u8]` (it reads no global/external state and mutates none — the only allocations are the returned BookState::entries Vec and the reconstructed MarketState), so the same bytes always yield the same (MarketState, BookState). It validates the fixed self-describing layout — a leading MAGIC sentinel (BadMagic on mismatch), then market scalars (spot, r_dom, r_for, t), conventions, the three smile benchmark pillars + reference forward/time from which MarketHedgeSmile::new reconstructs an identical smile, then the length-prefixed book — and calls Reader::finish() to reject trailing bytes, never a silent default. DECISION/RATIONALE: there is NO schema_version field and NO N/N-1 negotiation; hot-upgrade carries state across a code swap through this ONE current format with only a MAGIC discriminant. An upgrade deploys a single uniform engine version (old build serializes, new build restores) so there is no mixed-version window — the format evolves in place rather than versioning, consistent with the platform-wide single-unversioned-contract decision and proved exact by roundtrip_restores_identical_state / restored_state_reprices_identically. (Guardrail: no versioned APIs; hot-upgradable single-version estate. Pairs with cl_d9376a70dfdbd751 on serialize_state.)

run_core() is the lock-free pricing thread loop. It upholds a strict ordering guarantee: the control plane (publish/surface/snapshot/exotic/observe commands from `ctrl_rx`) is fully drained BEFORE the hot price ring is processed each iteration. This ensures a caller that awaits a publish acknowledgement and then submits a price request always observes a price computed against the just-published state, with no cross-channel reordering race. The loop terminates on a shutdown AtomicBool, a Control::Stop, or a disconnected control channel. On an idle iteration (no prices, no control) it parks for 50 µs to avoid pinning a shared CPU.

BookState is the replicated state machine: a HashMap<u64, f64> (instrument key → price/value) that accepts BookUpdate commands via apply. BookUpdate has three variants: Set {key, value} (last-writer-wins exact store), Add {key, delta} (IEEE-754 add in log order, 0.0 if absent — deterministic because all nodes replay the same ordered log), and Remove {key} (no-op if absent). The state is serialized to/from a compact binary wire format via encode/decode, and to_bits maps each f64 value through f64::to_bits for bitwise-exact comparison across nodes.

gpu_grid_honors_ragged_path_count verifies that ScenarioPricer correctly handles path counts that are not aligned to WG_SIZE (i.e., ragged tails). With paths=300_007 (deliberately non-divisible by WG_SIZE), it computes a 2×2-ladder scenario grid on both GPU and CPU and asserts: (a) every grid node records exactly paths=300_007 paths, and (b) each node price satisfies |gpu - cpu| <= node_bound(spot, vol, t, drift, strike, discount) — the per-node statistical bound derived from the exact bumped parameters.

interior_corruption_distinct_from_torn_tail is the discrimination proof (§2.6(3)): two forged logs share a good prefix (records 0,1). (a) prefix + record 2 with intact sync + BAD CRC (payload byte flipped after framing) + a valid record 3 after it → Err(CorruptInterior { at_sequence: 2 }). (b) prefix + record 2 with intact sync+header but body TRUNCATED at EOF → Ok, healed to the prefix length (2 records, file truncated to prefix.len() bytes). These two inputs were indistinguishable under the marker-less format and now yield strictly different verdicts.

RiskEdge::drill_risk() enforces the full request-scoped guard chain: readiness gate enter, require_ready, resolve caller from session token or principal, authorize caller with `ReadAny` authority. Only then does it branch on serve mode: Direct runs the local store, Federate routes to federated_drill_risk. The guard chain is identical to aggregate_risk — no gated RPC skips any step.

margining_dispatch_is_bitwise_faithful asserts that price_with_margining and greeks_with_margining are perfect zero-overhead dispatchers: calling them with Margining::EquityStyle produces bitwise-identical results to calling price/greeks directly, and calling them with Margining::FuturesStyle produces bitwise-identical results to futures_style_price/futures_style_greeks directly. Verified across three distinct market inputs and both Call/Put option types by comparing .to_bits() on every field returned by strip_fields.

PILLAR (CLAUDE.md guardrails 6 + 11 — scale & performance are requirements: the pricing hot core must stream prices to high-performance counterparties at the latency budgets in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2). `CoreBudget::architecture_1_2` is the single, authoritative encoding of the per-price hot-core tail-latency budget: a parameterless `const fn` returning `Self { p50_ns: 2_000, p99_ns: 10_000, p999_ns: 25_000 }` — i.e. the 2µs/10µs/25µs p50/p99/p99.9 envelope from ARCHITECTURE §1.2. Being a `const fn` over literals it is pure and side-effect-free by construction (no allocation, I/O, or mutation); it has no WRITES edges. The bench load harness (CoreReport::budget_breaches) measures the live core against exactly this struct, so the latency pillar is reconciled against a single source of truth rather than asserted. SELF-INVALIDATING: editing any budget constant (or the signature) shifts this anchor and flips the claim stale, re-opening review against the doc.

hedge_weights_recover_a_pure_pillar_target asserts the correctness of hedge_smile_overlay_cost by verifying the unit-pillar recovery property: for each of the three pillar strikes, constructing a target exposure equal to vanilla_smile_exposures at exactly that pillar must yield hedge weights [0,…,1,…,0] (1.0 at the matching pillar, 0.0 at the others) to within 1e-9 absolute tolerance. This pins the linear-system inversion in the overlay solver against a known analytic ground truth.

Producer::publish uses a true two-stamp seqlock writer protocol: (1) store `writing = (seq << 1) | 1` with Release to raise the in-progress flag, (2) write the payload into the slot's UnsafeCell via PayloadCell::write, (3) store `stable = seq << 1` with Release to close the write window, (4) advance the global `head` (AtomicU64, cache-padded) with Release as the last step. The two Release stamp stores straddle the payload write so any concurrent consumer copy that overlaps the write observes either the odd in-progress stamp or a before/after stamp mismatch, and retries. Single-producer ownership makes the UnsafeCell write safe with no locks.

Acceptor::handle_frame is the single inbound dispatch point for the FIX acceptor. It feeds the raw frame to the session state machine (on_inbound) and forwards any generated outbound frames. If the session signals a deliverable message it parses the frame with FrameCursor and routes by MsgType: QuoteRequest→on_quote_request, NewOrderSingle/NewOrderMultileg→on_new_order. A session protocol fault returns an empty outbound list rather than panicking, leaving disconnection to the caller.

PricingCore::price(&mut self, req: PriceRequest) -> PriceResponse computes a single vanilla option price in four deterministic steps: (1) load the current MarketState via arc-swap (lock-free reader); (2) call smile.implied_vol(req.strike, forward, st.t) to look up the smile-surface Black vol for the request strike; (3) form VanillaInputs{spot, strike, vol, t, r_dom, r_for} and call celnet_vanilla::greeks(option_type, &inputs); (4) write the resulting PriceSnapshot into the top-of-book seqlock and increment the priced counter. The test price_matches_direct_vanilla_at_smile_vol confirms that resp.greeks.price == celnet_vanilla::greeks(…, &VanillaInputs{…, smile_vol, …}).price to 1e-12 relative / 1e-14 absolute tolerance.

modify_rebaselines_in_place_at_next_sequence is an inline test verifying the Modify-subscription invariant: a Modify on an open subscription (sequence N) must reply with a fresh Snapshot at sequence N+1, and the prior structure's tradable tokens must be retired (no longer live) so a stale click on a pre-modify token cannot trade the new structure.

merge_delta_vector accumulates currency-exposure legs by finding an existing leg by ccy and adding its amount, or appending a new leg if the currency is not yet present. The operation is additive and preserves first-seen order.

PathwiseGreeksPricer::path_estimators returns N_EST pathwise Greek estimators for each of spec.paths paths, dispatched to the GPU pipeline when a wgpu adapter and compiled pipeline are available, or falling back to the CPU oracle (narrowed to f32 precision per element via `f64::from(p as f32)`) to keep the output contract identical on both paths. It enforces spec.paths in 1..=MAX_PATHS before dispatch.

american_lsm implements the Longstaff-Schwartz regression-based Monte Carlo for American/Bermudan options using scrambled Sobol QMC (via SobolSequence + BrownianBridge) with degree-3 polynomial regression in normalised moneyness x=S/K (not raw S, to keep the design matrix well-conditioned — raw spot³ ≈ 10⁶ would bias the least-squares solve). Backward induction exercises path p at date k when intrinsic(s) >= estimated continuation value from ridge_regress. Carry accessors are read once before the path loops.
