Returns LsmEstimate{price, std_error} as the mean of per-path discounted cashflows.

audit_channel constructs a matched (AuditSink, AuditDrain) pair sharing an Arc<AuditShared> for atomic counters (next_sequence, accepted). AuditDrain.try_commit is non-blocking (try_recv); AuditDrain.commit_blocking blocks until the next record or sender disconnect; AuditDrain.drain_available loops try_commit to exhaustion. All three drain variants call `account` to update highest_committed, enabling lossless gap detection.

VaR/ES and curvature-spot are NON-ADDITIVE measures that require a re-gathered firm node, not a per-shard sum. `FleetReducer::firm_var_es` calls `gather_firm_node` (which fan-ins constituent positions from all shards) then passes the resulting firm node to `Cube::node_var_es`. The `summing_shard_vars_overstates_firm_var` test explicitly asserts `firm_var < naive_shard_sum` — the diversification / sub-additivity invariant — proving that callers must NEVER compute VaR by summing per-shard VaRs. The same pattern applies to `firm_curvature_spot` (via `Cube::node_curvature_spot`) and `firm_var_es_sensitivity` (via `Cube::node_var_es_sensitivity`).

The core_load binary enforces the §1.2 ABSOLUTE in-core latency budget (p50 ≤ 2 µs, p99 ≤ 10 µs, p99.9 ≤ 25 µs) by calling `report.budget_breaches()` and exiting non-zero with a per-percentile diagnostic if any ceiling is exceeded. It supports `--quick` for a lighter smoke run and an optional JSON output path for snapshot refresh.

ReplicaSet::new() enforces two structural invariants at construction time: (a) no two replicas share the same ReplicaId (returns MembershipError::DuplicateId); (b) every declared standby id references a member of the same set (returns MembershipError::UnknownStandby). These checks run once at set-build time, so all subsequent routing methods can assume a valid, self-consistent membership snapshot without re-validating.

run_rejects_non_psd_correlation verifies that a basket pricer invocation with a correlation matrix that has off-diagonal entries >1 (e.g. [[1,1.01],[1.01,1]]) is rejected with CorrelationError::NotPositiveDefinite before any pricing computation, ensuring the Cholesky decomposition pre-check is enforced at the CLI entry point.

`run_cli` spawns the `celnet` binary as a child process and enforces a hard 20-second deadline: it polls `child.try_wait()` every 25 ms and kills the child if the deadline is exceeded, then panics with a diagnostic message. This prevents test hangs when the server under test deadlocks or stalls, giving the test harness bounded resource usage.

compaction_watermark_beyond_log_is_rejected verifies the watermark over-claim guard: compacting with watermark=3 on a log that only has sequences 0..=2 (last_sequence==2) must return Err(CorruptInterior { at_sequence: 3, reason }) where reason contains 'watermark', and must leave the log untouched (still 3 plain Data records, next_sequence still 3 after both the rejected compact and a reopen).

celnet-journal is a durable append-only event-log crate providing crash-safe, sequence-ordered persistence for domain state machines. Its public seam is: Journal::open (create-or-recover a file, healing any torn tail on startup), Journal::append (write one CRC-framed, fsync'd record, returning its u64 sequence number), Journal::replay (iterate all durable records in sequence order via a callback closure), and Journal::compact (atomically replace the log with snapshot + residual). The EventCodec trait is the plug-in seam: a new consumer plugs in by implementing EventCodec::encode (deterministic bytes from event) and EventCodec::decode (event from bytes) then calling Journal::append/replay with the encoded form. The Journal struct carries no generics itself — the codec seam is exercised at the call site, not baked into the log type.

`venue_convention_identities_are_pinned` pins the three Deribit crypto-venue constants that govern how the strike-axis oracle ingests crypto expiries: `EXPIRY_CUT_UTC_SECONDS == 28_800` (08:00 UTC cut), `STYLE_EUROPEAN == "European"`, and `SETTLEMENT_IS_INVERSE_COIN == true` (inverse/coin-settled, not linear-USD). These are asserted at the string/bool level so any future upstream change to the `deribit` module constants is caught by the test rather than silently propagated to the surface calibration.

The Underlying smart constructors (Underlying::fx, ::metal, ::equity, ::commodity, ::digital_asset) each stamp the settlement_ccy field from the pair's/ref's quote (numeraire) leg at construction time — e.g. Underlying::fx clones pair.quote as settlement_ccy before wrapping the pair in underlying::Ref::Fx. This means settlement_ccy is never a separate caller concern: it is derived deterministically from the asset reference and stored once, so downstream message consumers can read settlement_ccy without re-deriving it from the pair legs.

`Subscription::execute` implements the click-to-trade protocol for streamed lines with a race-free waiter registration guarantee: the `oneshot` receiver is inserted into the shared `waiters` map under a monotonic `correlation_id` BEFORE the `Execute` frame is sent over the control channel, so the demultiplexing driver can never deliver the outcome before the receiver is in place. If the send fails (stream closed), the waiter is cleaned up immediately and `ClientError::StreamClosed` is returned.

RFQ reject–then–accept state machine: after a successful `RfqHandle::reject`, the same quote can no longer be accepted — `accept` returns `ClientError::Status` with code `FailedPrecondition`. The reject acknowledgement carries the original `quote_id` and a non-zero `epoch_nanos` timestamp. Source: `reject_returns_typed_ack_and_quote_cannot_be_accepted`.

Seqlock<T>::store(&self, value: T) is the single-writer, multi-reader publish primitive for PriceSnapshot top-of-book. Write protocol: (1) load current even seq; (2) store seq+1 with Release (marks write in-progress, odd); (3) write payload word-by-word (relaxed per-word atomics); (4) store seq+2 with Release (even, marks complete). Seqlock<T>::read(&self) -> T retries until it observes an even `before` sequence and confirms `before == after` (both Acquire loads), rejecting any torn read. In debug_assertions mode a writer_active flag traps concurrent store() calls. This is the zero-lock mechanism that lets the reader thread observe PriceSnapshot without any mutex.

commit_each proposes a sequence of BookUpdate entries to a live Raft cluster one by one, re-electing a leader on step-down, and waits for each entry to commit before advancing. Returns the final committed log index. This is the standard serialized-commit helper used by snapshot tests to build a known committed log prefix before triggering snapshot/restore operations. It is deadline-bounded via assert_within_deadline.

execute_books_then_rejects_forged_expired_consumed is a deterministic inline unit test that verifies four click-to-trade token security properties in sequence: (1) forged token → UnknownToken reject, (2) genuine token → Executed with the stamped premium, (3) same key idempotent retry → same execution_id, no double-book, (4) different key re-click on consumed token → AlreadyConsumed reject, (5) clock-advanced expired token → Expired reject. The test uses a manual clock for deterministic token expiry.

failover_to_standby_keeps_aggregate_invariant proves two guarantees of the fleet's failover contract: (a) when a replica is declared DOWN with a declared hot standby, every partition key whose natural owner is the downed replica routes to the standby with RouteReason::Standby, while all surviving owners continue to route with RouteReason::Primary — no cell is lost or misrouted; (b) the firm aggregate over the full measure set is unchanged by the topology change, because aggregation reads each shard's natural-owner slice independently of health status (failover is a routing concern, not an aggregation concern).

barrier_bounded_by_vanilla verifies the fundamental no-arbitrage bound: for all combinations of up/down barrier, call/put option type, and knock-in/knock-out style, the barrier price lies in [0, vanilla_price]. The test covers an up-barrier (H=125, K=100) and a down-barrier (H=80, K=100) and asserts `−1e-10 ≤ barrier_price ≤ vanilla + 1e-9`.

double_barrier_table_loads_and_is_well_formed enforces structural invariants on the frozen double-barrier oracle: every numeric field (spot, strike, lower, upper, vol, t, price) must be finite; the corridor must satisfy 0 < lower < upper; every price must be non-negative (≥ −1e-9); and both KnockOut and KnockIn kinds must appear in the loaded records.

`prefix_is_really_discarded_on_disk` verifies that `Log::discard_prefix(boundary, term)` physically removes compacted records: the on-disk entry count shrinks from `total` to `total − (boundary+1)`; `term_at(i)` returns `None` for i < boundary; `matches_prev(boundary, term)` holds (so AppendEntries can immediately replicate boundary+1); and `entries_from(boundary+1)` returns correctly-indexed entries with `first.index == boundary+1` and `last.index == total−1`.

celnet-entitlements is the deny-by-default risk-entitlement crate for the celnet platform. Its public contract is: (1) construct a `Principal` via `Principal::grant_all()` (all-access, deny-overridable) or `Principal::scoped().grant(Rule::on(dim, val))` (explicit allow-list, deny by default when no grants match); (2) bind it with a `Hierarchy` into an `EntitlementFilter`; (3) call `EntitlementFilter::prune(&facts) -> Vec<RiskFact>` to filter a fact slice, or `EntitlementFilter::entitled_cube(facts) -> Cube` to build an entitlement-gated risk aggregation cube. A new entitlement arm plugs in by supplying a `Principal` built from `Rule` scopes and wiring it into `EntitlementFilter::new`; no other extension points are required.

RiskEdge::aggregate_risk_impl prunes by entitlement BEFORE roll-up: entitled_cube filters the position store snapshot to only positions the caller's principal may see, then a scope sub-tree filter (resolved_group_value == value) narrows further, and only the resulting cube is aggregated. This guarantees a caller never sees positions outside their entitlement boundary in any aggregate node.

single_barrier_prices_match_quantlib_all_flavours asserts that the celnet single-barrier pricer matches the frozen QuantLib oracle to REL=1e-9 and ABS=1e-11 across all 288 grid rows. It enforces flavour completeness: all four BarrierType variants (DownOut, DownIn, UpOut, UpIn) must be present for both Call and Put, preventing a silently-truncated oracle from hiding missing knock-direction coverage.

stream_blotter::run enforces strict sequence monotonicity across all three multiplexed vanilla-call subscriptions: the first event received on each subscription must be a `StreamEvent::Snapshot` (otherwise the function returns an error), and every subsequent `StreamEvent::Tick` must carry a sequence number strictly greater than the previously observed one (`line.sequence <= last_seq` triggers an immediate error). The function errors if zero live ticks are produced in total, guaranteeing that the SDK's streaming path has actually delivered live market data before returning `Ok`. Subscriptions are opened over a single multiplexed session (`client.open_session()`) with caller-supplied subscription-id hints (1000, 1001, 1002), confirming the session multiplexing contract.

divergence_report() flags a feed source as divergent only when (a) there are at least MIN_SOURCES_FOR_GATING sources (gating_undecidable=false), (b) the source's L∞ deviation over the smile pillar vols exceeds the absolute tolerance_vol_points threshold, AND (c) it exceeds the data-adaptive MAD-scaled bound MAD_K × MAD_TO_SIGMA × mad / VOL_POINT. The dual gate (absolute floor + panel-relative MAD) ensures a source is never flagged merely because the whole panel is genuinely dispersed. The consensus is the per-quantity median over all sources; a single or dual feed never triggers exclusion (gating_undecidable path).

AuditSink.record assigns a globally-monotone sequence number to every AuditRecord via SeqCst fetch_add on shared.next_sequence before sending it over the unbounded channel; on channel closure it returns AuditClosed (wrapping the unsent record). The SeqCst ordering guarantees that every concurrent caller sees a strictly increasing, gap-free sequence, enabling the drain to detect losses.

For every dimension (`Trader`, `Book`, `Desk`, `Underlying`, `Location`, `Entity`), `Cube::group_by` produces a partition where: (a) group keys are pairwise distinct, (b) summing all eleven `NetGreeks` fields over groups matches `firm_aggregate` to 1e-9, (c) vega ladder totals are conserved, and (d) position/exotic/leaf counts sum to the firm totals. Each dimension must produce ≥ 2 groups on the `mixed_book` fixture.

The JournalError Display implementation formats the three error variants with human-readable, diagnostically distinct messages: Io wraps the underlying IO error as 'journal io error: {e}'; CorruptInterior names the corrupted sequence number and a human reason string as 'journal interior corruption at sequence {at_sequence}: {reason}'; PayloadTooLarge states the rejected length and the hard compile-time ceiling MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN as 'journal payload too large: {len} bytes (max {MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN})'.

serve_conn services one peer TCP connection in a read-reply loop: it reads one framed message per iteration (blocking with idle-timeout via read_frame_or_idle), dispatches to handle_rpc under the NodeCore mutex, and writes the reply frame. It exits on any IO error, a corrupt frame, or the stop flag — never panics. The core mutex is held only for the synchronous handle_rpc call, not across IO.

run_matches_the_leaf_bitwise_under_both_margining_styles verifies that the future-option CLI run() function is bitwise-identical to the underlying celnet leaf pricing for both equity-style (present-value of intrinsic) and futures-style (no discounting of daily margin) margining. It also asserts that futures-style discount_rho is exactly 0.0 in IEEE 754 bits — a financial invariant, not a rounding artifact.

Wing-delta observable: `Observable::RiskReversal { delta: 0.25 }` (and similar wing observables carrying a delta parameter) is round-tripped through `subscribe_series` and back — the subscription's `observable()` accessor returns the exact variant including its `delta` field. The seeded snapshot carries a finite real RR vol. Source: `wing_observable_series_carries_its_delta`.

StandardFrtbParams encodes all FRTB MAR21 FX risk-weight and correlation constants with hand-typed paragraph citations and bitwise-exact assertions guarding against floating-point drift. Key values: fx_delta_rw = 0.15 (MAR21.88); fx_delta_rw_liquid = 0.15/sqrt(2) (MAR21.88 relief); fx_vega_rw = min(0.55*sqrt(40/10),1) = 1.0 (MAR21.93/.94); vega_corr_alpha = 0.01 (MAR21.94, decay kernel exp(-0.01*|T_i-T_j|/min(T_i,T_j))); fx_curvature_rw = 0.15 (MAR21.98). The Low correlation scenario scales rho as max(2rho-1, 0.75*rho) per MAR21.6(2). Any future edit to these constants must re-verify against the cited paragraphs.

crash_recovery_rebuilds_byte_identical_book_and_reprices_bit_identically verifies the two-phase crash-recovery contract: (a) after replaying a fsync'd journal from a clean drop with no shutdown, the recovered BookState is bit-for-bit identical to the pre-crash state for every field (id, option_type, strike bits, notional bits, whole-struct PartialEq); (b) the recovered market state is the LAST accepted mark (not an earlier one), confirming last-mark-wins semantics; and (c) repricing every recovered book entry on a fresh PricingCore produces the exact same u64 bit-patterns for all Greeks as the pre-crash pricing run. This test enforces deterministic, bit-exact reproducibility across simulated crashes.

ScriptedReader::read serves a deterministic scripted sequence of IO outcomes for unit testing: each call pops the front step and either copies min(data.len(), buf.len()) bytes and returns Ok(n), returns an Err constructed from the supplied ErrorKind, or returns Ok(0) when the queue is exhausted (signalling EOF). No buffering: every call consumes exactly one script step.

`row5_zero_vol_simulation_matches_independent_deterministic_profile` verifies the full XVA pipeline at σ=0: at zero diffusion the simulated spot path collapses to the deterministic S(t)=S₀·exp((r_d−r_f)·t), so the simulated EPE/ENE must match a hand-built profile to within 1×10^{-12}, and the CVA computed from both profiles must also agree to 10^{-12}. This closes the simulate→aggregate→CVA loop against a closed-form ground truth.

conflation_correctness_under_overflow verifies the full conflation contract under adversarial conditions (2,000,000 items into a 64-slot ring with an artificially slowed consumer): (1) the consumer converges on the latest item (assert_eq!(*got.last(), PRODUCED-1)), (2) received + skipped == PRODUCED exactly, (3) cursor reaches PRODUCED, (4) delivery is strictly in-order and duplicate-free (windows(2) check), and (5) skipped > capacity proving that real conflation engaged (not a trivial pass). The consumer is primed to start in the lapped regime by waiting until the producer has published cap*4 items, making the skipped > cap assertion scheduling-independent.

WasmModel::price marshals CarryInputs to a flat little-endian byte buffer via input_to_bytes, calls the guest export 'price' with (opt_to_abi(opt), in_ptr, in_len), and canonicalizes the returned f64 at the host boundary — any NaN is normalized to CANONICAL_NAN_BITS. WasmModel::price_and_greeks additionally calls the guest export 'scratch_out' to obtain the output pointer, calls 'price_greeks', reads GREEKS_BYTES back via read_guest, and deserializes them with abi::greeks_from_bytes. Both paths call WasmModel::refuel before each call to reset fuel to the full FuelBudget.

every_reachable_target_solves_without_failure asserts that strike_from_delta returns Ok(…) for every target produced by reachable_targets across the full wide_regimes grid × all conventions × both option types. This is the non-error guarantee: no target within the reachability boundary must ever produce a DeltaSolveError.

`hrw_fallback_picks_argmax_among_healthy` verifies the HRW fallback contract: when a key's natural owner (highest-weight replica) is marked `Health::Down` and has no standby, `PartitionMap::route` must return the `oracle_argmax` among the remaining healthy replica ids with `RouteReason::HrwFallback` and `natural_owner` pointing to the downed replica. For keys whose natural owner is healthy the result must be `RouteReason::Primary` with the argmax id. The test sweeps all 7 replicas as the downed one and 600 key seeds per sweep to guarantee at least one key exercises the fallback path.

RFS attributed subscribe: `StreamSession::subscribe_attributed` echoes the caller's correlation id (type `Option<u64>`) in the opening `StreamEvent::Snapshot.correlation_id` field, and populates `attribution` with the resolved maker chain. The snapshot attribution owner is always a named `Seat` (non-empty `AutoPricer` or `Trader` id). Source: `rfs_subscription_echoes_attribution_on_snapshot`.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-observability provides three disjoint, zero-alloc-hot-path observability pillars: (1) a bounded SPSC telemetry ring (HotProbe/TelemetryDrain) for sub-microsecond HotSample capture from the pricing hot core, (2) an unbounded audit channel (AuditSink/AuditDrain) with monotone sequence numbers for lossless compliance-grade audit trails, and (3) HdrHistogram-backed latency recorders (LatencyRecorder/LatencyByKind) with coordinated-omission correction. All three offload to the drain/consumer side; the hot producer path is lock-free and allocation-free, satisfying CLAUDE.md guardrail 11.

greek_oracle_agrees_on_known_good_markets is the testkit's Greek self-consistency gate: it iterates every market in reference_markets(), every option type (Call, Put), and all 9 GreekKind variants (DeltaSpot, Vega, RhoDom, RhoFor, Theta, Gamma, Vanna, Volga, Charm), calling assert_greek_matches_fd with tighter tolerances for first-order Greeks (rel=1e-4, abs=1e-6) and relaxed tolerances for second-order Greeks (rel=1e-2, abs=1e-5) to account for the double-bump amplification. Any pricer that breaks analytic-FD agreement on these reference markets will fail this gate.

touch_prices_match_quantlib_all_kinds asserts that the celnet touch pricer matches the frozen QuantLib oracle to REL=1e-6 and ABS=1e-8 across all 1,224 grid rows. It enforces that all four touch kinds (OneTouch, NoTouch, Dnt, DoubleTouch) are present in the oracle, guarding against truncation silently removing an entire payoff family.

install_snapshot_stale_index_guard_is_high_water: a second InstallSnapshot for an already-applied boundary (last_applied >= last_included_index) is a no-op — the handler replies success=true but leaves snapshot_index() unchanged. The stale guard `last_applied >= lii` must be strict-GTE: a `> with ==` mutant would wrongly re-install at the exact boundary, and a `> with <` mutant would wrongly reject. Idempotent re-delivery is therefore safe.

solve (PDE) drives the Rannacher-start Crank-Nicolson backward solver for a vanilla or single-barrier PDE problem on a log-spot grid. The grid is aligned to the exact log-barrier level when `problem.knock_out = Some(level, up)` (via `aligned_to_barrier`), or centred on the expected log-spot when no barrier is present. The first `grid.rannacher_steps` are taken with θ=1 (backward Euler, L-stable, damps payoff-kink oscillations) and the remaining with θ=0.5 (Crank-Nicolson, second-order). Far-field Dirichlet edges are refreshed to the analytic discounted-forward asymptotic at each τ level before the tridiagonal solve.

survival_curve_identities asserts three mathematical properties of SurvivalCurve that must hold for any hazard parametrisation: (1) Flat curve — cumulative_hazard(t) is bit-exactly λ·t and survival(t) is bit-exactly libm::exp(−λt), guaranteeing zero numerical drift from the single-multiply closed form; (2) Piecewise curve — cumulative_hazard(t) matches an independent piecewise-linear reference (cum_hazard_ref) to 1e-14 rel / 1e-18 abs, and survival(t) is bit-exactly exp(−cumulative_hazard(t)) at every test point including boundaries and beyond the last pillar; (3) marginal_default(a, b) equals exactly survival(a) − survival(b); (4) survival is monotone non-increasing over a 64-point pseudo-random LCG grid on [0, 40].

run_no_loss verifies the no-conflation broadcast contract for N consumers receiving M items each from a paced producer. The producer paces to the slowest consumer by waiting until every consumer's progress counter satisfies count >= (seq+1).saturating_sub(capacity) before publishing the next slot, preventing any slot from being overwritten before all consumers have read it. Post-run each consumer asserts: skipped()==0 (zero conflation in paced regime), received()==n_items, and got==want (exact ordered sequence 0..n_items). This is the primary correctness gate for the SPMC fan-out: each consumer sees every published value exactly once, in order, with no loss.

pin_current_thread (all three module-local copies: core_load, gpu_load, surface_rebuild) attempts to pin the calling thread to physical core `core_index` using the `core_affinity` crate: it calls `get_core_ids()` and, if the index is in-bounds, calls `set_for_current(id)`. It returns `true` iff pinning succeeded, `false` on any failure (unsupported OS, out-of-bounds index, or permission denial). Pinning is a best-effort performance hint — it is never a correctness requirement and failures are tolerated by all callers.

merge_node_additive sums position_count and merges the additive risk sub-structure: if both nodes have additive data, merge_additive combines them; if only the other has it, it is cloned into acc. Non-additive (VaR/ES) fields are never summed here — they require a re-gather pass.

`log_matching_truncates_divergent_uncommitted_tail` verifies Raft log-matching (§5.3) and the §5.4.1 up-to-date election rule together: a node (X) seeded with a stale term-1 entry cannot win election against two nodes (Y/Z) holding a term-2 authoritative entry; the winning leader's AppendEntries truncates X's divergent tail; and after convergence X's on-disk journal is byte-identical to the leader's committed log and replays to the oracle state — the stale value (-999) never appears.

Session::handle_logon implements the role-split logon handshake. An Acceptor mirrors the logon (build_logon with reset_seq=false) and transitions state→Active. An Initiator treats the inbound logon as confirmation and transitions state→Active without emitting a frame. Both branches are the sole location where SessionState::Active is set.

LimitTree::set enforces a one-limit-per-metric-per-scope invariant via upsert: if a `LimitSpec` with the same `metric` already exists at the given scope, it is replaced in-place; otherwise it is appended. This means a second `set` call for the same (scope, metric) pair supersedes rather than accumulates, so the tree always holds at most one limit per metric per scope. The tree is an unsorted Vec of (scope, Vec<LimitSpec>) pairs; scope lookup is O(n) in the number of registered scopes.

The `admits_up_to_cap_then_sheds` test asserts three contracts simultaneously: (1) the limiter admits exactly `cap` concurrent in-flight requests for a single replica before shedding; (2) `inflight(id)` returns `Some(cap)` at saturation; (3) a third admit on the saturated replica yields `Admission::Shed { replica, cap }` with the correct values; and (4) a different replica that shares the same limiter is completely unaffected — confirming per-replica isolation of the counter.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY (celnet-exotics): The crate is the full exotic-products pricing engine for the Celnet platform, providing closed-form, PDE (ADI/PSOR FD), and Monte Carlo (QMC Sobol + antithetic) pricers for: single/double barriers (Reiner-Rubinstein closed form + rebate decomposition), digital/touch options, TARFs and accumulators (antithetic-pair Euler MC), lookback options (Conze-Viswanathan fixed + floating closed form), Asian options (Turnbull-Wakeman analytic + MC), forward-starts and cliquets, American/Bermudan options (PSOR FD + Longstaff-Schwartz MC), perpetual options, multi-asset baskets (scrambled Sobol QMC with Cholesky correlation), and the LSV (Local-Stochastic Volatility) model via particle calibration + ADI PDE. The public contract seam is ExoticInputs, which carries the generalized Carry struct (ADR-0008) so all pricers are asset-class-agnostic. The market-hedge overlay (Vanna-Volga) adds smile cost on top of any flat-vol pricer. A new product arm plugs in by accepting &ExoticInputs and calling i.carry_rate()/discount_df()/carry_df() for drift/discount — never matching on Carry directly.

civil_from_days implements the Gregorian calendar algorithm (Howard Hinnant's integer-only civil_from_days) converting a Unix day count to (year, month, day) with no external calendar dependency. The epoch offset 719,468 shifts the Unix epoch (1970-01-01) to the proleptic Gregorian era base. The era/doe/yoe/doy/mp chain is exact integer arithmetic — no floating-point, no table lookup.

at_hit_continuous_at_the_barrier verifies the continuity invariant of one_touch_price as the spot approaches the barrier from the in-the-money side. For both an up-barrier (H=105) and a down-barrier (H=95), the test confirms that as S→H with |S−H|/H = k ∈ {1e-4, 1e-6, 1e-8}, the price gap (1−V) is non-negative (value never exceeds the rebate), shrinks proportionally to k (gap ≤ 10k), and is monotonically decreasing. This enforces the requirement that the one-touch pricer has no discontinuity at the barrier.

FixSession::handle_frame() routes inbound FIX bytes through the session layer first (`session.on_inbound`), which validates protocol/session-layer correctness and appends any admin replies to the outbound buffer. Only messages that pass the session layer and carry an application `deliver` type are dispatched to application handlers: QuoteRequest → `on_quote_request`, NewOrderSingle/NewOrderMultileg → `on_new_order`. A session-layer error causes an empty application response (no panic); the session layer already emitted the admin reject.

pin_current_thread_to_core(core_index) attempts to bind the calling OS thread to the logical core identified by core_index in the host's enumerated core list. It returns true if and only if the OS accepted the affinity assignment; it returns false — never panics — when core_index is out of range (index beyond available core count) or when the OS rejects the call. The function has no side effects beyond the affinity syscall and leaves thread affinity unchanged on any failure path.

delta_d_strike_matches_finite_difference verifies that the analytic ∂Δ/∂K (delta_d_strike) matches a central finite-difference approximation with step h = 1e-6·K to tolerance (1e-5 relative, 1e-8 absolute). This is tested at three strike points (0.9F, 1.05F, 1.2F) — deliberately avoiding the premium-adjusted call turning point where finite differences become ill-conditioned — across all four conventions and both option types.

valid_crc_record_with_nonmonotonic_sequence_is_surfaced verifies that a structurally-intact record (CRC passes) whose sequence number breaks strict monotonicity is surfaced as CorruptInterior rather than silently healed. A forged log with frame(seq=0) followed by frame(seq=5) must yield Err(CorruptInterior { at_sequence: 1, reason }) where reason contains 'monotonic', because 1 is the expected next sequence and the jump to 5 is unambiguously a corruption or reorder — not a torn tail.

Session::handle_resend replays the stored message range [begin, end] in response to a ResendRequest. For each sequence number in the range: if stored, it emits any pending gap-fill SequenceReset covering administrative gaps before replaying the stored frame; if not stored, it accumulates a gap. Any trailing gap at end+1 is closed with a final SequenceReset(GapFill=true). This guarantees that all sequence numbers in [begin, end] are covered by exactly one outbound frame — either the original or a gap-fill — with no duplicates.

QuoteEdge::request_multi_dealer_quote() builds a multi-dealer panel by reusing the single-dealer `request_quote` path verbatim for the native LP (ensuring byte-identical pricing), then injecting synthetic LP sources only when the serving mode is not `Forward` (a forwarding edge keeps only its own native line). The `MultiDealerEngine` ranks all sources concurrently. The ranked dealer rows are pinned onto the stored quote record so that a subsequent `AcceptQuote` naming any `lp_id` books exactly the line shown — idempotent re-request re-pins identical rows.

EgressGovernor enforces key-based conflation and a token-bucket rate limit on downstream price delivery. offer() conflates same-key updates in O(1) — if a key is already pending, the newer-seq update replaces the older one (counted in EgressMetrics::conflated); if the ordered queue is at capacity, the newcomer is dropped (dropped_capacity). drain_to() dequeues and publishes at most floor(tokens) updates per call (one token per delivery), refilling via the configured drain_rate_per_sec; a sink error re-queues the failed update at the front to preserve age order without consuming the token.

`authorize_caller` is the session-aware entitlement gate layered on top of `authorize`. If the `ResolvedCaller` carries an authenticated session (`caller.user.is_some()`), it enforces role: `RequiredAuthority::Admin` requires `user.is_admin()`, otherwise returns `Err(Status::permission_denied)`; an authenticated non-admin satisfies `ReadAny`. If there is no session it delegates `ReadAny` to `authorize` (mode-gated) and always denies `Admin` in Enforce mode regardless of any entitlement principal. All decisions are emitted as `AccessAudit` records.

FrameReader::find_frame_end locates the end of a FIX frame in the internal buffer by scanning for the checksum sentinel b"10=" at a field boundary (position 0 or preceded by SOH), followed by exactly 3 ASCII digits and a trailing SOH (total 7 bytes). On a miss it records scan = buf.len().saturating_sub(6) to avoid re-scanning bytes already confirmed not to contain the sentinel, providing O(n) amortised scan across reads.

handle_update enforces strict monotone sequence ordering: it classifies each incoming Update as Gap (sequence jumped forward, skipping one or more), Stale (sequence is at or behind last_seq — silently dropped), or Tick (contiguous, delivered as StreamEvent::Tick). On a gap it immediately emits StreamEvent::GapDetected{last_good, observed} and sends a Resync control message; only a Tick advances sub.last_seq. Decode errors produce Err(ClientError) delivered on the subscription channel.

concurrent_coherent_pair_never_tears is the real-thread regression companion to the exhaustive loom model. It verifies, under 300,000 concurrent publishes of (seq, seq) pairs to a 2-slot ring, that: (1) no torn read ever occurs (the two halves of each delivered pair always agree: assert_eq!(a, b)), (2) delivery is strictly in-order and never duplicated, (3) c.received() == delivered count, and (4) received + skipped == ITERS and cursor == ITERS at termination. The torn-read freedom relies on the seqlock stamp mechanism rejecting mid-write slots.

celnet-router provides stateless, allocation-free partition-to-replica routing for the celnet fleet. Its public contract is: (1) PartitionKey::digest() produces a u64 fingerprint; (2) PartitionMap::route(key) returns a Route{replica, natural_owner, reason} following a three-tier priority — Primary (natural owner up), Standby (declared hot standby up), HrwFallback (best healthy replica by rendezvous weight) — or RouteError if no replica is reachable; (3) InflightLimiter::try_admit(replica) enforces a per-replica concurrency cap with lock-free CAS. A new arm plugs in by: constructing a ReplicaSet (duplicate-id and dangling-standby validated at construction), wrapping it in PartitionMap, and optionally pairing it with an InflightLimiter built from the same ReplicaSet.

compaction_on_empty_log_is_rejected verifies that compacting with any watermark on an empty (never-written) log is rejected as CorruptInterior: there is no durable sequence to checkpoint, so the watermark over-claims by definition.

essvi_reprices_its_input_quotes confirms that a deterministic nested-grid calibration on the eSSVI model (22 rounds of 60×60 refinement, no external solver) recovers the generating (ρ, ψ) parameters to ≤1e-9 total-variance error at every input pillar. The objective is the sum of squared total-variance residuals; brackets shrink to 10% of the previous range each round, achieving geometric convergence to exact recovery for noise-free quotes.

handle_heartbeat performs gap detection on heartbeat sequence numbers using the same `is_gap` predicate as handle_update. If the heartbeat sequence is ahead of last_seq it emits StreamEvent::GapDetected and sends a Resync; if the sequence is current it emits StreamEvent::Heartbeat{sequence, epoch_nanos}. A missing subscription is silently ignored. Heartbeats never advance last_seq.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY. celnet-heston is the self-contained Heston stochastic-volatility pricer: it exposes two independent, cross-validated closed-form pricing routes — `cos` (Fang–Oosterlee 2008 cosine-series) and `carr_madan` (Carr–Madan damped-integrand FFT-style) — both accepting `(OptionType, &MarketInputs, &HestonParams) -> f64`. The crate owns its own minimal `Complex` arithmetic (no external num-complex dep), a 16-point Gauss–Legendre panel integrator, and the overflow-stable `char_exponent` CF kernel. A new caller plugs in by constructing `MarketInputs::new(spot, strike, t, r_dom, r_for)` and `HestonParams::new(kappa, theta, vol_of_vol, rho, v0)` then calling either pricer; puts and calls are both returned via exact put–call parity so neither route has a separate put path. The two pricers cross-validate each other in the `carr_madan_and_cos_agree` and `put_call_parity_internal` tests shipped in the crate.

The in-suite core_load test (core_load_measures_and_passes_1_2_budget) deliberately does NOT assert the strict §1.2 absolute ceilings (p50 ≤ 2µs / p99 ≤ 10µs / p99.9 ≤ 25µs): cargo nextest saturates all cores so measured latencies reflect sibling-test contention, not the hot path. Instead it asserts a 100× gross-sanity ceiling (CoreBudget::architecture_1_2().p99_ns × 100) — a contention-robust floor that only a catastrophic regression breaches. The strict gate runs only in the dedicated core_load binary / bench_gate arm 1 / CI core-load-gate lane on a pinned thread.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-bench is the performance-proof crate for the celnet FX-options platform. It turns the latency/throughput budgets from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2 into reproducible, asserted proof across four distinct gate arms: (1) in-core absolute budget (price + full 13-Greek set, p50 ≤ 2µs / p99 ≤ 10µs / p99.9 ≤ 25µs, measured pinned/elevated via `core_load`); (1b) surface-rebuild absolute budget (per-pair all-tenors VV + SSVI recompute p99 ≤ 150µs, via `surface_rebuild`); (2) wire-path relative regression gate (round-trip RFQ latency under concurrent RFS streaming load, relative to a committed JSON baseline, via `wire`); (3) fleet §11 SLO relative regression gate (cross-shard federation overhead, publish→snapshot lag, conflation correctness, many-subscriber fan-out spread, via `fleet_slo`). All four arms are wired into the `bench_gate` binary which exits non-zero on any breach. The crate also provides shared, allocation-free input fixtures (`representative_inputs`, `representative_batch`, `sweep_inputs`) consumed identically by benches and unit tests, and an iai-callgrind instruction-count gate (`iai_instructions`) with soft-regression limits on `Ir` and `EstimatedCycles`.

validate_perpetual_terms(expiry_years) enforces that a PerpetualOption's enclosing Instrument.expiry_years is exactly 0.0, rejecting NaN via the != 0.0 test (since NaN != 0.0 is true, a NaN expiry is refused rather than silently accepted as 'no expiry'). validate_listed_future_terms(option, expiry_years) enforces the term ordering future_expiry_years >= expiry_years > 0 (both finite), and also validates the future_symbol presence and the Margining enum tag. Both guards return WireError::InvalidTerms on violation — never clamping or defaulting the offending value.

def_from_spec converts a FixConnectionSpec to a FixConnectionDef, enforcing two invariants: the id must be derivable (explicit id_override > spec.id.trim() > slugify(name), each falling through to the next if blank) and the desk field must be non-empty — a missing desk is rejected with "a FIX connection must belong to a desk". All other fields (name, kind, bind_addr, sender/target comp IDs, enabled) are copied verbatim.

assert_contracts is the fuzz-harness property oracle for FrameCursor::parse. For any input that parses Ok it asserts: (C3) msg_type() is non-empty; (C4) raw() is pointer- and length-identical to the input slice; (C5) every field tag is >0 and every field value is a sub-slice within the input buffer; (C6) get(35) equals msg_type(). For Err inputs it asserts only the absence of a panic. These six contracts are exhaustive: they cover identity, containment, and consistency of the zero-copy cursor.

price_cross_asset::run enforces byte-identical pricing across the four asset-class code paths (FX, equity, commodity, crypto) for an identical market (spot=100, strike=105, vol=0.22, t=1.0, r_dom=0.03, r_for=0.012, call): each cross-asset vanilla's `price` and `vega` must equal the FX baseline bit-for-bit (`line.greeks.price.to_bits() != fx_line.greeks.price.to_bits()` triggers an error), and must also agree with an independently computed generalized-BSM oracle (`celnet_vanilla::greeks`) to within 1e-10 absolute tolerance. This triple-identity (asset-class A == FX baseline == independent oracle) confirms that the asset-class tag is an identity transformation and does not perturb the linear payoff computation.

cost_of_carry_arm_prices_and_tags_rates asserts three invariants of the CarryInputs carry-arm dispatch: (1) price_and_greeks().price equals the standalone price() call to 1e-12 absolute tolerance; (2) a CostOfCarry arm produces RateSensitivities::Carry{..} (not Fx); (3) CostOfCarry{r, b = r − q} and FxRates{r_dom = r, r_for = q} price identically to 1e-12, confirming the two carry arms are one shared closed form.

JournalError::source returns the inner IO error for the Io variant (so error-chain tooling can traverse the cause), and None for all other variants (CorruptInterior and PayloadTooLarge carry no chained cause).

gaussian_eliminate_matches_dense_reference verifies that the surface calibration's inline solve3 and solve4 routines are numerically equivalent to an independent textbook partial-pivot Gaussian elimination on arbitrary diagonally-dominant systems. Over 32 LCG-seeded random trials each component of the solution must agree within 1e-10 absolute error. Additionally, rank-deficient inputs (a rank-1 3×3 and a rank-deficient 4×4) must return None — never a NaN or garbage solution. This test is the sole correctness gate for the sparse linear solver that underpins all multi-node surface calibration.

ladder_steps_reshuffle_minimally enforces that the fleet's consistent-hashing partition scheme (PartitionMap) achieves minimal reshuffle on both scale-up and scale-down: on a single-replica ADD from N to N+1 replicas, moved keys land only on the newly added replica and the moved fraction stays below 1/N_after + 0.15; on a single-replica REMOVE from N to N−1 replicas, only keys whose natural owner was the dropped node move and the moved fraction stays below 1/N_before + 0.15. Keys owned by incumbents that retain their owner are never disturbed.

exposure_simulation_matches_frozen_bits asserts that ExposureProfile::simulate produces bit-reproducible EPE/ENE profiles: for two canonical netting sets (MIXED and NET_SHORT) the EPE and ENE values at nodes 0, steps/2, and steps are bit-identical to pre-computed frozen constants (MIXED_EPE_BITS, MIXED_ENE_BITS, NET_SHORT_EPE_BITS, NET_SHORT_ENE_BITS). Additionally the time grid is constrained to t_k = k·Δt using the same float-operation order (Δt = horizon / steps), and the discount factor at each node equals exp(−r_dom · t_k) to within 1e-14. These frozen-bit assertions make the simulation deterministic and flag any change in path generation, discounting, or profile accumulation.

build_quote_request encodes a complete FIX QuoteRequest (MsgType R) frame from a QuoteRequestParams struct. It unconditionally sets tag 460 (Product) to b"4" (CURRENCY) and maps Settlement→SecurityType (FXVO/FXNO), OptionType→tag-201 (0=Put/1=Call), ExerciseStyle→tag-1194 (0=European/1=American), and expiry_years to a custom tag TAG_EXPIRY_YEARS. The encoder is cleared before use so no field from a prior call leaks into the output.

ExtendedSurface::slice_at extrapolates and interpolates the eSSVI pillar surface to an arbitrary θ (ATM total variance). Before the first pillar it returns the first pillar's (ρ, ψ) at the requested θ (flat extrapolation). After the last pillar it does the same. In the interior it linearly interpolates ρ and ψ between the bracketing pillars in θ-space. The returned ExtendedSlice is constructed via ExtendedSlice::new (not projected), so the caller must ensure pillars are already butterfly-free.

The `dispatch` function enforces all cross-field domain invariants before calling any pricing engine: (1) exactly one of --strike, --delta, or --atm must be supplied for Price/Stream/Rfq commands — a missing specifier returns `DispatchError::Invalid`; (2) `--settlement-style inverse-coin` is rejected unless `--asset crypto`; (3) struck exotic families (vanilla, digital, barrier, asian, quanto, tarf, pivot, fixed-strike lookback, american) require an explicit `--strike` via `strike_for(family)?`, while unstruck families carry `0.0` silently; (4) the window-barrier product rejects the `--model analytic` flag because it has no closed form.

converged_params_are_pinned_stressed pins the exact bit-pattern of calibrated parameters for all four fitted SmileModel variants on the 'stressed' FX quote fixture (steeper skew, more anchors). Serves as the determinism gate for the calibration pipeline under non-benign inputs.

solver_residual_is_at_solver_tolerance_on_wide_grid asserts that the residual |delta(conv, opt, solved_K) − target| is strictly below 5e-12 for every reachable target on the wide market-regime grid. This is the primary numerical accuracy gate for the solver: tighter than the 1e-11 tolerance checked in solver_strike_matches_independent_bisection, and exercised over the full wide_regimes parameter sweep rather than a single base case.

The Instrument oneof product field (proto field tag) encodes a 24-arm product taxonomy, all sharing the outer Instrument envelope (underlying, tenor, expiry_years, quantity, side, solve, pricing_model, settlement_style). The PricingModel selector (default=0=Default, LocalStochVol=1) travels on the same Instrument message and is silently-default-safe: assert_eq!(PricingModel::Default as i32, 0) is asserted in the round-trip tests, so an unset pricing_model is byte-identical to Default. Similarly SettlementStyle::Linear as i32 == 0, Margining::EquityStyle as i32 == 0, and ExerciseStyle::American as i32 == 0, meaning all proto3 zero-defaults have semantically meaningful names for the overwhelmingly common case.

Market series protocol: `SeriesSubscription::subscribe_series` opens with a `SeriesEvent::Snapshot` seeding at least one historical point with a finite, positive value (e.g. ATM-vol > 0, spot near the fixture value). Each subsequent `SeriesEvent::Point` carries a sequence number strictly greater than the previous. Exactly one `Snapshot` is delivered per series subscription lifetime. `unsubscribe()` tears the series down server-side cleanly. Source: `market_series_emits_real_observed_points_over_one_session`.

SurfaceReport::print_summary renders the §1.2 surface-rebuild gate verdict: for each model it prints cold calibration cost (labelled NOT §1.2-gated), per-tick recompute throughput, and the full latency distribution (min/p50/p99/p99.9/p99.99/max). It then prints a summary table comparing each model's p99 against the committed 150 µs ceiling (`self.budget.p99_ns`), computing margin as `ceil / meas` and marking "ok" or "FAIL".

The equity_cost_of_carry_model_reconciles_to_independent_oracle test asserts three layered invariants: (1) a guest using Carry::CostOfCarry{r, b=r-q} produces prices within 1e-12 relative error of the GBS oracle across five equity regimes including negative carry (q>r); (2) the host correctly reconstructs RateSensitivities::Carry (not Fx) from the guest's rate_kind=1 tag on the greeks path; (3) replay of the same snapshot N=8 times is bit-identical (outcome.runs==8). This test is the primary integration proof that the cost-of-carry ABI arm is end-to-end correct.

run_stream opens a celnet-client session, subscribes a vanilla two-way stream for the requested pair/tenor/option/strike, prints a snapshot line and up to req.ticks sequenced tick lines, then drops the subscription cleanly. Every await is bounded by CALL_DEADLINE to prevent terminal hangs. Gap/lag/heartbeat/reconnect events are all reported with their sequence numbers.

pathwise_lr_greeks (WGSL compute shader, greeks.wgsl @workgroup_size(256)) computes five per-path estimators in a single GBM terminal-value draw: (0) call payoff max(S_T−K,0); (1) pathwise delta = 1_{S_T>K}·S_T/S_0 (d(payoff)/d(spot) via chain rule); (2) pathwise vega = 1_{S_T>K}·S_T·(√T·z − σT) (d(payoff)/d(σ)); (3) digital payoff 1_{S_T>K}; (4) likelihood-ratio delta of digital = 1_{S_T>K}·z/(S_0·σ√T). The Sobol draw is `z = inv_norm_cdf(u32_to_open_unit(sobol_coord(sobol_base+p)))`. PathwiseGreeksPricer::estimate averages each column (discount-adjusted) via pairwise_sum, returning a GreeksEstimate. The test `pathwise_greeks_match_analytic` validates delta and vega against the closed-form GBM sensitivities.

intact_syncword_failing_crc_interior_is_corrupt verifies §2.6(1): with N=6 records of fixed-width payloads, flipping byte at offset `2*record_len + SYNC_LEN + HEADER_LEN + 1` (inside record 2's payload) yields Err(CorruptInterior) with reason containing 'interior'. This is the canonical test that the sync-word format enables interior vs torn-tail discrimination.

CAPABILITY SUMMARY — celnet-plugin-api is the user-extensibility SDK for the celnet platform. It exposes three object-safe trait seams — PricingModel, SmileModel (: Smile), and Calibration — plus a ModelRegistry trait and a WIT world (`celnet-plugin`) that structurally mirrors them. A new model plugs in by: (1) implementing PricingModel::descriptor + price (and optionally price_and_greeks) for pricing; (2) implementing SmileModel::descriptor + Smile::implied_vol for surface models; (3) implementing Calibration::descriptor + calibrate for surface fitters. The registry routes by ModelId + ModelKind via ModelRegistry::provides/descriptor/of_kind. First-party native models and wasmi-sandboxed Wasm plugins are interchangeable behind the same registry — PricingModel::price takes &CarryInputs (carry-tagged, generalized: Carry::FxRates for FX, Carry::CostOfCarry for equity/commodity) and returns PluginResult<f64>. The contract is side-effect-free and allocation-free on the hot path; determinism (same inputs → bit-identical output via celnet_core::math) is a contract obligation enforced by the replay harness.

gen_single_barrier selects up to 8 barrier golden vectors covering all four knock variants (DownOut, DownIn, UpOut, UpIn) × call/put, taking at most 2 rows per (barrier_type, option_type) key and skipping any rebated rows (rebate != 0). The kind/side mapping is KNOCK_OUT↔LOWER, KNOCK_IN↔LOWER, KNOCK_OUT↔UPPER, KNOCK_IN↔UPPER. Tolerance is rel=1e-6/abs=1e-8, oracle 'quantlib-1.42.1 barrier_gk.csv row {idx}'.

NonAdditiveExposure::from_scenarios computes portfolio-level VaR and Expected Shortfall by delegating to `celnet_risk_cube::Cube::node_var_es(pricer, node, scenarios, alpha)`. This is the only path that populates the `var` and `es` fields; the `stop_loss` field is always `None` from this constructor and must be set separately via `with_stop_loss`. VaR/ES are non-additive: they cannot be summed across positions, so they must always be computed at the aggregate `NodeAggregate` level, never by summing position-level contributions.

The conformance `instrument_of` builder is the canonical mapping from every product-family string in the golden-vector corpus to an `InstrumentSpec`. It covers all 24 product arms: vanilla, strategy (risk-reversal/strangle/straddle/seagull), single/double barrier, digital, touch (one/no/double), variance-swap, volatility-swap, asian-option (TW/Curran), forward-start, cliquet, quanto, tarf, pivot, accumulator, lookback (continuous/discrete, fixed/floating), window-barrier, american (FD and LSM-bermudan), basket, fx-forward, fx-swap, ndf, perpetual-option, listed-future-option. Source: `instrument_of` in `conformance.rs` (360 lines, complexity 81).

CAPABILITY (crate summary): celnet-risk-normalize is the cross-asset risk normalisation layer between the raw carry-seam pricers and portfolio-level risk consumers. Its public seam is three-stage: (1) `canonicalize(pos)` / `canonicalize_with(pricer, engine, pos)` — projects any asset-class `PositionRisk` through the `CarryPricer` trait to a `CanonicalLeaf` (notional-scaled Greeks, spot-unadjusted premium-excluded delta, premium currency, price); (2) the `dispatch` / `AssetPricer` subsystem — fan-out over the `LEAVES` static array of `CarryPricer` impls (FxLeaf, EquityLeaf, CommodityLeaf, CryptoLeaf) with error-priority escalation; (3) `Numeraire::from_leaves` — converts a slice of `CanonicalLeaf`s into a single-numeraire risk summary (delta_vector, delta_numeraire, premium_numeraire, vega_numeraire) via a caller-supplied `SpotResolver`. New asset-class arms plug in by implementing `CarryPricer` and adding a leaf to `LEAVES`; the `PositionRisk.carry` / `PositionRisk.fx` constructors are the two entry points into the position type.

NodeCore::install_snapshot applies a leader-sent snapshot in safe durable order: (1) write the snapshot to disk first; (2) reshape the durable log to the boundary (Log::install_snapshot retains a matching tail or discards the whole log); (3) only if the log actually advanced, reseed applied BookState and watermarks (last_applied, commit_index) from the snapshot. A stale install (log already at or past the boundary, or last_applied already past the boundary) is a no-op returning Ok(None). After reseeding, any retained committed tail above the boundary is immediately applied via apply_committed — making the post-install applied state identical to a fresh boot from the same snapshot.

MarketContext::fx(spot, vol, r_dom, r_for) is the ergonomic FX constructor: it sets discount_rate=r_dom and carry=CarryModel::fx(r_for) (which wraps r_for in FxRates inside the carry oneof). The accessors r_dom() and r_for() return exactly the stored bits — r_dom() returns self.discount_rate, r_for() returns carry.as_ref().and_then(CarryModel::fx_r_for).unwrap_or(0.0) — preserving bit-identical round-trips relative to the former flat-scalar form. with_spot, with_vol, with_r_dom, and with_r_for each produce a new MarketContext with exactly one field replaced, no arithmetic, making them pure bump-constructors for finite-difference Greeks.

replicate_round is the leader replication heartbeat: it snapshots per-peer send plans under the lock (choosing InstallSnapshot for peers behind the log base, AppendEntries with entries or as a heartbeat otherwise), issues all peer RPCs concurrently via scoped threads each bounded by rpc_timeout = min(heartbeat*3, io_timeout, 20ms), then folds all replies under one lock acquisition. On AppendReply success it advances the peer's match_index/next_index; on failure it backs next_index toward the follower's reported high-water. After folding it calls leader_advance_commit to advance commit from the new majority. The round aborts silently if the node stepped down during RPC flight.

Session::handle_resync resolves gaps using a two-branch strategy: if the retained replay buffer covers the gap (front_seq <= last_sequence+1), it replays the missing suffix in-order with blocking sends; otherwise it emits a fresh snapshot priced on sub.last_market (the most recent on-path tick) at sequence+1. After either branch lagged is cleared to false and sub.delivered is updated.

fitted_smile_reprices_anchors asserts two contracts: (1) for the benign fixture, every model reprices all off-ATM anchors exactly to within 1e-7 in vol (exact fit, since each model has at least as many shape parameters as anchors); (2) for the stressed five-point fixture, the maximum anchor repricing error for each model does not exceed the frozen reference error STRESSED_MAX_ANCHOR_ERR plus 1e-12. This is the primary numerical accuracy gate for the surface calibration pipeline.

rebuild_produces_a_real_all_tenors_surface is a correctness self-test that verifies the surface rebuild pipeline produces real, finite, positive volatilities: it builds a EURUSD fixture with exactly 11 standard tenors, runs `cold_calibrate` for MarketHedge and ParametricSurface models, and asserts that for every (tenor, moneyness) grid point `implied_vol` returns a finite positive value. It also asserts that the `recompute_marks` accumulator is finite and positive, confirming real computational work rather than a short-circuit.

`Cube::group_by` partitions all facts into `NodeAggregate` buckets keyed by `group_value(key, dim)`. It accumulates each fact into the first matching bucket (linear scan), inserting a new `NodeAggregate::empty(g)` when no matching group exists. The result vector has exactly as many entries as distinct group values; order reflects first-occurrence insertion. Called with 14 distinct callers in the codebase.

`pivot_tra_bank_pv_mc` prices a pivot-TARF from the bank's perspective: at each fixing the intrinsic `gain_sign·(S_k − strike)` is scaled by leverage when the spot is on the unfavourable side of the pivot. When cumulative client gain reaches the target the path terminates; under `TarfRedemption::CappedGain` only the remaining target is settled, under `FullGain` the full coupon is paid. The bank PV sign convention is: client-gain legs subtract from bank_pv, client-loss legs add.

entitled_facts_for_scope filters positions by entitlement and optional scope in one pass, then sorts by position_id for stable deterministic ordering. The scope filter applies resolved_group_value(hierarchy, fact, dim) == value, ensuring scope matches are hierarchy-resolved rather than raw field comparisons.

run_load drives a mixed-load scenario against a live edge over a single shared HTTP/2 channel: it opens `config.stream_subscriptions` concurrent RFS sessions (each subscribing to a distinct strike so each is independently sequenced), then runs `config.rfq_concurrency` closed-loop RFQ tasks sharing an atomic issued-counter until either `config.rfq_requests` are issued or the wall-clock cap is hit. Each RFQ is timed with a 2 s per-request timeout; per-task HdrHistogram results are merged. Returns `Err` if zero RFQ round-trips complete. Stream drainers are stopped via an `AtomicBool` and joined with a 2 s timeout. The returned `WireReport` captures merged RFQ percentiles, throughput, and the count of drained streaming messages.

`MultiDealerRfq::accept` is the multi-dealer best-bid/offer click-to-trade path: it delegates to `accept_line(panel, side, String::new())`, which serialises and sends an `AcceptLine` carrying the `RankedPanel`'s winning dealer row. `RankedPanel::best_bid` and `best_offer` resolve the winning dealer by looking up `best_bid_lp_id` in the dealer map, returning `None` when no quote is present — ensuring no aliasing to a neighbour's quote.

CoreLink::start boots the pricing subsystem as three concurrent actors — a dedicated busy-poll OS thread ("celnet-pricing-core") that owns the SPSC request/response rings, a response-router OS thread that pops completed PriceResponses and forwards them into a tokio channel, and two async tasks (submitter + dispatcher) that multiplex concurrent callers via a correlation-id map. Back-pressure on a full request ring retries with a 50 µs timer sleep (never a spin) and bails if the shutdown flag is set; a dropped dispatcher drains the pending map so every outstanding price().await resolves to CoreUnavailable rather than hanging forever.

replay::replay(model, snapshot, runs) is the determinism-verification harness: it calls price and price_and_greeks on the same snapshot a minimum of 2 times (runs.max(2)), and returns ReplayError::Diverged if any subsequent result is not bit-identical to the first via bits_eq / greeks_bits_eq. assert_agree(a, b, snapshot) extends this to cross-model agreement: it calls both a and b on the same snapshot and returns ReplayError::Diverged if their outputs differ bit-for-bit — used to verify that a native and Wasm twin produce identical results.

instruction_gate constructs a per-benchmark LibraryBenchmarkConfig that combines the shared soft-regression limits (SOFT_INSTRUCTION_REGRESSION_PCT on Ir, SOFT_ESTIMATED_CYCLES_REGRESSION_PCT on EstimatedCycles, both sourced from soft_regression_limits()) with a per-benchmark hard absolute ceiling on Ir. This dual-layer design means every iai-callgrind benchmark gets a CI-fail-on-regression soft guard AND a hard absolute Ir ceiling below which the operation must stay regardless of history.

`Underlying::as_digital_asset` is the exhaustive, total projection of the underlying oneof onto its digital-asset arm: it returns `Some(&CryptoPair)` only for the `DigitalAsset` variant and `None` for every other asset class (Fx, Metal, Equity, Commodity) and for an absent ref. The match arms enumerate all variants explicitly (no wildcard), so adding a new asset class to the one contract is a compile error here rather than a silent mis-projection. Pure: it borrows `&self` and returns a borrow, mutating nothing.

`linear::fx_equiv_rates(i) -> (r_dom, r_for)` recovers the GK-equivalent domestic/foreign rate pair from the unified Carry: `r_dom = carry.discount_rate()` and `r_for = r_dom - carry.carry_rate()` (= r - b = funding rate). This is the seam that maps the crypto funding-rate carry convention onto the same two-rate spot-discounting formula as the FX GK leaf, making `linear::price` bit-identical to `celnet-vanilla::price` under matching rates (as the comment in `aux` documents). Pure: reads `&LinearInputs`, returns `(f64, f64)`, no WRITES.

gk_price_as_oracle(b: &BatchInstrument) -> f64 is the CPU closed-form GBM (Garman-Kohlhagen) pricer used as the validation oracle for the GPU batch path: d1 = (ln(spot/strike) + (r_dom − r_for + 0.5σ²)T) / (σ√T), d2 = d1 − σ√T, price = spot*exp(−r_for*T)*N(sign*d1) − strike*exp(−r_dom*T)*N(sign*d2) for call (sign=+1) or put (sign=−1), clamped to zero. All transcendentals route through celnet_core::math (libm-backed, deterministic). cpu_batch_with_as_erf maps this oracle over a &[BatchInstrument] slice. The test `batch_reconciles_three_way` asserts GPU batch, CPU path Monte Carlo, and this oracle agree within `as_erf_price_bound`.

`fx_swap_pv` prices an FX swap as the algebraic sum of two offsetting forward legs: a near leg with side `near_side` at `near_t` and a far leg with side `−near_side` at `far_t`, both evaluated by `fx_forward_pv`. This makes the swap PV the difference of two discounted FX-forward residuals, consistent with the convention that the near and far legs carry opposite sign on the domestic-currency notional.

OisSchedule::new validates: (1) periods non-empty, (2) all accrual year-fractions strictly positive, (3) pay times strictly increasing with schedule.start strictly before the first pay time. Any violation returns a typed ScheduleError (Empty / NonPositiveAccrual / StartNotBeforeFirstPay / NonIncreasingPayTimes).

Returns true if `d` is a TARGET2 system holiday: 1 Jan, Good Friday, Easter Monday, 1 May (Labour Day), 25 Dec, or 26 Dec. No weekend-shift substitution — all dates are observed exactly on the calendar date. Pure.

Analytics-correctness (arbitrage-gate deliverable): celnet-surface::arbitrage::ArbitrageReport::is_arbitrage_free is the pure hard-reject predicate combining all three no-arbitrage axes within tolerance tol — butterfly/density (min_butterfly ≥ −tol), vertical/call-spread monotonicity (max_vertical_increase ≤ tol), and risk-neutral density positivity (min_density ≥ −tol). A slice/surface is accepted only when every axis is within tol; any single breach makes the report not arbitrage-free. Pure: deterministic in (&self, tol), reads only the report's reduced extrema, no WRITES edges.

`forward_start_price` prices a forward-start option as `e^{−r_for·reset} · spot · V_unit`, where V_unit is a unit-spot vanilla (gk_price with spot=1, strike=moneyness, maturity=expiry−reset). If expiry ≤ reset the option has already started and the payoff collapses to the intrinsic max(cp·(1−moneyness), 0). The formula is exact for a GBM model with flat vol.

PILLAR (CLAUDE.md guardrail 11 — instrument for mission-critical ops with HdrHistogram p50/p99/p99.9, without diminishing performance). `LatencyRecorder::percentile_ns(q)` is the single quantile-readout primitive that the named p50_ns/p99_ns/p999_ns accessors all delegate to: it returns `self.hist.value_at_quantile(q / 100.0)` — the HdrHistogram value at the q-th percentile, in nanoseconds (q is a percentage, converted to a [0,1] quantile). It is a pure read-only accessor: it reads the recorded latency histogram and mutates nothing, so quantile readout never touches the zero-alloc pricing hot path (recording is offloaded; this only reads the already-merged histogram). This is the tail-latency budget surface in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1.2.

Pre-trade limit-breach exposure safety (deliverable: limits-breach-detection). exposure_of is a pure, deterministic, total function over LimitMetric: it reads the aggregated net Greeks, vega ladder, gross concentration, and non-additive VaR/ES/StopLoss out of borrowed &NodeAggregate / &NonAdditiveExposure and returns the scalar exposure with no I/O and no mutation of any input. Determinism is the load-bearing safety property — pre-trade and post-trade checks (its four callers) measure the same metric against the same limit cap identically, so a breach can never be hidden by a non-reproducible reading. Pure (no WRITES edges); self-invalidates on change.

CliBarrier.style is a const fn that classifies barrier topology into knock-out/knock-in: DownAndOut and UpAndOut map to BarrierStyle::KnockOut; DownAndIn and UpAndIn map to BarrierStyle::KnockIn. This classification is used upstream to select the in-out parity formula.

Enforcement::from_tag decodes the two limit enforcement modes — Soft (warn only) and Hard (block execution) — from a wire i32 tag. An unknown tag is a protocol error. The two-arm exhaustive match ensures any new enforcement mode added to the proto is a compile-time gap in the client.

Raft persistent-state corruption safety (deliverable: replog-quorum-durability). persist::decode is a pure, deterministic deserializer: given a byte slice it validates exact RECORD_LEN, recomputes crc32 over the body and rejects any mismatch by returning None, then reconstructs (current_term, voted_for, commit_index) with no I/O and no mutation of any shared state. Purity + CRC validation is the safety invariant — a torn or bit-flipped persisted vote/term/commit record can never be silently accepted, so quorum-commit durability and single-vote-per-term election safety survive a crash mid-fsync. Pure (no WRITES edges); self-invalidates on change.

rank_side(rows, now_nanos, side) is the pure best-LP selector: it filters rows to those whose valid_until_nanos >= now_nanos (last-look gate — stale quotes are categorically excluded from winning), then picks the min under SideKey::partial_cmp_total. The SideKey for Bid negates the price (-bid) so that min-selection gives the highest bid; for Offer the price is taken straight so min gives the lowest offer. Tie-break is lexicographic: (better_price, earlier epoch_nanos, smaller lp_id) — fully deterministic with no NaN ambiguity (non-finite prices lose to any finite price via partial_cmp_total). Returns None when all rows are stale or the slice is empty.

lookback_payoff simulates one antithetic-signed lookback path and computes the path payoff. At each step it updates the running minimum and maximum using the reflected-Brownian-bridge interval extrema: `bridge_min = ½[(x_prev+x_next) − √((x_next−x_prev)² − 2·var_step·ln(u[k]))]` and `bridge_max` symmetrically (u[k] uniform variate for the bridge correction). The four payoff cases are: floating-strike call `S_T − min`, floating-strike put `max − S_T`, fixed-strike call `(max − K)⁺`, fixed-strike put `(K − min)⁺`.

LatencyRecorder.with_expected_interval constructs an HdrHistogram with 3 significant figures over the range [1 ns, MAX_NS] (60 s), enabling coordinated-omission-corrected recording. It gracefully degrades to an unconstrained 3-sig-fig histogram on the theoretically-impossible constructor failure, keeping mission-critical code panic-free.

discrete_moments computes the first and second moment of a discretely-averaged arithmetic Asian from the observation schedule. M1 = `(1/n) Σ S₀·exp(b·t_k)`. M2 = `(S₀²/n²) Σ_i Σ_j exp(b(t_i+t_j) + σ²·min(t_i,t_j))`, exploiting symmetry by iterating the upper triangle and doubling off-diagonal terms so the full n×n sum is formed with n(n+1)/2 exponential evaluations.

PositionRisk::numeraire_ccy returns the quote-leg currency of the position's underlying, dispatching by asset class: for Fx and Metal underlyings it calls as_ccy_pair().map(|p| p.quote); for Equity it returns Some(e.currency); for Commodity it returns Some(c.currency); for DigitalAsset it attempts Ccy::parse(&p.quote) and returns None when the quote leg is a non-fiat coin identifier rather than a recognized ISO 4217 currency. This last case is the only one that can legitimately return None and represents the deferred coin-numeraire case documented in crate docs.

DELIVERABLE proto/new-payoff-shapes (ListedFutureOption arm) = DONE (RC cut a0817d6; arm 31). `price_listed_future_option(o, market, expiry)` is the side-effect-free server lowering of a wire listed-future option onto the Black-76 commodity-on-future leaf: it first runs the canonical term validator (`validate_listed_future_terms` — present `future_symbol`, known margining tag, `future_expiry_years >= expiry_years > 0`), rejects a non-positive/non-finite strike as `PriceError::Domain` and an out-of-range margining tag as `PriceError::UnknownEnum` (never clamped/defaulted), maps the margining enum to `CommodityMargining`, builds `CommodityInputs::on_future(spot, strike, vol, expiry, r_dom)`, and returns the leaf Greeks via `greeks_with_margining`. Pure: it reads only `(o, market, expiry)` and returns `Result<Priced, PriceError>`, mutating no external state. The booked future_symbol is contract identity, not a pricing input. This is the second of the two genuinely-new payoff shapes the backlog tracked as OPEN; now built + golden/parity-gated across all 5 clients, with futures-style honest-zero discount-rho asserted.

cost_of computes the sum-of-squared calibration residuals for a CalibratedSmile at a set of (log-moneyness, total-variance) anchor points. For StochasticVol it uses absolute vol residuals r = black_vol(strike) − vol; for Parametric/ParametricSurface/ExtendedSurface it uses total-variance residuals r = slice.total_variance(k) − w. MarketHedge is not a fitted model and triggers unreachable!(). Used by the fit-pin tests to confirm convergence quality.
`WireAtmConvention::from(AtmConvention)` is an infallible bijection for the two ATM convention variants: `AtmForward ↔ AtmForward`, `DeltaNeutralStraddle ↔ DeltaNeutralStraddle`.

The `price` module's `run` function, exercised by `outright_matches_direct_vanilla`, produces price/vega/gamma and a convention delta that are bit-for-bit identical (tolerance 1e-14) to the `celnet_vanilla::greeks` and `celnet_vanilla::convention_delta` functions called directly on the same `VanillaInputs`. This cross-check proves the CLI's market-to-inputs pipeline introduces zero numerical drift for the outright-strike case.

PremiumStyle is the FX quotation-units axis and premium_from_domestic_pips is its canonical converter (docs/CONVENTIONS.md PremiumStyle → premium units; docs/ANALYTICS-SPEC premium quotation). Given a price already in domestic pips (v_dpips), it exhaustively maps the four PremiumStyle variants to their quoted unit: DomesticPips passes the raw PV through unchanged; PercentForeign divides by spot (per unit of foreign/base notional); PercentDomestic divides by strike (per unit of domestic/quote notional at strike); ForeignPips divides by spot·strike. The match is exhaustive over PremiumStyle, so no style is defaulted, and the DomesticPips arm is the identity (domestic_pips_is_the_raw_pv). Pure: a total function of (style, v_dpips, spot, strike) returning f64 with no writes/allocation/IO; deterministic under the f64 CPU-canonical/libm rule. Self-invalidates if the PremiumStyle variant set or any per-style scale factor changes (WRITES gate).

`shift_carry` translates absolute rate scenario bumps into the correct carry-arm fields: for `FxRates { r_dom, r_for }` it sets `r_dom += discount_abs` and `r_for += discount_abs − carry_abs`, preserving the cost-of-carry identity `b = r_dom − r_for` under independent additive shocks to the discount rate and the carry basis; for `CostOfCarry { r, b }` it shifts `r += discount_abs` and `b += carry_abs` directly.

block(counter, key0, key1) is a pure 4×32-bit counter-based bijection implementing 10 rounds of the Salmon-Moraes-Dror-Shaw (2011) Philox-style CBRNG. Each round computes two 64-bit products p0 = M0 * c[0] (M0 = 0xD2511F53) and p1 = M1 * c[2] (M1 = 0xCD9E8D57), splits to hi/lo, and mixes: c = [hi1 ^ c[1] ^ k0, lo1, hi0 ^ c[3] ^ k1, lo0]. Between rounds the key schedule bumps k0 += W0 (0x9E3779B9, golden-ratio fraction) and k1 += W1 (0xBB67AE85, √3 fraction). After exactly ROUNDS=10 iterations the function returns c with no side effects, no allocation, and no I/O. The same (counter, key0, key1) triple always produces the same four output words.

BootstrapError::fmt produces a structured, human-readable diagnostic for each failure mode of OIS curve bootstrapping: NoQuotes → static str "no calibrating OIS quotes supplied"; ForwardStartingQuote → "a quote schedule does not start at the curve origin (spot)"; NonIncreasingMaturity → "quote maturities must be strictly increasing"; Solve(e) → wraps the inner SolverError as "pillar root-solve failed: {e}"; Curve(e) → wraps the inner CurveError as "assembled curve rejected: {e}". The last two variants propagate nested error context via write! rather than f.write_str, preserving the full causal chain for diagnostics.

discounted_payoff aggregates basket legs according to the basket kind and applies the option payoff. For BasketKind::Basket the aggregate is `Σ weight_i · S_i(T)` (weighted sum). For BestOf it is `max_i(weight_i · S_i(T))`. For WorstOf it is `min_i(weight_i · S_i(T))`. The intrinsic `(agg − K)⁺` or `(K − agg)⁺` is then discounted by `df`.

The parity oracle `gk_european` implements the Garman-Kohlhagen closed form independently of `celnet_vanilla`: d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r_d - r_f + ½σ²)·T) / (σ√T), d2 = d1 − σ√T; Call = S·e^{-r_f T}·N(d1) − K·e^{-r_d T}·N(d2); Put = K·e^{-r_d T}·N(-d2) − S·e^{-r_f T}·N(-d1). Its only callers are parity tests — it never wraps production code, guaranteeing the cross-check is code-disjoint.

`convert(amount, ccy, resolver)` is the single atom for currency conversion into the reporting numeraire: it calls `resolver.rate_into_numeraire(ccy)` returning `Option<f64>`, fails with `NumeraireError::MissingRate(ccy)` if absent, then hard-validates the rate is finite and strictly positive (fails with `NumeraireError::InvalidRate(ccy)` otherwise), and returns `amount * rate`. No zero-rate silent pass-through, no NaN propagation. Pure: reads its three args, returns `Result<f64, NumeraireError>`, mutates nothing.

OptionType::flip(self) -> Self is a const pure involution: Call maps to Put and Put maps to Call. It is the put-call symmetry operator used in premium-adjustment transformations and put-from-call/parity conversions. Zero callers in production code but referenced in the premium_adjusted_flag test; its total absence of side effects and exhaustive match make it a compile-time-checkable involution.

The strategy-test oracle `gk` is a second independent Garman-Kohlhagen implementation (no `celnet_vanilla` import): Call = S·e^{-r_f T}·N(d1) − K·e^{-r_d T}·N(d2); Put = K·e^{-r_d T}·N(-d2) − S·e^{-r_f T}·N(-d1), with d1 and d2 identical to the standard formula. Its two callers are multi-leg strategy parity tests, establishing that strategy prices equal the sum of per-leg GK values.

gauss_legendre_64 computes the 64-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature nodes and weights on [−1, 1] by Newton iteration on the Legendre polynomial P₆₄ from Chebyshev-like initial guesses. The roots are symmetric about 0, so only the positive half (32 roots) are computed and mirrored. The weight formula is w_i = 2/((1−x_i²)·(P'₆₄(x_i))²). Newton iteration runs for up to 100 steps and terminates when |dx| < 1e-15 (machine precision).

The `surface` module's smile calibration pipeline guarantees arbitrage-freedom on a standard 25Δ broker slice: `SurfaceResult::arbitrage.is_arbitrage_free(1e-6)` must hold for any benign EUR/USD-style input (ATM=10.5%, RR25=-0.5%, BF25=0.2%). Additionally, the calibrated smile reprices the ATM vol at the ATM strike to within 1e-9 (`r.smile.implied_vol(r.atm_strike, r.forward, 1.0).0 ≈ atm_vol`), verifying the pipeline's internal consistency.

`OrgDimension::from(CliDimension)` is a lossless, total bijection from the CLI dimension enum to the wire `OrgDimension` type: every CLI variant maps to its identically-named wire counterpart (Firm, Trader, Book, Desk, CcyPair, Location, Entity) with no default branch, guaranteeing that adding a CLI variant without a matching wire variant is a compile error.

Convention premium-adjusted mapping (docs/CONVENTIONS.md DeltaConvention→premium-style): ConventionRecord::is_delta_premium_adjusted is a pure total function of self.delta — returns true exactly for the two premium-adjusted variants DeltaConvention::SpotPremiumAdjusted and DeltaConvention::ForwardPremiumAdjusted, false for the unadjusted Spot/Forward variants. const fn, no writes/allocation/IO; deterministic. Self-invalidates if the enum→bool mapping or DeltaConvention variant set changes (WRITES gate).

price_asian prices an arithmetic Asian option by Monte Carlo with a geometric-average control variate. It runs two passes: the first collects antithetic-pair (arithmetic, geometric) samples and accumulates online covariance via Welford to estimate the regression coefficient β = Cov(arith, geo)/Var(geo). The second pass applies the control correction Y = arith_sample − β·(geo_sample − E[geo]) where E[geo] is `geometric_asian_price / df` (the undiscounted analytic geometric mean). The final price is `df·E[Y]`.

TrivialForward::price computes the FX forward intrinsic value for a call or put without any volatility term: price = sign·(S·df_for − K·df_dom) where sign=+1 for Call and −1 for Put. This is the zero-vol limit of the GBS formula, used as a reference implementation to validate that the host correctly passes spot, strike, and both discount factors to the guest through the ABI.

greeks(opt, i) is the complete, pure generalized-BSM Greeks engine for equity vanilla options: it returns EquityGreeks containing price, delta_spot (∂V/∂S = e^{(b-r)t}·Φ(±d1)), delta_forward (∂V/∂F = Φ(±d1)), gamma (e^{(b-r)t}·φ(d1)/(S·σ√t)), vega (S·e^{(b-r)t}·√t·φ(d1)), theta (generalized-BSM carry-tagged decay), discount_rho (∂V/∂r holding b fixed), carry_rho (∂V/∂b holding r — the dividend-rho), vanna (−e^{(b-r)t}·φ(d1)·d2/σ), volga (vega·d1·d2/σ), charm (∂Δ/∂T), speed (∂γ/∂S), zomma (∂γ/∂σ), and color (∂γ/∂T). The two rate sensitivities are INDEPENDENT partials in the (r, b) basis: since d1/d2 depend on b but not r, the φ-terms cancel in carry_rho, yielding clean closed forms. No I/O, no mutation, no allocation beyond the returned struct.

`EquityLeaf::lower` enforces a typed carry-seam discipline: it accepts only `Carry::CostOfCarry { r, b }` under an equity underlying and hard-rejects `Carry::FxRates` (which would silently mis-map FX two-rate carry onto an equity pricer) with `CarryPriceError::UnsupportedCarry`. The dividend yield is reconstructed as `q = r - b` (i.e. `b = r - q` in cost-of-carry form) and passed as the equity pricer's `q` argument with `repo = 0.0`. An equity underlying carrying `Carry::FxRates` is a malformed input, not a silent approximation.
